description:

CVG-038 is the more urgent of the two, because its cite is not merely closed — it is closed with a resolution that contradicts the row. converge-fmz resolved with "Core 9 ... -> rule 9. ... Against the app: PASS, 'all 8 parts of the operation are on one page, and nothing on the board stops anything'", and named CVG-038 as answerable first-hand by running the surface kit's rule 9 against the app. The row has stayed GAP through two reconciles since. Every one of these is a red row whose named fix is finished: a reader following the cite lands on completed work and learns nothing about what would close the row.

The right fix is NOT a bulk find-and-replace of the work field. These rows went GAP pending the thing that has now landed — the harness runs, the kit rules exist — so each row's disposition may have moved toward spec, exactly the direction LEDGER-FORMAT §3 says must be re-derived from a live run rather than quietly enjoyed. The integration commit c80e6ab already did this for CVG-010 ("turnkey GREEN, drift toward spec"); these fifteen are the remainder.

For whoever takes it: run each row's probe, print what it actually says, decide the disposition the output supports, and either move the row green with no work ref or keep it red citing a LIVE item. evaluations/turnkey/run.py is the harness; uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py is the gate.

Worth considering while in there: teach verify.py to fail a GAP/VIOLATION row whose work ref is resolved in docs/work-items.json. The data to check it is already in the tree, and this is the third time the rule has had to be enforced by hand.

Not fixed here: converge-nf4's named scope was four rows (the operation.v1 clause 10 row, CVG-051, CVG-066, CVG-186), and re-pointing fifteen more without running their probes would be the blind bump the protocol forbids.

title: Three documents are held loosely and none of them says so; the decision lives only in the ratification record
description:
Contract: documents.v1 Core 6 and Core 7 (status lives in the H1, and a document carries a dated changelog), reading against PROTOCOL v3 section 5 and skills/freeze-bar/SKILL.md, which name hold loosely as a state and say where the decision belongs.

On 2026-09-04 the steward answered "loosely, ratified, go". The record, at docs/workflow/owner-ratifications-2026-09-03.md round 4, reads:

    Locking: hold loosely. composition.v1, documents.v1, and the vision meet
    the four conditions but are NOT locked; the steward chose to let the family
    mature first.

The freeze-bar skill says what that state costs to keep honest:

    - The bar is met, and that is written down.
    - The document is deliberately not locked.
    - The steward's call is recorded, with the reason, in the document itself.

    An unlocked document that nobody decided to leave unlocked is not holding
    loosely; it is a draft that stalled.

Measured on this tree 2026-09-06:

    $ grep -rn -i "hold loosely\|holding loosely\|held loosely" docs/VISION.md \
        contracts/composition.v1.md contracts/documents.v1.md
    (no match in any of the three)

So all three read as ordinary drafts. A reader opening docs/VISION.md today cannot tell a document deliberately left open from one nobody has got to, which is the exact distinction the skill exists to preserve, and the reason it says the call goes in the document.

Why it is worth an item rather than a note: the reason recorded for the hold was "let the family mature first", and the family has since moved from two passing kits to six of seven. A reason that lives outside the document it applies to is not re-read when the thing it waited on changes. This one has been true and unexamined for two days.

Scope note, so whoever takes it does not overreach: writing the hold into a document is a change to that document, and two of the three are contracts. Which is fine while they are drafts. But what the sentence says is the steward's, not a lane's - the lane writes down a decision that was made, and does not invent its wording. If the steward would rather lift the hold than record it, that is one word and this item closes without an edit.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN docs/VISION.md, contracts/composition.v1.md and contracts/documents.v1.md WHEN each is read THEN each either says in its own text that it is deliberately held unlocked and why, or is no longer held loosely because the steward lifted or acted on the hold; AND GIVEN a document in that state WHEN a reader opens it THEN they can tell it from a draft nobody decided about. FALSIFIED IF a document is recorded as held loosely somewhere else while its own text says only DRAFT.

title: Core 11: two recorded calls on this host still name none of the four, so the clause cannot be judged
description:
Contract: operation.v1 — Core 11. Ledger row CVG-021.

converge-aaw landed the first two stamped CALL lines in `hw-converge/HIGHWAY.md` (ratify; irreversible), and turnkey step (j) now classifies recorded calls into the four. Read live on this host on 2026-09-04:

    Core 11 (CVG-021) SKIP: 4 of 6 recorded call(s) name which of the four they
    are (ratify: 3, irreversible: 1); the other 2 name none, so this run cannot
    say the calls that reached the steward were the four.

The two unnamed ones are older plan-record entries written before the stamp convention existed. Until every recorded call names which of the four it is, the reading declines — and it declines honestly: a stamped call that is none of the four is a FAIL, so the step can go red, it simply has nothing to go red on yet.

CVG-021 stays GAP and cites this item. Its predecessors are both resolved: converge-5vz (wrote the stamp convention) and converge-aaw (wrote the first stamped calls).

What closes this: every call recorded in the plan record names which of the four it is — either by the manager session stamping new calls as it makes them until the unstamped two are no longer among those read, or by a decision on how to treat pre-convention entries. Then step (j)'s Core 11 reading turns PASS and CVG-021 is re-derived to CONFORMS.

Verify with: `uv run evaluations/turnkey/run.py --env local --steps j --workspace ~/dev/hw-converge --project converge`
acceptance: GIVEN turnkey step (j) reads the plan record on this host WHEN every recorded call names which of the four sanctioned calls it is THEN the Core 11 reading reports PASS rather than SKIP; AND ledger row CVG-021 is re-derived against that reading with the run's own words; AND `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` exits 0.

title: The operation kit judges the lanes at work; the lanes that reported back are unjudged
description:
Filed while closing converge-q66 on 2026-09-04.

The operation payload now carries lanes in two lists: `lanes` (at work, read in the lane words Working / Quiet / Silent — may have died) and `reported` (already come back, read in the work words Done / Stuck). That split is what lets `experience-operation.v1` Core 8 be kept without stretching a three-word vocabulary over a state it has no word for.

`conformance/experience-operation/run.py` reads only `op["lanes"]`:

- rule 8 checks the state word and the evidence of the lanes at work, and never looks at `reported`. A reported lane could carry any word at all, or no evidence, and the kit would still report PASS.
- rule 9 (Watch session) counts `lanes` without a session; a reported lane whose session is still alive is offered a Watch control that no rule checks.

Owner: whoever owns `conformance/experience-operation/`.

Suggested fix: rule 8 also asserts that every entry in `reported` reads one of the work words `experience.v1` Core 6 fixes (Done · Stuck) and carries evidence; and that no lane id appears in both lists, so the split cannot be used to hide a lane from either check.
acceptance: GIVEN an operation payload whose `reported` list carries a lane with a word outside the work vocabulary, or no evidence, or an id that also appears in `lanes` WHEN the kit runs THEN it reports FAIL naming that lane.

title: The constraint strip's fix has no test — nothing stops it being clipped again
description:
Contract: platform-web.v1 §14 — "it renders at 390 and 1280 pixels with nothing cut off and nothing overlapping" (ledger row CVG-213, which no scan can settle).

converge-6qk fixed the workspace header's constraint strip: its three chips (HARD LIMIT / STRATEGY / LANES) were being swallowed by `overflow:hidden` at every width. The fix is three CSS declarations in `app/static/css/shell.css`. Nothing in the repository would notice if a later change undid it — the whole defect lived for weeks precisely because no check looks at rendered geometry.

That lane owned only `app/static/css/shell.css`, so it could not add the test. The harness it used is complete and working, and was left uncommitted at `ai_working/w8-shell-css/measure_strip.py` in the lane worktree (lanes/w8-shell-css). It follows the shape of the existing `app/tests/test_console_overflow_rendered.py`: an in-process app server, a Playwright Chromium context per width, and a MANUAL_PROCEDURE that stands in when Playwright is unavailable.

What it measures, per width and per console state: each chip's box against the strip's padding box (that is where `overflow:hidden` clips), each chip's own text overflow, the strip against the viewport edge, whether the objective spills out of its own box, and whether the objective and the strip actually overlap on both axes. It carries a realistic long objective, because the defect only appears when the objective is long enough to win the flex fight.

Widths that matter: 390 and 768 (the strip is hidden below 980), then 1000, 1100, 1200, 1280, 1440, 1600, 1920. The 1000–1200 band is the one that catches the interesting failure — the naive one-declaration fix passes at 1280/1440/1920 and produces a 1127px-tall header at 1000 with the console open.
acceptance: GIVEN the app test suite WHEN it is run with Playwright available THEN a rendered test asserts that all three constraint chips are fully inside the strip's clip box at 1000, 1280, 1440 and 1920 with the console both open and closed, AND it fails if the strip's `flex:0 0 auto` or the header's `flex-wrap:wrap` is removed, AND it skips with a printed reason plus a manual procedure when Playwright is unavailable.

title: The ask test's own tripwire has fired: the route landed, the assertion still says it cannot
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 §9 (Ask is a scoped request whose output is always a proposal).

`app/tests/test_direction_writes_rendered.py::test_ask_is_offered_at_three_scopes_and_never_pretends_it_recorded_anything` fails, and it is failing exactly as its own comment asks it to:

    # only honest outcome is a refusal that names the gap. When the route lands
    # this assertion must fail and be replaced by one about the proposal.
    assert "Nothing was asked" in said

Measured 2026-09-04:

    the app said: Proposal VISION.v1-candidate is waiting in Review.
    working tree unchanged: False
    HEAD unchanged: True
    AssertionError: an ask that could not be carried did not say so

So the ask route (converge-ddt) has landed, the ask really does write a `*-candidate.md` proposal, and the assertion that pinned its absence is now the only thing wrong.

**This is pre-existing, not a regression.** Verified by running the same test in a scratch worktree at HEAD~1, before lane w8-direction-final's commit: it fails identically there. That lane owns only `app/static/js/render/direction.js`, `actions.js`, `api.js`, `direction.html`, `direction.css` and its own new test file, so it recorded this rather than editing another lane's test.

The fix is the replacement the comment already names: assert that the ask returns a proposal — the candidate file beside the document, the toast naming it, and the document itself untouched.
acceptance: GIVEN the app with the ask route answering WHEN `pytest app/tests/test_direction_writes_rendered.py` runs THEN every test passes, AND the ask test asserts the proposal it now produces — the `*-candidate.md` written beside the document, named on screen — rather than asserting that nothing was asked.

title: platform-android: no Android body exists, so nine clauses cannot be checked
description:
Contract: platform-android.v1 §1-§9 - the whole contract, ratified DRAFT 2026-09-03.

There is no Android body anywhere in this repository or beside it, so not one of
the contract's nine clauses can be checked. The nine ledger rows (CVG-240 to CVG-248)
each say so in those words rather than reporting a quiet pass.

The clauses describe a bottom navigation bar, notification channels, the system back gesture, a share target, a widget or quick-settings tile - all of them shapes a real Android application
takes. None of that can be judged from a file scan, a route table, or the
companion web page; it needs the body itself.

Making these checkable therefore means building the body, and that is a
sub-project rather than a lane in this queue: its own repository, its own
steward, and its own Converge instance with its own ledger derived from this
same contract. Filed so the debt is visible in one place, and parked in the
same breath so nobody mistakes it for work that can start here.

Derived 2026-09-04 by the gap analysis in docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md.
acceptance: GIVEN a Android body built against experience.v1 and platform-android.v1 WHEN a conformance kit for that body runs against it THEN each of the nine clauses is either kept, with a rule that can tell a right body from a wrong one, or says in plain words what a machine cannot settle about it. Until such a body exists there is nothing here to start.

title: Editing run.sh while a run is in flight re-executed its tail and launched a second container
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 14 (the adopter harness is how Core 14 is measured)

Measured 2026-09-06, lane w14-adopt-rerun. The adopter run started at 08:57:06Z. At about 09:05Z the header COMMENT block of evaluations/adopter/run.sh was edited to document the --scenarios existing-project invocation - five lines added near the top, roughly 250 bytes. The run finished correctly at 09:16:45Z and wrote RESULT.md. One second later, at 09:16:46Z, the SAME run.sh process (same pid) logged "output:" again, registered a second container adopter-20260906091646-s2 in the infra ledger, launched it, and started a second AI user with a fresh 2400s budget.

The cause is bash, not the harness: bash reads a script incrementally, remembering a BYTE OFFSET into the file. Inserting bytes above that offset shifts everything below it, so when the long-running command returned, bash resumed reading at an offset that now landed mid-script - re-running the tail from the "output:" log line onward. Only one "preflight" line appears in the log, which is the tell.

The cost, had nobody been watching: a duplicate hour-long container and provider session, and a RESULT.md overwritten by a run nobody asked for. It was caught within a minute because the log was being polled; the duplicate process was killed and its container destroyed (amplifier-digital-twin list shows no adopter-* remaining).

Not a defect in run.sh's own logic - the script is correct and ran once. It is a hazard of the way it is invoked, and it is invisible: nothing warns, and the second run looks exactly like a legitimate one in the log.

Options for whoever takes this, cheapest first: (a) say it in evaluations/adopter/README.md - do not edit run.sh, harness.py or anything else the run reads while a run is in flight; (b) have run.sh exec a copy of itself from a temp file, which makes the whole script immune (the classic fix); (c) have the harness refuse to launch when a container matching its own run-id prefix is already running.

Worth noting beyond this harness: any long-running .sh in this repository has the same exposure, and a lane editing scripts while its own run is going is a normal thing to do.
acceptance: GIVEN a run of evaluations/adopter/run.sh in flight, WHEN the script file is edited, THEN either the run is unaffected (it reads no more bytes from the edited file), or a reader of evaluations/adopter/README.md was told plainly not to do it. GIVEN the harness log of such a run THEN it shows exactly one container launch per scenario asked for.

title: composition.v1 §5 sanctions two install paths while the readiness bar asks for one, so the README cannot be right either way
description:
Contract: composition.v1 §5

The steward's definition of ready for early adopters is "one install command; nothing else to know". composition.v1 does not say that. §1 says a lean base and §2 says automated steps use only that base's helpers — neither is about how many commands there are. §5 says, in as many words, "The shared work queue rides on both install paths": the contract assumes two.

So the README's two paths (README.md:53-100) are not a broken clause. Nothing is broken. But the README cannot be made to satisfy the bar while the contract sanctions the thing the bar objects to, and today it tries to serve both — README.md:53 calls the --app behavior "THE install path", and README.md:93-96 then recommends the other one for exactly what an adopter does first, an end-to-end run against a target repo. Whichever path a reader picks, the README told them the other.

The remedy is a decision, not an edit: either the contract names one path and the other becomes an advanced note, or the readiness bar stops asking for one and the README is judged on making the choice trivial instead. Both are the steward's word, so this reaches them as a ratify call rather than a lane.

Found by the onboarding audit, docs/workflow/ONBOARDING-AUDIT-2026-09-04.md, findings a-1, a-2, and "Two things no contract covers", 1.
acceptance: Given the steward has answered, when a reader opens README.md's install section, then either exactly one command is presented as the path an adopter takes and any second path is clearly marked as advanced, or the readiness bar records that two paths are correct and says how a reader chooses in one sentence. Given either outcome, when the same reader finishes that section, then nothing later in the README recommends against the path it just told them to take.

title: Steward decision + ready-to-file upstream issue: bkrabach/amplifier-bundle-converge@main ships a session-wide spawn: block
description:
RESIDUAL from converge-w3v. The cause is outside this repository, so this lane proved it and stopped. Two things are needed from the steward: a decision, and (if the decision is "fix the fork") the issue text below, which is written to be pasted as-is.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (2026-09-04, this host, control/treatment/attribution/removal-control; every row is the composed mount plan's `spawn` plus the tool modules a spawned helper inherits per the shipped apply_spawn_tool_policy):

  A control  -- unrelated `anchors` session, nothing composed:
      spawn: null   helper keeps: tool-bash, tool-delegate, tool-skills
  B treatment -- the same session as this host composes it (22 app bundles):
      spawn: {"exclude_tools": ["tool-delegate","tool-skills","tool-bash"]}
      helper LOSES all three
  C attribution -- each of the 22 app entries composed alone; exactly ONE carries a spawn policy:
      git+https://github.com/bkrabach/amplifier-bundle-converge@main#subdirectory=behaviors/converge.yaml
      (microsoft/amplifier-bundle-converge, installed on the same host, is clean: spawn null)
  D removal control -- the host app list MINUS that one entry:
      spawn: null   helper keeps all three, 22 tool modules

Reproduce: `uv run conformance/composition/run.py .` in this repo; rule 6c now reports it by name.

THE DECISION (converge-w3v names three options; recommendation last):
  1. The fork drops the `spawn:` block (bundle.md:54 and behaviors/converge.yaml) -- fixes it for everyone who installed the fork.
  2. The entry is removed from this host's app list: `amplifier bundle remove` / edit ~/.amplifier/settings.yaml:27 -- fixes this host only, leaves the published bundle harmful.
  3. The steward rules the two Converge bundles are the same product and one is stale -- then 1 and 2 both follow.
  RECOMMENDED: 2 first (it is one line and immediate -- every session on this machine currently spawns helpers with no bash, no delegate, no load_skill), then 1 so the harm does not travel to the next person who installs the fork.
  NOT DONE BY THIS LANE: settings.yaml is host-wide shared state with other lanes live on it, and it is outside this lane's file ownership.

-- UPSTREAM ISSUE TEXT (paste into bkrabach/amplifier-bundle-converge) --

Title: A session-wide `spawn.exclude_tools` strips bash, delegate and load_skill from every spawned helper in every session on the host

Installing this bundle with `--app` takes tools away from sessions that have nothing to do with Converge.

`bundle.md:54` (and the same block in `behaviors/converge.yaml`) declares:

    spawn:
      exclude_tools:
        - tool-delegate
        - tool-skills
        - tool-bash

An app bundle is composed onto EVERY session (amplifier_app_cli/runtime/config.py hands `get_settings().get_app_bundles()` to `load_and_prepare_bundle` as `compose_behaviors`), and `spawn` lands in the composed root mount plan. `apply_spawn_tool_policy` then filters those modules out of the parent tool list on every spawn -- for all agents, in all sessions, not just Converge's.

Measured on a host with this bundle app-installed (control, treatment, attribution, removal control -- full numbers above): an unrelated `anchors` session's spawned helper loses tool-bash, tool-delegate and tool-skills. Removing this one entry from the app list restores them; no other one of the 22 installed app bundles declares a spawn policy at all.

The block's comment calls it the "GUARANTEED path" for the agents' negative-capability contracts. It is -- it guarantees them for everybody's agents, in everybody's sessions.

Ask: drop the `spawn:` block from both files. Per-role spawn tool policy is the upstream feature request this needs (see microsoft/amplifier #388); until it lands, agent tool limits belong in the agents' own `tools:` blocks and body instructions.

For reference, microsoft/amplifier-bundle-converge removed exactly this block on 2026-09-02 after measuring the same harm, records the rule in PINS.md ("Never reintroduce a session-wide `spawn:` block"), states it as a contract clause (composition.v1 Core 6), and as of 2026-09-04 has a standing conformance rule (6c) that fails when an app-installed release of the product strips a neighbour's tools.
acceptance: GIVEN this host WHEN `uv run conformance/composition/run.py .` is run in amplifier-bundle-converge THEN rule 6c reports PASS -- the unrelated session's mount plan carries no session-wide spawn.exclude_tools and its spawned helper keeps tool-bash, tool-delegate and tool-skills -- which becomes true once either the fork drops the block or the entry leaves the host's app list. Falsified by 6c still reporting FAIL and naming an app-installed release of this product.

title: The Direction header shows the whole objective sentence, so it grows to a third of the screen
description:
Contract: platform-web.v1 §14 (nothing cut off, nothing overlapping) — this is not a breach of it, it is the cost of keeping it, and it is a design call someone should make deliberately.

`#objectiveText` in `app/templates/direction.html` is filled with the first sentence of the batch's Outcome section (`app/data.py`, `manager_card`). In the real batch that sentence is 270 characters. The header renders it in full at 16px with no clamp, so the header's height is a function of how much someone wrote.

Measured in Chromium against a realistic objective, before and after converge-6qk's strip fix (header height, console open):

  1000  233px -> 261px
  1100  186px -> 238px
  1200  163px -> 215px
  1280  140px -> 215px
  1440  140px -> 215px
  1600  117px -> 163px
  1920  117px -> 117px

The growth is real and was accepted knowingly: before the fix the header was shorter because two of the three constraint chips were not being drawn at all. But 261px of a 800px viewport is a third of the screen spent on a band that is meant to be a summary, and the document surface below is the actual work.

Options a steward or the owning lane might weigh: clamp the objective to two lines with the full text one gesture away; take a shorter objective from the batch; or accept the height as the honest price of showing all three constraints. This lane owned only `app/static/css/shell.css` and could not touch the template or the payload, so it recorded the number rather than choosing.
acceptance: GIVEN the Direction view at 1280px with the console open and a 270-character objective WHEN the workspace header is rendered THEN the header occupies no more than a stated, deliberately chosen height, AND the full objective text is reachable without leaving the view, AND all three constraint chips remain fully readable.

title: operation.v1 Core 14 has no ledger row, so the ledger goes red the moment the ratified clause lands in the contract
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §Core 14

The steward ratified Core 14, "The first wake is investigate, then propose", on 2026-09-06 (docs/workflow/owner-ratifications-2026-09-06.md). The proposal named this consequence rather than leaving it to be discovered: ledger/checks/verify.py §6.1 requires every Core clause to be cited by at least one row.

Measured in this worktree on 2026-09-06, before the clause is applied:

  $ uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py
    operation.v1.md          13 Core clauses, cited 13/13  OK
  ALL LEDGER SELF-CHECKS PASS

contracts/operation.v1.md still carries 13 Core clauses here because the apply lane is putting clause 14 into it in parallel. On the commit where that lands, the same command reports 13/14 MISSING ['Core 14'] and exits non-zero until a row exists.

The row's honest starting verdict is not yet, not kept. What the clause promises is now written in two places -- the clause 14 section of modes/converge-manager.md and context/manager/first-wake.md, both landed under converge-dnip -- but no run has taken a project along that path. evaluations/adopter/RESULT.md is the only recorded result and it reads red, from 2026-09-04, before either file existed. A row seeded at kept because the section exists is exactly the drift the ledger is for. converge-njaj carries the same missing observation.

ledger/rows.yaml was outside converge-dnip's file ownership, which is why this is filed rather than done.

Nearest precedent: converge-lhkf, the same shape for composition.v1's new kit-assert bullet.
acceptance: Given contracts/operation.v1.md carries Core 14, when someone runs uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py, then it prints operation.v1.md 14 Core clauses, cited 14/14 OK and all ledger self-checks pass. Given the new row, when a reader looks at its verdict, then it reads not yet -- with the reason beside it naming that no recorded run has taken a project along the first-wake path -- and it is not kept until an adopter-harness run says so. Given the row cites work, then the item it names is converge-njaj, the item that would produce that run.

title: Seven operation clauses have no runner — the turnkey's nine steps exercise none of them
description:
Contract: operation.v1 — Core 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 11, 13, and its own "Conformance kit asserts" list.

The turnkey harness (evaluations/turnkey/run.py) went green on 2026-09-04 and the steward ratified the sentence recording it into the contract. Its nine steps assert: a fresh environment, one install, the install check, a project started, work derived from a contract gap, two real lanes, integration, a re-check, and a return brief.

Seven Core clauses are exercised by none of those steps. Re-derived from a live observed run on 2026-09-04 (`uv run evaluations/turnkey/run.py --env local --workspace ~/dev/hw-converge --project converge --steps e,f,g,h,i`), each row's probe reads only whether modes/converge-manager.md still carries the clause's section — which is the mode encoding the rule, never the manager session following it:

    CVG-012  Core 2   the plan is visible — order, dependencies, collisions, opportunistic picks, with reasons
    CVG-013  Core 3   never the bottleneck — work that proceeds without the steward is maximised
    CVG-014  Core 4   feedback is signal — evidence quoted, reports merged and split before filing
    CVG-016  Core 6   width is a collision decision — lanes fill only with items that provably touch different files
    CVG-019  Core 9   stalls are decisions — no progress across iterations becomes stuck with cause
    CVG-021  Core 11  four calls reach the steward — anything else is a defect to file
    CVG-023  Core 13  hand off when done — a manager session that has lost its footing writes a hand-off and stops

Each is a promise about what a manager session DOES across a wave, and each needs an observation nothing currently takes. Some are cheap (clause 6: compare the files two concurrent lanes own against the launcher's manifest; clause 13: count hand-offs against manager sessions that ended by choice). Some need counting events across a whole wave (clause 3, clause 11 — evaluations/ratchet already counts owner-facing prompt events, but for the reconciler, not for a manager session). Clause 4 needs a raw report and its filed item side by side.

Discovered while re-deriving fifteen ledger rows for converge-0gb. These seven were red pending the turnkey; the turnkey is green and does not touch them, so the reason they are not yet kept has changed and is now written down.

Whoever takes this should not assume one lane closes all seven. Pick the ones an observation can reach, and say plainly which are left.
acceptance: GIVEN operation.v1 Core 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 11 and 13 WHEN a check is run that observes a manager session's behaviour rather than the mode file's text THEN at least one of the seven carries a live reading that says whether the promise was kept, and each of the remaining ones names what observation it still waits on; AND the matching ledger row quotes that reading; AND `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` exits 0.

title: On Home at phone width the Manager Console control reads "on" while no pane is drawn
description:
A residual of converge-nxf's fix, written down by the lane that made it rather than left for a steward to find.

WHAT IS TRUE NOW. Below 980px the console is an overlay, and `platform-web.v1` Core 1 says it is a pane beside Direction or Operation, never a third place -- so `app/static/css/console.css` now stows the sheet while the shell is on Home. The console's own open state is deliberately untouched: the pane must be exactly as the steward left it the moment they open a manager session.

THE GAP. `#consoleToggle`'s `aria-pressed` and its `active` class are set from `state.consoleOpen` in `app/static/js/render/console.js`, so on Home at 390 the control reads "on" while nothing is drawn. Measured 2026-09-04 at 390x844 on Home: `{pointerEvents: 'none', gridClosed: false, togglePressed: 'true'}`. A steward who taps it there sees nothing change on that screen -- the tap turns the pane off for Direction and Operation, which is real but invisible from where they are standing.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED HERE. `app/static/js/render/console.js` and `app/static/js/state.js` are outside lane w8-web-polish's file ownership.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT AVAILABLE. Starting the console CLOSED below 980px -- which is what converge-nxf itself suggested -- was measured against the suite and is not viable: eight rendered test files drive `if width < 980: page.click("#consoleToggle")` to push the sheet down before acting (`test_offline.py`, `test_direction_final.py`, `test_direction_persist.py`, `test_direction_polish.py`, `test_direction_writes_rendered.py`, `test_presence.py`, `test_shell_home.py`, `test_writes_named.py`). With the console starting closed, every one of those clicks OPENS it instead, and each then waits for `pointer-events: none` that never comes. Whoever changes the default has to change those eight callers in the same commit.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS. Either the control says what is true on Home (not pressed, or a word naming where the pane is), or the pane is genuinely off on Home and the eight callers above move with it.
acceptance: GIVEN the app at 390 pixels on Home WHEN the steward reads the Manager Console control THEN what it says matches what is on the screen -- and if they tap it, something they can see changes; AND `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests` stays green.

title: A held-loosely document now says it is held, but not why — the reason lives only in the lock sheet
description:
Contract: documents.v1 Core 6 (status lives in the H1 parenthetical and nowhere else) against skills/freeze-bar/SKILL.md, which says what the hold-loosely state costs to keep honest:

    - The bar is met, and that is written down.
    - The document is deliberately not locked.
    - The steward's call is recorded, with the reason, in the document itself.

Lane w19-tidy closed converge-0ket by writing `held loosely 2026-09-06` into the H1 of contracts/documents.v1.md, contracts/operation.v1.md and contracts/platform-web.v1.md. That satisfies the first two bullets and half of the third: a reader can now tell a document deliberately left open from a draft nobody decided about.

The reason is still outside the document. It is recorded per document in docs/workflow/LOCK-SHEET-2026-09-06.md:

    | `documents.v1`   | hold loosely | Its own clause 5 is pinned open against it — eight of forty-three clauses break the rule it would freeze. |
    | `operation.v1`   | hold loosely | Two clauses are not yet kept: one waits on an event this host has never had, one is a real miss. |
    | `platform-web.v1`| hold loosely | One promise not yet kept, six that need a rendered viewport, and no kit of its own. |

Why that is not simply a lane oversight: Core 6 says status lives in the H1 and nowhere else, and a reason will not fit an H1 without turning the heading into a paragraph. The two honest places left are the changelog section (which documents.v1 Core 4 makes conditional, and which platform-web.v1 does not have) or a sentence under the H1 — and choosing between them is a change to what a contract's anatomy allows, not an edit to make in passing.

The cost is the one converge-0ket itself named: a reason that lives outside the document it applies to is not re-read when the thing it waited on changes. All three reasons are dated 2026-09-06 and each names a specific condition that could clear on any day.

Left undone rather than fixed in passing: lane w19-tidy's ownership of these three contracts is the H1 parenthetical only.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN a document whose H1 says it is held loosely WHEN a reader opens it THEN the reason the steward left it open is in that document, in a place documents.v1's anatomy allows — or documents.v1 says plainly that the reason belongs in the lock record instead, and names where. FALSIFIED IF the reason is written into the H1 parenthetical, which Core 6 reserves for status.

title: Where a manager session starts: workspace root, and <workspace>/.converge/<manager-id>/ for its record and lanes
description: Contract: operation.v1 §1 (a steward starts a manager session from the CLI in their project) and composition.v1 §2 (nothing lands outside the project). Cause, measured 2026-09-05: modes/converge-manager.md says nothing about WHERE a manager session runs or where its plan record and lane worktrees live; it points at the ten-lane-highway practice, whose SKILL.md (line 116) says 'create one per highway, e.g. ~/dev/hw-<name>' — so thirteen batch directories now sit under ~/dev, outside every workspace root, and a manager session starts wherever the steward happened to type amplifier. Fix in this repository: the mode states that a manager session runs from the WORKSPACE ROOT (the nearest ancestor holding WORKSPACE-MANIFEST.json, else the project repository's root) and that its plan record, lane worktrees, logs and infra ledger live at <workspace>/.converge/<manager-id>/ — never under the home directory — passing that path as BATCH_DIR to every highway/goal-batch launch; context/manager gains the same rule where the launch is taught; README gains a 'Start your first manager session' section (cd to the workspace root; the one command; what appears where); the .converge/ directory carries a README explaining itself and is git-ignored by the template. The skill's example text is upstream — record the upstream note in the item's resolution, do not edit the CLI.
acceptance: GIVEN modes/converge-manager.md THEN one clause names the workspace root as where a manager session runs and <workspace>/.converge/<manager-id>/ as where its record and lanes live, with the reason; GIVEN README.md THEN a reader who has never heard of Converge can start a manager session in three steps from the workspace root; GIVEN the documents kit THEN PASS; GIVEN a dry read of the mode by the manager session THEN the next highway launch on this host uses <workspace>/.converge/converge/ as BATCH_DIR.

title: platform-windows: no Windows body exists, so nine clauses cannot be checked
description:
Contract: platform-windows.v1 §1-§9 - the whole contract, ratified DRAFT 2026-09-03.

There is no Windows body anywhere in this repository or beside it, so not one of
the contract's nine clauses can be checked. The nine ledger rows (CVG-280 to CVG-288)
each say so in those words rather than reporting a quiet pass.

The clauses describe a title bar carrying the manager session, a tray icon, the system notification centre, a sidebar, full keyboard reach - all of them shapes a real Windows application
takes. None of that can be judged from a file scan, a route table, or the
companion web page; it needs the body itself.

Making these checkable therefore means building the body, and that is a
sub-project rather than a lane in this queue: its own repository, its own
steward, and its own Converge instance with its own ledger derived from this
same contract. Filed so the debt is visible in one place, and parked in the
same breath so nobody mistakes it for work that can start here.

Derived 2026-09-04 by the gap analysis in docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md.
acceptance: GIVEN a Windows body built against experience.v1 and platform-windows.v1 WHEN a conformance kit for that body runs against it THEN each of the nine clauses is either kept, with a rule that can tell a right body from a wrong one, or says in plain words what a machine cannot settle about it. Until such a body exists there is nothing here to start.

title: Ask reports the wrong cause for every failure, including offline
description:
`app/static/js/actions.js`'s `sendAsk` catches every failure with one fixed sentence: "Nothing was asked — this app answers no proposal route yet (<message>). Filed as converge-ddt."

Two things are now wrong with it.

1. The route exists. converge-ddt landed on main (48cdc90, lane w8-ask-route), so "this app answers no proposal route yet" is false for every failure the control can now meet.
2. Offline it names the wrong cause. converge-719 makes `sw.js` refuse an offline write in its own plain sentence — "you are offline, so nothing was asked — reconnect and ask again, or tell the manager session directly" — and `api.js` carries that sentence out as `err.message`. `sendAsk` then wraps it in a claim about a missing route. Measured 2026-09-04 in a rendered browser with the network off: the sentence itself is correct all the way to `err.message`; only this toast's frame around it is wrong.

Every other write in the file already does the right thing — `Could not steer: <sentence>`, `Could not file the feedback: <sentence>` — so the fix is to make this one match: report `err.message` and stop asserting a cause.

The offline banner shows the correct sentence whole and unprefixed, so a steward is not actually misled today; the toast beside it contradicts the banner, which is its own defect.

Owner: whoever owns `app/static/js/actions.js`. The converge-719 lane owns only `sw.js`, `offline.js`, `base.html` (banner + script tag) and the banner rule in `shell.css`, so this is written down rather than made.

Serves platform-web.v1 Core 2 ("evidence is shown rather than claimed") and §11.
acceptance: GIVEN the app with the network off WHEN an ask is sent THEN the toast carries the worker's own refusal sentence and claims no other cause, and GIVEN the network up and the ask route answering WHEN an ask fails for any other reason THEN the toast does not claim the route is missing.

title: Two lines still name ledger/checks/surface_clause9.py, which was deleted with the retired page's last reader
description:
Contract: documents.v1 — a document says what is true, and a fact that has stopped being a fact is removed rather than left standing.

ledger/checks/surface_clause9.py was deleted on 2026-09-06 by converge-g499, the reconcile after the web page was retired. The file rendered its subject from amplifier_converge.web.app, which the retirement removed, so every run of it exited 1 with an empty stdout and a ModuleNotFoundError. CVG-038, the one row that ran it, no longer does.

Two lines outside that lane still name it, and each is one sentence to settle:

1. src/amplifier_converge/README.md line 39 lists it as one of three live readers of conformance/_superseded/surface/. Two readers remain — conformance/documents/run.py and tests/conftest.py — so the retired kit still stays where it is; only the count and the list are now wrong.

2. converge-4iu0 item 2 explains that the `web` extra in pyproject.toml stayed because ledger/checks/surface_clause9.py and conformance/_superseded/surface/README.md both invoke `uv run --extra web`. The retired kit's README still does, so the extra still has a reader and must not be dropped on the strength of this deletion alone. Whoever settles converge-4iu0 should read this before deciding.

Neither line is in ledger/, which is why this is filed rather than fixed.

---

WHAT LANDED ON 2026-09-06 (lane w19-tidy, commit 5df2f22). TWO OF THE THREE
ACCEPTANCE CLAUSES ARE MET. THE FIRST IS NOT, AND THE FOUR LINES THAT FAIL IT
ARE ALL IN ledger/ — WHICH THIS ITEM'S OWN DESCRIPTION ASSUMED WERE CLEAR.

CLAUSE 2 — MET. src/amplifier_converge/README.md now names the two readers of
conformance/_superseded/surface/ that actually exist (conformance/documents/run.py
and tests/conftest.py), and says in past tense what happened to the third: it
went with the page on the same day, because it rendered its subject from the
module the retirement removed.

CLAUSE 3 — MET, on the "kept" branch. The `web` extra stays, and its remaining
reason is now written down in the same file rather than living only in a work
item: conformance/_superseded/surface/README.md still invokes `uv run --extra
web` (lines 45 and 58), and uv refuses outright — rather than warning — when an
extra named on the command line is not defined. Confirmed on this tree:

    $ grep -rn "extra web" conformance/_superseded/surface/README.md
    45:uv run --extra web amplifier-converge web --repo . --port 8091
    58:uv run --extra web --with httpx conformance/surface/render.py \

CLAUSE 1 — NOT MET. The full grep, run on this tree after the change:

    $ grep -rn "surface_clause9" . --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=.venv --exclude-dir=__pycache__
    src/amplifier_converge/README.md:41   ✓ past tense — "it went with the page on the same day"
    ledger/rows.yaml:205                  ✓ the record of its deletion
    ledger/rows.yaml:272                  ✗ "Four probe helpers now live beside it — turnkey_step.py, surface_clause9.py, …"
    ledger/rows.yaml:280                  ✗ "surface_clause9.py imports the shipped surface kit"
    ledger/rows.yaml:2839                 ✗ "the same reasoning surface_clause9.py records for the surface kit"
    ledger/rows.yaml:3918                 ✓ "is deleted here (CVG-038)"
    ledger/rows.yaml:4114, 4118           ✓ the record of its deletion
    ledger/checks/return_log_ratio.py:29  ✗ "That is the reasoning surface_clause9.py already records for the surface kit"
    docs/work-items.json:1795, 2040       — an export of the queue, not a document (see converge-4iu0 item 4)

Four lines claim, in the present tense, that the file exists or that it reads or
records something. Two of them (272, 280) are a top-of-file comment block that
already carries its own correction history and says a comment which has quietly
stopped being true is the same species of drift as a row that has — so it is
failing its own stated rule. The other two cite reasoning the deleted file
"records", which sends a reader looking for a file that is not there.

WHY THIS WAS MISSED WHEN THE ITEM WAS FILED: this item's description says
"Neither line is in ledger/", and ledger/rows.yaml:205 — written by the deleting
lane — says "Two lines outside ledger/ still name it; filed as converge-3hew
rather than touched." Both were surveying for the file being NAMED as a live
reader of the retired kit, and both were right about that. Neither noticed that
the ledger's own prose elsewhere still describes the file in the present tense.
The acceptance says "across the tree", and across the tree it is not clear.

Left undone rather than fixed in passing: ledger/rows.yaml is in lane w19-tidy's
ownership for rows CVG-054 and CVG-301 only, and ledger/checks/return_log_ratio.py
is not in it at all. Neither of the failing regions is in either row.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: four sentences put into the past tense, in two files. None
of them is load-bearing — they are all citations of reasoning the deleted file
recorded, and that reasoning is preserved verbatim in ledger/rows.yaml:4114-4118
and in return_log_ratio.py's own comment, so nothing is lost by saying it in the

title: Lane w9-old-truths' brief listed feedback_voice.js as ownable but not the one sw.js line that must move with it
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §5 (a lane brief is the whole of what a worker session gets), and skills/lane-brief/SKILL.md's "explicit file-ownership split".

Lane w9-old-truths was briefed to close twelve items, converge-s7e9 among them, and its GOAL.md summary names that work outright: "s7e9: move the voice half out of actions.js into feedback_voice.js." Its ownership list includes `app/static/js/feedback_voice.js` — a file that did not exist yet — but not `app/static/sw.js`.

converge-s7e9's own description names that omission as the whole reason the split had not already happened: "create app/static/js/feedback_voice.js from the section marked 'Feedback as a voice note' in actions.js, import it there, and add '/static/js/feedback_voice.js' to PRECACHE in app/static/sw.js." Its acceptance is "the precache check names /static/js/feedback_voice.js as present", which cannot hold without that line. Measured with the module in place and no PRECACHE entry:

    MISSING /static/js/feedback_voice.js
    FAILED app/tests/test_web_polish.py::
        test_the_precache_list_carries_every_module_the_app_loads

So the brief asked for a change whose stated acceptance its own ownership list forbade, and the same brief requires the whole app suite green at the end. There was no obedient reading that satisfied both.

A second, smaller instance in the same brief: converge-6pbg's acceptance covers `app/templates/operation.html` explicitly ("WHEN a steward reads the shell fold AND the Operation feedback fold THEN neither says a voice note is not recorded here"), and that file is not in the ownership list either.

WHAT THE LANE DID, so it is on the record rather than discovered later: it made both edits — one array line in sw.js, one sentence in operation.html — and disclosed them in the commit messages, in the resolutions, and in DONE.json. It first checked the two concurrently-live lanes' briefs (w9-queue-and-kits, w9-reconcile-4) and neither owns either file, so the collision risk the ownership split exists to prevent was nil.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN LEFT AS A JUDGEMENT CALL. The lane-brief skill's remedy for a criterion outside the lane's ownership is to record it as a residual and keep outcome A. That remedy assumes the criterion can be left undone. Here it could not: leaving s7e9 undone was available, but doing it partially was not, and the brief named it in its own one-line summary of the lane. A brief that names work in its summary should own the files that work needs.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: either the brief-writing procedure derives the ownership list from the files each item's description names (s7e9 named sw.js in plain words), or the skill gains a sentence about what a lane does when an item's acceptance and its ownership list contradict each other — which is a different situation from a criterion that is merely out of reach.
acceptance: GIVEN a lane brief that names a work item whose description names a file WHEN the ownership list is written THEN that file is either in the list or the brief says in so many words which part of the item the lane is expected to leave undone; AND skills/lane-brief/SKILL.md distinguishes "a criterion outside this lane's ownership" (residual, outcome stays A) from "a criterion whose ownership list contradicts the item's own acceptance", naming what a lane does in the second case.

title: Direction: restore can only reach the steward's read point, not an arbitrary history snapshot
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 section 6.

Section 6 asks that restoring from history be a real action at four scopes. converge-wrx made it one: the History view now offers Restore at wording, paragraph, section and whole-document scope, and each is the app's own changes/{change_id}/restore write, one sentence at a time — committing on a draft, writing a proposal beside a locked document.

What it cannot reach is any snapshot other than the steward's own read point. The only sentences app/changes.py can still find are the ones in the current reading (the diff between the read point and HEAD), so a History row older than that read point has no restorable wording behind it. The panel says this plainly on the screen rather than implying time travel it does not have.

Closing this needs server files no Direction lane has owned so far — app/serve.py and app/writes.py. The design field carries the smallest shape that works; it is two optional parameters, not a new subsystem.

Found while working converge-wrx; filed rather than made, because the routes are another lane's files. Confirmed still true and still out of reach by lane w8-direction-polish on 2026-09-04, which owns only the browser half (app/static/js/**, app/templates/direction.html, app/static/css/direction.css) and deliberately did NOT ship a control with no route behind it. The acceptance was lost into this description when the item was first filed; it is in its own field now, unchanged in wording.
acceptance: GIVEN a document with several commits in its History WHEN the steward picks a snapshot older than their read point and restores at any of the four scopes THEN the document (or, if locked, a proposal beside it) carries the wording as of that snapshot, and the History panel no longer says arbitrary snapshots are out of reach.
design:
Measured while working w8-direction-polish, 2026-09-04. The restore machinery ALREADY works for an arbitrary snapshot: app/changes.py's changes_for(repo, path, since=<sha>) and find_change(..., since=<sha>) take any commit, and a card's `before` is exactly the wording as it stood at `since`. What is missing is only a way for the browser to name one — app/serve.py hard-codes `since` to the steward's stored read point in both document() and _reword().

So the smallest honest shape is two optional parameters, and app/writes.py need not change at all (apply_change already takes the resolved card, and already makes the lock check that decides commit-vs-proposal):

1. GET /api/managers/{mid}/docs/{repo}/{doc} accepts an optional ?since=<sha>, used INSTEAD of the stored read point for that one response. It must not move the read point: the read point belongs to the steward, and reading history is not reading.
2. POST .../changes/{change_id}/restore (and /edit, for the same reason) accept an optional `since` in the body, passed straight to changes.find_change.

Bound both: `since` must be one of the shas data.history_for(repo, path) returns for THIS document, else refuse in plain words — "that is not a commit in this document's history". A route that reads any revision the caller names is a different, larger promise than section 6 makes.

Browser half, once the route exists (all inside the Direction lane's own files — app/static/js/render/direction.js, actions.js, api.js): the History row already selected in state.historyId carries its sha; restorePanel reads the document at that sha to list the four scopes against it, each restore write carries the sha, and the Details paragraph naming this item is deleted. app/tests/test_direction_polish.py::test_the_history_panel_still_says_what_a_restore_cannot_reach pins the honest sentence today, and is the test to delete in the same commit that makes that sentence false.

Also worth knowing: app/README.md ("History: restoring, at four scopes") names converge-4pq as the open gap, so this item's id is load-bearing in shipped documentation and in the screen's own words. Whoever closes this updates both.

title: CVG-106's absence probe greps for sqlite/shelve/pickle and misses a JSON store, so the app's per-steward state store passed unnoticed
description:
Contract: experience.v1 Core 7 — "**The app holds no data of its own.** ... A second copy of the truth is a defect, not a cache." Ledger row CVG-106.

MEASURED 2026-09-04 by a scheduled reconcile against target-repo @ a5c6c02.

CVG-106 is an `absence` row, and its own `proves` states the point of that choice:

    "a future silent store flips this row red rather than passing unnoticed"

That is exactly what did not happen. The probe is:

    if grep -rlE "sqlite3|shelve|pickle\.dump" app/*.py | grep -q .; then echo APP-KEEPS-A-STORE; else echo APP-KEEPS-NO-STORE-OF-ITS-OWN; fi

`app/state_store.py` exists and keeps a persistent per-steward store — the read point and the kept marks — as a JSON document written atomically (`json.dump` at line 66, `os.replace` at line 68). Its own module docstring says the two facts "live here and nowhere else", and that keeping them in the browser "would have been easier and wrong".

The store is real on disk, not merely in code:

    -rw------- 1 bkrabach bkrabach 251 Sep  3 23:25 /home/bkrabach/.amplifier/converge-app.state.json

The probe names three storage mechanisms and JSON is not among them, so it printed APP-KEEPS-NO-STORE-OF-ITS-OWN and the row stayed CONFORMS through the change. `app/serve.py` even takes a `--state` argument for this file.

TWO SEPARATE THINGS, and only the first is this item:

1. THE CHECK. An absence assertion is only as good as its list, and this one was written against the storage mechanisms of the day. It must be able to see a store written as a plain file. The same class of narrowness is worth a look across the other five CONFORMS `absence` rows (CVG-010, 181, 186, 189, 212) — CVG-186's list went stale the same way and was rebuilt once already (converge-nf4).

2. THE READING — whether a steward's own read point is "data of its own" under Core 7 — is NOT this item. converge-71q carries it, and this reconcile moved CVG-106 to OPEN-PINNED against that item rather than deciding it.

The order matters: 71q can be answered either way, and this row will still be passing over the store silently until the probe can see it.
acceptance: GIVEN app/state_store.py writing a JSON state file WHEN CVG-106's assertion runs THEN it reports that the app keeps a store, rather than reporting the absence of one; AND the probe is negative-controlled — introducing a plain-file store on a scratch copy is observed to flip it, and removing it is observed to flip it back.

title: A wedged manager session polled for twenty minutes instead of declaring itself stuck
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 9 — "Stalls are decisions, not loops. No progress across iterations → stuck with cause, routed to the plan or the steward."

Caught by the adopter harness run of 2026-09-06T03:50:03Z, scenario 2 (`evaluations/adopter/RESULT.md`, container adopter-20260906035003-s2), alongside converge-p17d, which is the defect that wedged it.

After its own locked-document guard refused the changelog edit, the manager session recognised the sequencing bug and tried to recover by grepping and delegating. It then made no progress for over twenty minutes of continuous polling and never declared itself stuck. The AI user driving the session watched the whole time and got nothing: no cause, no route to the plan, no call to the steward. The scenario's remaining steps were never reached, and the harness read their absence as the FAIL it is.

Core 9 exists precisely for this shape. A refusal it cannot get past is an honest exit — "stuck: the lock guard refuses the changelog edit; here is the file, half-frozen" — and that sentence would have handed the person watching something to act on. Twenty silent minutes hands them nothing.

Note the ordering with converge-p17d: fixing the guard removes THIS wedge, not the behaviour. Any future refusal it cannot get past produces the same silence unless the stall itself becomes a decision.

What fixed looks like: a manager session that stops making progress says so, with the cause, within a bounded number of iterations — never an unbounded retry loop with a person waiting on the other end.
acceptance: Given a manager session that hits a refusal or error it cannot get past, when it has made no progress across a bounded number of iterations, then it declares stuck with the cause in plain words and routes it to the plan or the steward, rather than continuing to poll. Given the adopter harness scenario 2 re-run, then any stall appears in the transcript as a declared stuck with a named cause.

title: CVG-020: repoint the probe at the returns-vs-briefs count the mode now produces
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 10 — "A brief on every return."

converge-823 built the missing half: `modes/converge-manager.md` clause 10 now makes the manager session stamp the return in the log's entry heading the moment the steward's message arrives (`## <date> <HH:MM> — <headline>`), and write the five parts under it as labelled sentences at the end of the turn. Written at two different moments, returns and briefs are now countable against each other. That lane owns the mode and the log only, so the ledger row was left untouched — this is the hand-off.

CVG-020's probe today asserts `MODE-ENCODES-CLAUSE-10-LOG-EXISTS-BRIEFS=9` — briefs with no denominator. The replacement counts both sides. Run verbatim by `bash -c` from the repo root, as ledger/checks/verify.py runs refs:

```
if grep -q "^## Clause 10 - " modes/converge-manager.md && grep -q "Stamp the return before you answer it" modes/converge-manager.md && [ -f docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md ]; then awk 'function f(){if(e_){r++;if(a&&b&&c&&d&&x)br++}a=b=c=d=x=0} /^## [0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9] [0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]/{f();e_=1;next} /^## /{f();e_=0;next} e_&&/\*\*Time away\.\*\*/{a=1} e_&&/\*\*Finished\.\*\*/{b=1} e_&&/\*\*Stuck\.\*\*/{c=1} e_&&/\*\*Needs you\.\*\*/{d=1} e_&&/\*\*Anything quietly broken\.\*\*/{x=1} END{f();print "MODE-STAMPS-RETURNS RETURNS=" r+0 " BRIEFS=" br+0}' docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md; else echo STATE-CHANGED-REREAD-THIS-ROW; fi
```

Measured 2026-09-04 against the merged mode, the verbatim ref in a temp tree:

| log under test | output |
|---|---|
| the real log today | `RETURNS=0 BRIEFS=0` |
| one stamped return, five parts | `RETURNS=1 BRIEFS=1` |
| one stamped return, *time away* folded into *finished* (the defect a real manager session committed) | `RETURNS=1 BRIEFS=0` |
| two stamped returns, one never briefed | `RETURNS=2 BRIEFS=1` |
| an unprompted brief (date-only heading) | `RETURNS=0 BRIEFS=0` — not counted as a return |
| mode reverted, log perfect | `STATE-CHANGED-REREAD-THIS-ROW` |

The reading to record with it: the row turns green when RETURNS equals BRIEFS **and** RETURNS is above zero. Today it is 0/0 — the mechanism is encoded and the comparison is computable, but it has no denominator until a real manager session stamps its first return, so the row stays red on the same reason it has always been red, with the reason now one step shorter. It goes red the moment a stamped return goes unbriefed.

What the probe cannot prove, and the row should say so: a return the manager session never recorded at all leaves no trace either way. That is the honest limit of a record the returning session keeps itself. Closing it further would need a record of returns kept by something other than the session that returns.
acceptance: GIVEN ledger/rows.yaml WHEN CVG-020 is re-derived THEN its probe compares stamped returns against completed briefs (the ref above, or one that counts the same two numbers), its `expect` pins the count measured on the merged result, its `proves` says what the count cannot say, and `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` reports that ref meeting its expect. Falsified if the row still pins a brief count with no denominator, or if the new ref is pinned without being run.

title: A proposal ratified in the app never reaches the contract: the console candidate has sat ratified since 2026-09-05
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 Core 7 (a proposal carries the word to answer with), and PROTOCOL v3 section 5, which says that on ratification the edit lands with a dated changelog entry.

Found on 2026-09-06 while building docs/workflow/LOCK-SHEET-2026-09-06.md.

docs/workflow/owner-ratifications-2026-09-05.md records three words given at the Desk that day. Two of them landed: composition and operation each carry a changelog row for the change they ratified. The third did not.

  2026-09-05T20:01:47-07:00 - Ratified: experience-console (experience-console.v1-candidate)

contracts/experience-console.v1.md has not changed since 2026-09-03:

    $ git log --oneline -2 -- contracts/experience-console.v1.md
    19a3d7b  H1 status: record the steward's given words - nothing locked
    95d2a06  contracts: experience-console.v1 (DRAFT) - the Manager Console

    $ grep -c "REQUIRED\|IDIOM\|EXCLUDED" contracts/experience-console.v1.md
    0
    $ grep -n "Changelog" contracts/experience-console.v1.md
    (no match)

The proposal it names, contracts/experience-console.v1-candidate.md, is still sitting in contracts/ unapplied, and the umbrella kit still reports its ten clauses as carrying none of the four words.

The mechanism, read in the code: app/writes.py record_decision appends the steward's word to the day's ratification record and touches nothing else. Its own docstring says so - "Append the steward's word to today's ratification record." So a word given in the app records the decision and leaves the change unapplied unless a person or a lane applies it, and nothing watches the gap between the two.

Two ways this could be wrong and they need different fixes, so whoever takes it should decide which before touching anything:

1. The word is live and the apply is simply owed. Then the fix is to apply the candidate to the contract with a changelog row citing the 2026-09-05 record, the same way composition and operation were applied.
2. The word came from a trial of the app's decision write rather than a decision the steward meant. Then the record overstates what happened and the fix is in the record, not the contract - and that is a steward's call, not a lane's.

Either way the second half is the same and is the reason this is worth an item rather than a note: nothing today tells anyone that a ratified proposal has not landed. A check that compares each recorded ratification against the contract it names would have caught this on 2026-09-06 rather than leaving it for a reader.

Why it matters now: this contract is one of four the lock sheet holds loosely pending a word on its proposal. Locking it in its current state would freeze the exact text the record says the steward already agreed to replace.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN docs/workflow/owner-ratifications-2026-09-05.md records a ratification of experience-console.v1-candidate WHEN the contract it names is read THEN either the change is applied with a changelog row citing that record, or the record is corrected to say what actually happened; AND GIVEN any recorded ratification WHEN a check is run THEN it says plainly whether the contract that ratification names carries the change - not yet while any ratified proposal sits unapplied. title: Twenty-one work items carry leaked tool-call markup in their description, and their acceptance field is empty
description:
Contract: documents.v1 Core 9 ("A work item names its contract in one line, defines done in plain words") — the words are there, but they are in the wrong field, wrapped in markup no reader wrote.

Found 2026-09-04 while sweeping rule 9a for converge-dgit. Twenty-one of the 176 exported items end their description with a literal closing tag and then carry their acceptance criteria inline, like this (converge-8er, verbatim tail):

    ...may not cite a closed item as the thing that will fix it.</description>
    <parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN `python3 ledger/checks/return_log_ratio.py` WHEN...

Every one of the twenty-one has an EMPTY acceptance field: the text the filer wrote as acceptance was serialized into the description instead. The cause looks like a tool-call argument leak at filing time — the filing agent's own function-call markup landing in the description string — and it is not confined to one lane or one day.

The items, measured from docs/work-items.json on 2026-09-04: converge-15o, -1pb, -1sfp, -2ib, -76y, -823, -8er, -8r5, -8vj, -9ke, -a5g, -bdc, -czkb, -d9j, -drh, -dvfr, -eci, -pip, -qfg, -tdy, -tm5.

Two costs, both real. A reader of the queue sees markup in the middle of a sentence and has to work out that it is not content. And anything that reads the acceptance FIELD — a dashboard, a lane brief, a person deciding whether to claim — sees nothing at all, though the item does define done.

Deliberately not fixed while sweeping 9a: rule 9a reads the whole item, so it passes either way, and moving text between an item's fields is a different change from naming its contract. Two things need deciding by whoever takes this: whether the fix is a migration of the twenty-one (move the inline block into the acceptance field, strip the tags) or only a fix at the filing end so no twenty-second appears, and where the leak happens — the filing tool, the provider's tool-call serialization, or the agent composing the call.

Discovered from converge-dgit (the documents 9a sweep).

title: Three experience.v1 umbrella clauses are unkept in the web body: the five-at-once limit, the parity mapping, and saying what this body cannot do
