title: Three operation clauses are measured only in part — the harness reads the artifact, never who produced it
description:
Contract: operation.v1 — Core 7, Core 8, Core 12.

Re-derived from a live observed run on 2026-09-04 against this host's own wave:

    uv run evaluations/turnkey/run.py --env local --workspace ~/dev/hw-converge \
        --project converge --steps e,f,g,h,i

Half of each of these three clauses is now measured, live, and the half that is left is named:

CVG-017 — Core 7, "Done means the manager session re-ran the check. A marker is a claim. Done requires commits beyond base (a marker on an unchanged branch is stuck)". The parenthetical is measured: step (f) reported "6 lane(s) sit on an unchanged branch and are recorded stuck: w8-ledger-refs, w8-direction-writes, w8-console, w8-ask-route, w8-turnkey-step-i, w8-brief-convention". What is not measured is the sentence's subject — that the MANAGER SESSION re-ran the check. Step (h) re-runs it, but step (h) is the harness, by design: "contracts re-checked — by this harness, not by the lane that changed them".

CVG-018 — Core 8, "Integrate, verify, re-check. The manager session's own verification, never the worker session's; a post-merge gate when two or more lanes landed in one repository; then the contract check, before the next brief." The middle and the end are measured: step (g) reported "40 lane branch(es) are merged into main"; step (h) reported "The contract check was re-run by this harness after integration: composition.v1 PASS, documents.v1 PASS". The opening — whose verification it was — is not.

CVG-022 — Core 12, "The queue is the shared one, with custody. Atomic claim, heartbeat while held, resolution written for whoever asked." Claim and custody are measured: step (f) placed every held item's process, "no work item was held by a process outside a lane worktree (60 holders checked)". "Resolution written for whoever asked" is read by nothing — the queue stores a resolution string and no check judges who it was written for.

One shared cause: the harness reads artifacts a wave leaves behind, and an artifact does not record which process made it. Two of the three want an attribution the harness could take while the wave runs (it already watches from outside for clause 5); the third wants a reading of resolution text nobody has written.

Discovered while re-deriving fifteen ledger rows for converge-0gb. All three were red pending the turnkey; the turnkey is green and reaches part of each, so the reason has moved and is written down here rather than left pointing at finished work.
acceptance: GIVEN operation.v1 Core 7, Core 8 and Core 12 WHEN the turnkey harness is extended to record who re-ran the post-merge check, and to read the resolutions a wave wrote THEN a live run reports for each of the three whether the whole clause was kept, not just its measurable half; AND CVG-017, CVG-018 and CVG-022 each quote that reading; AND `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` exits 0.

title: A lane's plain state word reaches the screen in the machine's screaming form
description:
Found on 2026-09-04 while closing converge-d83 (the same defect, one element over).

`app/data.py` serves each lane a plain word — `statusLabel` is `Working` / `Quiet` / `Silent — may have died` for a lane at work, and `outcomeLabel` is `Done` / `Stuck` for one that has reported back. The payload is correct and `conformance/experience/run.py` rule 6a PASSes on it.

The screen is not. `app/static/css/operation.css:60` styles the pill that carries it:

    .lane-status { font-size:9px; text-transform:uppercase; ... }

so a steward reads `WORKING`, `QUIET`, `SILENT — MAY HAVE DIED`, `DONE`, `STUCK`. `DONE` is not `Done`: `experience.v1` Core 6 fixes the title-case word and the SCREAMING token is the machine's, which is the whole of the clause.

No rule catches it, and that is worth recording:

- rule 6a reads the payload, which is already plain;
- rule 6b scans served markup for the machine's tokens but skips `.css` routes (`conformance/experience/run.py`, `check_machine_vocabulary_is_folded`), and the token is never written down in the markup — the browser makes it at render time;
- `experience-operation` rule 8 reads the payload field too.

Same shape as converge-d83's second half: the wave phase was repaired in the payload AND had to opt out of `.wave-kicker`'s `text-transform:uppercase` before the plain word actually reached a person. The repair there is an inline `style="text-transform:none"` on the phase span in `render/operation.js`, because this lane does not own `operation.css`.

Two things to decide, not one:
1. the lane pill should stop upper-casing its word (the rule belongs in `operation.css`);
2. a rendered check should exist that would have caught it — `innerText` (text as RENDERED, transform applied), never `textContent` (text as written), which is how it survived a green suite. `app/tests/test_operation_plain.py` has the pattern.

Owner: whoever owns `app/static/css/operation.css` and the lane-card renderer.
acceptance: GIVEN the Operation page is open in a browser at 1280 and at 390 WHEN each lane card's state pill is read with `innerText` THEN every value is one of `Working` · `Quiet` · `Silent — may have died` · `Done` · `Stuck` exactly as written, and none is upper-cased.

title: The app still says a voice note is not recorded here, and it now is: two limit sentences and four assertions state a limit the app no longer has
description:
Contract: experience.v1 §14 (a body says what it genuinely cannot do) and experience-operation.v1 §10 (feedback in whatever form is to hand).

converge-rj1 landed the voice note: the feedback dialog offers `#feedbackVoice accept="audio/*"`, records where the browser can, and `POST /api/managers/{mid}/feedback/{form}` writes the recording into `.converge/feedback/` beside the text. So the limit is gone. The sentences saying it are not, and they are outside that lane's file ownership:

* `app/templates/shell.html:95-96` -- "Feedback as a voice note — not here" / "A voice note is not recorded here — say it in the Manager Console, or drop the audio file into the project's `.converge/feedback/` folder ... Filed as converge-rj1."
* `app/templates/operation.html:77` -- "Text and a screenshot are taken here. A voice note is not recorded here — ... Filed as converge-rj1."

Core 14 asks a body to say what it cannot do. It does not ask it to go on saying so afterwards, and a limit the app does not have is the same defect as a silence about one -- a steward reads it and does not try.

Four assertions in `app/tests/test_writes_named.py` hold those sentences in place, and one of them was written as the tripwire for exactly this moment:

* line 376 -- `assert "audio/*" not in shell and "MediaRecorder" not in shell`, whose own message reads "the app now takes audio - this assertion has fired: replace it with one about the voice write working, and delete the limit sentences (converge-rj1)". It has NOT fired, and that is worth knowing: it reads only the HTML at `/`, while the voice offer sits in `app/static/js/actions.js` beside the image offer it is parallel to (`accept="image/*"` is not in `/` either). The tripwire could never have seen the offer arrive where the offer naturally goes.
* lines 380-385 -- three phrases required to be present in the shell: "voice note is not recorded here", ".converge/feedback/", "converge-rj1".
* line 565 -- the rendered fold must say "voice note is not recorded here".
* line 600 -- `#feedback .op-parity` must say the same.

So all four currently pass while asserting something false.

Measured 2026-09-04 with the voice note landed, `conformance/experience/run.py` against a real server, before and after on the same scratch project:

    before: cannot_do ['raise or lower a priority (`priority`)', 'feedback as voice']
    after : cannot_do ['raise or lower a priority (`priority`)']

-- so the kit already agrees voice is no longer a limit. Nothing in the app agrees yet.

Filed rather than fixed: `app/templates/shell.html` is owned by nobody in wave 8, `app/templates/operation.html` is owned by the concurrently live lane w8-priority-write, and `app/tests/test_writes_named.py` by w8-writes-named.

The two changes belong in one commit: delete the sentences and move the four assertions in the same change, or the suite goes red between them.
acceptance: GIVEN the app is running with the voice note landed WHEN a steward reads the shell fold and the Operation feedback fold THEN neither says a voice note is not recorded here, AND `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests` is green with something still asserting that the voice write works.

title: Workspace header's constraint strip is cut off at every width — two of three chips never render
description:
Contract: platform-web.v1 §14 — "it renders at 390 and 1280 pixels with nothing cut off and nothing overlapping". Ledger row CVG-213 records that clause as one no scan can settle; this is a failure of it measured by hand.

Found while doing the rendered check for converge-c4s (console overflow) on 2026-09-03, in Chromium against the real app.

`.workspace-header`'s `.constraint-strip` needs 348px for its three chips (HARD LIMIT / STRATEGY / LANES, 116px each) but is only ever allotted 92-219px. `.constraint-strip` is `overflow:hidden`, so instead of pushing the page sideways it silently swallows its own content: the STRATEGY and LANES chips are cut off entirely at EVERY width measured, console open or closed.

Measured (strip width vs the 348px its chips need):
  1280 console open   -> 92px   all three chips clipped
  1280 console closed -> 138px  HARD LIMIT ok, STRATEGY + LANES clipped
  1440 console open   -> 102px  all three clipped
  1920 console closed -> 219px  HARD LIMIT ok, STRATEGY + LANES clipped

Cause looks like the flex split in `.workspace-header`: `.objective-block` and `.constraint-strip` are both shrinkable flex items, the objective's text is long, and the strip loses. Likely fix: `.constraint-strip { flex: 0 0 auto; }` in app/static/css/shell.css so the strip keeps its content width and the objective block (already `min-width:0`) yields instead.

Not caused by the console lane: the strip clips identically with the console open and closed, and `app/static/css/shell.css`'s workspace-header rules are untouched on branch lane/app-overflow. Reported rather than fixed because this lane's brief scopes out any other visual change.
acceptance: GIVEN the app open at 1280px on the Direction view WHEN the workspace header is rendered THEN all three constraint chips (HARD LIMIT, STRATEGY, LANES) are fully readable, with no chip cut off mid-word, in both console states and at 1440 and 1920 as well.

title: The app never says whether a contract is Kept — Direction shows Draft/Locked only (surface.v1 Core 8, kit rule 8b)
description:
Measured with the retargeted surface kit against the running app (uv run conformance/surface/run.py http://127.0.0.1:8097 --changes-nothing '/direction/*/mark-read'):

  [FAIL] 8b  no contract is shown as Kept · Not yet · Broken · Pinned open · Can't check — the state beside each one is ['Draft'], which is the document's own status, not whether the promise is being kept

surface.v1 Core 8 fixes two vocabularies. The lane one is spoken: lane cards on Operation say Working / Quiet / Silent — may have died (kit rule 8a passes, 111 states shown, every one a plain word). The contract one is never spoken anywhere. src/amplifier_converge/words.py defines CONTRACT_STATES and maps the internal tokens onto them (conforms -> Kept, gap -> Not yet, violation -> Broken, open pinned -> Pinned open, ...), but nothing reads the ledger: `grep -rn "ledger\|rows.yaml\|CONFORMS" src` returns only words.py itself and the lane/queue/document readers, none of which touch ledger/rows.yaml.

So Direction shows five contracts each chipped `Draft` — the document's own status from its H1, which is documents.v1 clause 6, not surface.v1 clause 8. A steward opening Direction cannot see whether a promise is being kept, which is the whole of clause 8's first half.

ledger/rows.yaml is seeded (62 rows, each carrying a disposition), so the reading exists on disk; what is missing is a reader and a chip.

Owning path: src/amplifier_converge/reading/ (a ledger reader mapping each contract to its rows' worst disposition through words.surface_word) and src/amplifier_converge/web/pages.py (_document_row, to show it beside the Draft/Locked chip rather than instead of it).

Not fixed here: lane w5-surface-kit owns conformance/surface/** only; src/ is explicitly out of scope. The kit rule that catches this is new and stays FAIL until the app speaks the words.
acceptance: GIVEN the companion app reading a project whose ledger is seeded WHEN Direction is opened THEN each contract shows one of Kept · Not yet · Broken · Pinned open · Can't check against reality, alongside its own Draft/Locked status; AND `uv run conformance/surface/run.py <the running app>` reports rule 8b PASS.

title: platform-web: offline the app shows nothing and says nothing
description:
Contract: platform-web.v1 §10, §11 ("Offline it reads what it last synced, and says when that was") and Core 11 ("Offline it refuses the five writes in a plain sentence").

Read from `app/static/sw.js` as committed:

    //   2. /api is network-first and is never written to the cache at all, so a stale
    //      decision or lane state can never be shown as if it were live.

That rule is a good one and it is the reason both clauses are unmet. Static assets are precached, so offline the shell loads — but every payload behind it comes from `/api`, which is never cached, so the shell renders empty. There is nothing that "was last synced" to read, nothing that says when, and no plain sentence refusing a write: `api.js` turns a failed fetch into a toast reading `Could not refresh: <message>`.

The two clauses and the service worker's rule are not actually in conflict — the clause asks for *what was last synced, labelled with when*, which is a different thing from a stale value shown as if it were live. Closing this is a design call about which payloads may be cached with a visible timestamp, not a one-line change.

Owner: whoever owns `app/`. This lane owns `ledger/` and `conformance/` only. No kit rule covers either clause today — no experience kit takes the network away — so the ledger rows are GAP citing this item rather than a rule id.

Ledger rows this closes: CVG-209, CVG-210. Grouped by cause and component on 2026-09-04 by docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md, which is where the whole mapping of rows to items is printed. The rows already named this item as their fix; what was missing was the list, written down here.
acceptance: GIVEN the installed app with the network off WHEN it is opened THEN it shows what it last synced with a visible "as of <time>", and any of the five writes attempted is refused in one plain sentence rather than a failed-request message.

title: Pinned open: the app now keeps a per-steward reading store, and experience.v1 clause 7 says it holds no data of its own (CVG-106)
description:
Contract: experience.v1 Core 7 — "**The app holds no data of its own.** It shows the project's documents, code record, work queue, lanes, return log, and pending decisions. A second copy of the truth is a defect, not a cache."

Measured 2026-09-04 (converge-dgc, the reconcile after wave 8). Since converge-f5f the app keeps `~/.amplifier/converge-app.state.json` (`app/state_store.py`, `--state` overrides the path). Read live on this machine: one steward, `stewards.bkrabach.read["amplifier-bundle-converge/vision"] = {"sha": "afd83c8b…", "at": "2026-09-03T23:25:47-07:00"}`, kept marks empty. Exactly two things per steward and nothing else — the read point (a commit sha the steward has read a document up to) and the kept marks (which changes that steward has said they are keeping). `app/README.md:38` already publishes it in the source-by-source table.

THE TENSION IS REAL AND THE CONTRACT ALREADY KNOWS IT. experience.v1's own Reserved / open questions section asks: "Where the reading cursor behind 'what changed since you last read' is kept, given the app holds no data of its own." That is this question, written by the contract's own author, unanswered.

Two facts pull opposite ways:
- The clause's teeth are kept. "A second copy of the truth is a defect, not a cache" — the store holds no document text, no work item, no lane state, no return log. A sha is a pointer into the truth, not a copy of it.
- The clause's letter is contradicted. The app does now hold a file of its own, per steward, outside the repository.

THE READING PROPOSED, for the steward to accept or reject: per-steward reading state is the STEWARD's, not the project's. Where you have read to is not a fact about the project — two stewards reading the same repository have different, equally correct answers, and neither belongs in the repository's history. Keeping it in the browser was considered and rejected in `app/state_store.py`'s own docstring, because the same person reads on a laptop and again on a phone and must see the same reading.

A CANDIDATE IS ALREADY WRITTEN: `contracts/experience.v1-candidate.md` now carries a second proposed change (clause 7) that distinguishes the project's truth — never copied — from the steward's own reading, kept per person outside the repository, and answers the Reserved question by name. It needs the steward's one word: *ratified · ratified with edits · declined · later*. Until then experience.v1 stands as the law and CVG-106 is OPEN-PINNED, asserting the current behaviour without forging the decision (PROTOCOL §3.3).

CVG-106's old probe passed on a stale proxy and would never have caught this: it grepped `app/*.py` for `sqlite3|shelve|pickle.dump`, and a plain JSON file is none of those. The rebuilt probe pins what the store actually holds — the path, the two-key vocabulary, and that no third module writes files — each break observed firing on a scratch copy 2026-09-04.
acceptance: GIVEN the steward has answered contracts/experience.v1-candidate.md's clause-7 change WHEN CVG-106 is re-derived THEN it carries kept against the ratified wording, or the reading store is gone and it carries kept against the current wording — not pinned open either way. Falsified if the clause is left as it stands and CVG-106 is quietly returned to kept while ~/.amplifier/converge-app.state.json is still written.

title: Nothing a reader reaches is addressed to the adopter's first day; the reading order opens with the rulebook
description:
Contract: documents.v1 §1

documents.v1 §1 says the documents are written for amplified information workers and that anyone who has never opened one can read it. That holds for each document on its own. What is missing is a document for the person who has not decided to be here yet.

README.md:174-179 sets the reading order: docs/PROTOCOL.md, then this README, then docs/ANNOUNCEMENT.md, then docs/design/mechanism-spec.md, then the presentation. The first thing an adopter is told to read is the ratified rules and the fourth is the mechanism specification. Three of the five are documents about how Converge works; none is about using it.

The install section reads the same way. Between README.md:59 and :100 a reader meets a capability layer, a behavior-includes-behavior include, schema_version 2 and helper closures, spawn.exclude_tools, an upstream feature request, and a dated live probe with its collateral finding. Every one of those is true, and every one is internals, placed exactly where the reader is trying to type one line.

README.md:102-136, "What ships", then lists the four agents, the five skills, the hook module, the recipe, the mode file and the src package by path — a maintainer's inventory of parts.

There is no getting-started or quickstart at the repository root. The one "Quickstart" heading, docs/CONTRACTS-README.md:122, is a quickstart by audience for reading contracts, and its steward entry says to read the vision, then the four contracts, then PINS.md. Reading, again, not starting.

Depends on converge-eqds and converge-njaj: a first-day page cannot be written until there is a start command to put in it and a path for it to describe.

Found by the onboarding audit, docs/workflow/ONBOARDING-AUDIT-2026-09-04.md, findings d-1 through d-4.
acceptance: Given a person who has heard of Converge this morning and knows nothing about how it is built, when they open the repository, then the first thing they are pointed at tells them what to do rather than how it works, and following it end to end leaves them with a running manager session on their own project. Given they have done that, when they look back at what they read, then they did not need to read the protocol, the mechanism spec, or any explanation of the composition to get there — those are still available, further down, for when they want them.

title: CVG-186 goes red on main: the app's Ask write starts a second process, and it is not git
description:
Contract: experience-collaboration.v1 Core 7 — "**The manager session is not in the hot path.** A write made in the app goes through the ordinary repository and proposal mechanism directly; the manager session learns of it as an event and folds it into its next turn."

Measured 2026-09-04 on main tip 48cdc90 ("merge lane/w8-ask-route"), with no lane branch merged into it:

```
$ bash -c '<CVG-186's ref, verbatim>'
WRITES-START-A-PROCESS-THAT-IS-NOT-GIT
$ grep -cE "subprocess\.run\(" app/writes.py
2
257:        done = subprocess.run(
450:        done = subprocess.run(
```

At a1b7f82 (origin/main, the previous integration point) the same ref printed `WRITES-GO-STRAIGHT-TO-THE-REPOSITORY-GIT-ONLY` and `subprocess.run(` appeared once. The three commits that changed `app/writes.py` in between are afb1273, 672b6fc and 52452e1 — the Ask route. The new call at line 450 runs `amplifier run --mode single --output-format json <prompt>` to draft the wording an ask becomes.

So the ledger row CVG-186 is CONFORMS with a probe that now fails: `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` on main reports `[FAIL] CVG-186 ... stdout='WRITES-START-A-PROCESS-THAT-IS-NOT-GIT'` and exits 1. The whole ledger gate is red on main because of it.

The reading is a real question, not a formality, and it is why this is filed rather than fixed: a headless drafting session is not *the* manager session, and clause 7's own words are about the manager session learning of a write as an event. Two defensible readings — (a) the clause is kept, the probe is too narrow, and it should distinguish "a manager session" from "any subprocess"; (b) the clause is broken, because a write in the app now blocks on a session finishing. Whoever settles it owns both the row's re-derivation and, if (b), the app change.

Discovered by lane w8-ledger-followups while proving its own two rows against a scratch merge of main. That lane's brief is CVG-020 and CVG-114; re-deriving a third row it was not briefed for, on a reading it does not own, is the blind bump `ledger/rows.yaml` forbids — so it is filed. `app/writes.py` is also outside its file ownership.
acceptance: GIVEN main WHEN `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` is run THEN it exits 0 with CVG-186's ref meeting its expect — either because the probe was re-derived to assert what clause 7 actually forbids (and the row's `proves` says so), or because the app's write path no longer starts a session. Falsified if CVG-186's `expect` is edited to match the failing output with no reading recorded.

title: The host cannot reach its own webhook: /api/collab/webhooks/host is behind the sign-in gate, so polling is what actually keeps the surface fresh
description:
`experience-collaboration.v1` Core 6 asks for webhooks where the host offers them and polling as the honest fallback. Lane w8-collab-bridge built both: `POST /api/collab/webhooks/host` records an arrival and flips the surface's freshness sentence from "Polling - checked every 60 seconds..." to "Webhook - the host called this app at <stamp>...". It checks a shared secret read from `~/.amplifier/converge-app.webhook-secret` (`CONVERGE_COLLAB_SECRET_FILE` overrides), refuses 403 without it, and refuses 503 when no secret file exists rather than trusting the caller.

What it cannot do is be called by a real host. `app/serve.py`'s gate is a middleware over everything except `PUBLIC_PREFIXES` (`/login`, `/static/`, `/branding/`, `/favicon`, `/manifest.webmanifest`, `/sw.js`, `/healthz`), with no loopback exemption by design. A GitHub webhook carries no `cv_session` cookie, so it answers 401 and never reaches the route. Measured on 127.0.0.1:8846, 2026-09-04: with a cookie the route works end to end and freshness flips; without one the gate answers first.

So today the freshness that actually runs is polling, every 60 seconds, from `app/static/js/render/collab.js`. That is a kept clause rather than a broken one — Core 6 names polling as the honest fallback and the surface says which mechanism is carrying it — but the preferred half is unreachable, and this is where the remaining work is.

The change (`app/serve.py`, outside lane w8-collab-bridge's ownership): add `collab.WEBHOOK_PATH` to the public paths, and nothing else. The route's own shared-secret check is what stands in for the cookie — it must not be relaxed at the same time, or the app would gain an unauthenticated write.

Two things worth deciding at the same time, and both are steward-shaped rather than obvious:
- whether the secret should be an HMAC over the body (what GitHub actually sends, as `X-Hub-Signature-256`) rather than the plain shared header this ships with;
- whether the app is reachable from the host at all, which is a deployment question this repository has not answered anywhere.
acceptance: GIVEN the app is running and the webhook path is public WHEN a request carrying the shared secret but no session cookie POSTs to `/api/collab/webhooks/host` THEN it is accepted and the freshness sentence names the webhook; AND WHEN the same request carries a wrong secret or none THEN it is refused, and no other route has become reachable without a cookie.

title: work_file accepts a description carrying its own tool-call markup, so a malformed model emission lands in the queue verbatim
description:
Contract: documents.v1 Core 9 ("A work item names its contract in one line, defines done in plain words") — the filing-end half of converge-68f5, which migrated the damaged items but could not fix the cause from this repository.

CAUSE, MEASURED. converge-68f5 named three candidate causes (the filing tool, the provider's tool-call serialization, or the agent composing the call) and asked whoever took it to decide which. Read from this host's own session log on 2026-09-04 — lane w8-priority-write, session e5c8afa1-9f96-4280-abfd-a0ae11dacf7a, events.jsonl lines 1055 (llm:response) and 1060 (tool:pre), the call that created converge-t6fp:

    line 1055  .data.raw.content[1].input.description  len=1903  leak=True
        "...the queue number is the manager session's to set.</description>
         <parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN a steward raises an item's priority..."
    line 1060  .data.tool_input                        ["description", "title"]
    line 1060  .data.tool_input.description            len=1899  leak=True  (same text)

Two things settle it. The markup is already present in the RAW provider payload (`llm:response`), before any Amplifier code touches the call — so neither the filing tool nor the tracker introduced it. And `tool_input` carries only `description` and `title`: there is no `acceptance` argument at all, which is why the field is empty rather than wrong.

So the model emitted its tool call in the textual `<parameter name="...">` form and closed the description with a tag named for the FIELD rather than the closing tag the form uses; the provider's serializer folded everything after it into the `description` string and produced no `acceptance` argument. The agent composing the call is where it goes wrong; the provider's recovery is what makes it silent. Neither is in this repository.

STILL LIVE, NOT HISTORICAL. converge-68f5 counted twenty-one damaged items and warned that a twenty-second would mean the cause was not found. Three more appeared while it sat open — converge-f9ac (13:31), converge-t6fp (13:31), converge-jpks (13:46), all filed 2026-09-04 by the same agent, all after 68f5 was filed at 13:17. All twenty-four are migrated now. The twenty-fifth is a matter of time.

WHAT WOULD STOP IT, and where. `work_file` / `work_add` in amplifier-work-tracker accept any string as a description. A description that contains a closing description tag or a parameter-name tag is never something a person wrote — it is always this defect. The tracker can refuse it (loudly, naming the malformation) or split it at the marker and fill `acceptance` itself. Refusing is the better half: the filing agent is still alive at that moment and can re-file correctly, whereas splitting guesses.

Filed rather than fixed: this lane owns docs/work-items.json, app/static/dev/stub_server.py, conformance/experience-direction/** and evaluations/turnkey/** — amplifier-work-tracker is a different repository, and AGENTS.md rule 5 says write the fact down for its owner rather than reach.
acceptance: GIVEN a work_file or work_add call whose description contains a closing description tag or a parameter-name tag WHEN the call is made THEN the tracker refuses it, naming the malformation and the field it belongs in, and no item is created — AND a fresh export of the converge queue scanned for those tags reports zero, as it does today. Falsified by a twenty-fifth item appearing with the same shape, which would mean the guard was placed somewhere the filing path does not reach.

title: Core 9 has still never seen a real stall on this host: the fixture proves the reading, not the habit
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §Core 9 ("Stalls are decisions, not loops"). Ledger row CVG-019. Discovered from converge-3rzz, the post-merge reconcile that re-derived the row after converge-wb0's stall fixture landed.

WHAT MOVED, AND WHAT DID NOT. converge-wb0 built `evaluations/turnkey/fixtures/stall_wave.py`, which seeds a wave whose second lane really stops with an unchanged branch. Re-run live on 2026-09-04 by this reconcile, against both variants, the reading now answers in both directions:

    PASS - 1 lane(s) stopped with an unchanged branch and each is named in a
    record that says it stopped - lumen-index: 'cycle 2: lumen-index is stuck and
    is not being relaunched.'; this reads that the stop was written down, not
    whether the cause it gives is the real one.

    FAIL - 1 lane(s) stopped with an unchanged branch and were not declared
    stuck: lumen-index - named, but no record says the lane stopped; the newest
    one naming lumen-index reads "cycle 1: launched lumen-units and lumen-index
    at width 2, ...", which is a mention and not a declaration.

So the instrument is finished. What is still missing is the observation. Run against THIS host's own manager workspace on the same day, the reading says:

    Core 9 (CVG-019) SKIP: no lane ended without commits, so no stall exists for
    this reading to judge - the reading ran and found nothing.

Every wave on this host has produced commits. A fixture proves the reading can tell a declared stall from an undeclared one; it says nothing about whether a manager session HERE declares its own. That observation lands the first time a real lane on this host ends with an unchanged branch, and the reading is now able to say which way it went.

WHAT A PASS ON THE FIXTURE STILL WOULD NOT PROVE, carried forward from converge-wb0 so it is not lost: not that the cause a record gives is the real or an adequate one (the reading shows the words; a reader judges them); not that the lane had not already been retried, because clause 9's "across iterations" needs a count of attempts and nothing on disk records one.

CVG-019 now pins the live SKIP through `ledger/checks/turnkey_clause.py`, not the frozen step block in RESULT.md, so the row goes red the day this host's own wave produces a stall - which is exactly the event that would close this item.

---

MEASURED 2026-09-04 by lane w9-queue-and-kits, which took this item and could not close it. The event has still not happened; here is where it stands and what changed while looking.

THE READING, TAKEN LIVE TODAY against this host's own manager workspace, still declines:

    Core 9 (CVG-019) SKIP: no lane ended without commits, so no stall exists for
    this reading to judge - the reading ran and found nothing

That is CORRECT, and it was checked rather than trusted. One lane on this host does have an unchanged branch right now - w9-adopter, branch lane/w9-adopter, base be593315, 0 commits - but its terminal session hw__hw-converge__w9-adopter is LIVE, and a lane still running on an unchanged branch is working, not stalled. This lane polled for it to end, in a bounded wait of 840s, and it was still running at the end of that wait. So the GIVEN is unmet, not evaded.

WHAT DID CHANGE, and why it matters to whoever closes this. The SKIP's sentence was reporting more than it had looked at. `commits_beyond` answers None for a lane whose worktree is gone AND whose branch no reachable checkout still holds - the normal end state of a merged lane - and such a lane was dropped in silence. Counted honestly, on this host:

    read 1 of 107 lane(s) in the manifest; 103 could not be read at all
    (worktree gone and branch not in any checkout reachable from here)

One of a hundred and seven. "The reading ran and found nothing" was a claim about the whole manifest; it was a claim about a single lane. The reading now says which it means (`lanes_read`, `lanes_in_manifest`, `lanes_unreadable`, and up to twenty named), pinned by three tests in evaluations/turnkey/tests/test_turnkey.py. The verdict is unchanged - no stall is visible - but a future SKIP can no longer be read as a survey of the wave.

WHAT IS STILL OWED, for whoever holds this when the event lands:
  * take the reading: `uv run evaluations/turnkey/run.py --env local --json-only --steps j --workspace <manager workspace>`, and read the CVG-019 entry;
  * re-derive CVG-019 in `ledger/rows.yaml` from that live reading, quoting it - `ledger/**` was not in this lane's ownership;

title: The composition kit's two live rules still decline — nothing asserts helper reachability or the neighbour promise
description:
Contract: composition.v1 — Core 3 ("Its own helpers carry a small local rulebook … and borrow nothing else", judged live) and Core 6 ("Nothing touches the tools of other work in your session", judged live), and the contract's own "Conformance kit asserts" bullets 2 and 3.

    uv run conformance/composition/run.py . --json-only
      session_reaches_helpers        SKIP  "needs a live Amplifier session; this kit reads files only"
      unrelated_session_keeps_tools  SKIP  "needs two live Amplifier sessions (Converge plus unrelated work) side by side"

The kit's own self-test pins the declining set to exactly {2, 3}, so a rule cannot quietly drift into declining to dodge a failure. But a pinned decline is still an unasserted promise, and both of these promises are the ones that matter most: the second is the measurement that produced the PINS.md rule "Never reintroduce a session-wide spawn: block", taken once by hand on 2026-09-02 and re-taken by nothing since.

These two rows (CVG-008, CVG-009) named converge-qtp — the turnkey harness — as their fix, on the composition kit README's own reasoning that closing them "needs the live harness, not a cleverer file scan". converge-qtp is finished and its harness is green, and it does neither: its nine steps stand up an environment, install once, run the install check, start a project, derive work, run two lanes, integrate, re-check and brief. None of them asks whether a Converge session reaches a helper, and none stands a second unrelated session beside it.

So the fix these rows wait on is not the turnkey. It is either an extension of the turnkey (it already stands up a fresh container and installs into it — reaching a helper from inside is a small addition; a second session beside it is a larger one), or a separate two-session evaluation.

Discovered while re-deriving fifteen ledger rows for converge-0gb.

title: Nothing records a return, so operation.v1 Core 10's "a brief on every return" cannot be asserted
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §10 — "**A brief on every return.** Time away · finished · stuck · needs you · anything quietly broken — in sentences, appended to a log the steward can read."

Half of this clause is now kept and measurable: `docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md` exists and carries nine dated briefs (measured 2026-09-04 by ledger row CVG-020's probe, `MODE-ENCODES-CLAUSE-10-LOG-EXISTS-BRIEFS=9`), and `modes/converge-manager.md` encodes the clause.

The other half is unassertable, and not for want of a probe. Nothing anywhere records that a RETURN happened — so no check can compare briefs to returns, and a count of briefs can never say whether one exists per return. Nine briefs against an unknown number of returns is a number without a denominator.

Two honest ways to close it, for whoever takes it:

1. Record the returns. If a return leaves a trace the steward's tooling can count (a line in the highway log, a session marker, a timestamped entry the manager session appends on wake), then the ratio becomes checkable and CVG-020 gets a probe that asserts the clause instead of half of it.
2. Decide the clause means the log, not the ratio. If "a brief on every return" is satisfied by the manager session's standing instruction rather than by a countable pairing, that is a reading the steward can ratify — and CVG-020 then re-derives to CONFORMS against the mode file plus the log, with the ratio recorded as out of scope.

Filed because CVG-020's `work` ref pointed at converge-qtp, which is RESOLVED — the turnkey harness landed. This ledger's own rule is that a closed item may not stay cited as the thing that will fix a red row, and the row needed a live item to cite. Discovered while reconciling after wave 7 (converge-nf4).

Not fixed here: that lane owns `ledger/**` only. The subjects are the mode file, the return log, and whatever would record a return.
acceptance:
GIVEN the repository WHEN operation.v1 Core 10 is checked THEN either a probe compares briefs in docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md against a countable record of returns and finds one brief per return — or the steward has ratified, in writing, that the clause is kept by the mode's standing instruction plus the log, and ledger row CVG-020 carries that reading with a probe that asserts it.

Ledger rows this closes: CVG-020. Grouped by cause and component on 2026-09-04 by `docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md`, which is where the whole mapping of rows to items is printed. The rows already named this item as their fix; what was missing was the list, written down here.

title: The direction kit's restore rule passed for the whole time converge-4pq was open
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 §6; conformance/README.md's promise that a check which cannot run says so rather than passing.

`conformance/experience-direction/run.py` rule 6, `restore_is_a_real_action`, reports:

    [PASS] 6  restore_is_a_real_action: restore reaches a write the app declares;
              on a locked document that write is the proposal path

§6 asks for more than that: "Restore a wording, a paragraph, a section, or the whole document." Restoring FROM somewhere is the whole point of restoring from *history*, and the kit never asks which snapshot the write can reach. So it passed, unchanged, through the entire life of converge-4pq — a period in which the app could reach exactly one snapshot out of however many the History view showed, and said so on the screen in its own words.

Measured on lane w8-direction-restore, 2026-09-04, running the kit against two live servers built from two trees — one before converge-4pq, one after:

    port 8792 (tree at f10c278, before)  VERDICT: PASS (pass=12 fail=0 skip=0)
    port 8791 (tree at 039e56d, after)   VERDICT: PASS (pass=12 fail=0 skip=0)

Identical, rule for rule, including rule 6's sentence. The kit could not tell the two apart. A conformance kit that reads the same on both sides of the work it is supposed to be judging is not measuring that clause.

This is a real limit rather than a bug: the kit is a static read of what the app served (its route table and client assets), and it launches no browser. It cannot drive a restore. What it CAN do is read the route table it already reads, and notice that the restore write takes an optional snapshot parameter — or say "Can't check" for the part it cannot reach, which conformance/README.md asks for and which is more useful than a PASS that means less than it looks like.

Filed rather than fixed: `conformance/**` is not in lane w8-direction-restore's ownership.

Suggested shape, for whoever takes it: split rule 6 the way rule 2 is already split into 2a/2b — 6a for "restore reaches a write, and on a locked document that write is the proposal path" (what the static read genuinely proves today), and 6b for "that write can name a snapshot other than the reader's own position", judged from the route table, or reported Can't check.
acceptance: GIVEN the experience-direction kit run against a build where restore can reach only one snapshot AND against one where it can reach any snapshot in the document's history WHEN both reports are compared THEN they differ on the restore rule, EITHER by failing on the first OR by reporting Can't check for the part the kit cannot reach.

description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 10 — "**A brief on every return.** Time away · finished · stuck · needs you · anything quietly broken — in sentences, appended to a log the steward can read."

converge-823 built the recording half: `modes/converge-manager.md` clause 10 now makes the manager session stamp the return in the entry heading the moment the steward's message arrives, and write the five parts under it at the end of the turn. converge-4xg (this lane) built the counting half: ledger row CVG-020's probe is now `ledger/checks/return_log_ratio.py`, which imports the turnkey harness's own `parse_return_log` and reports stamped returns against briefed returns.

2. The steward ratifies, in writing, that the clause is kept by the mode's standing instruction plus the log rather than by a countable pairing. CVG-020 then re-derives to CONFORMS against the mode file and the log, with the ratio recorded as out of scope.

The honest limit, recorded so nobody re-discovers it: a return the manager session never recorded at all leaves no trace on either side of the ratio. Closing that would need a record of returns kept by something other than the session that returns.

Filed because CVG-020's `work` ref pointed at converge-823, which is now RESOLVED, and this ledger's own rule (enforced by `ledger/checks/verify.py`) is that a red row may not cite a closed item as the thing that will fix it.

title: A stale editable install let the manager session's own re-run check pass against a deleted worktree
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 7 — "Done means the manager session re-ran the check ... and — where the item lives in an installed system — the installed thing showing the change."

Caught by the adopter harness run of 2026-09-06T03:50:03Z, scenario 1 (`evaluations/adopter/RESULT.md`, container adopter-20260906035003-s1). That scenario is GREEN; this was found inside it, by the AI user, after the manager session had already reported done.

What happened. A worker lane built the project in an isolated worktree and ran `pip install -e` there, which binds the installed package to that worktree's path. The manager session merged to main and re-ran the check itself, as Core 7 requires — and it passed, because the import was still resolving through the stale editable binding to the lane's worktree, not to main. The manager then cleaned up the worktree. Main was left with a broken install and a failing check, and the re-run that was supposed to catch exactly that had already said done.

The failure is quiet and it defeats the one guard against a worker's self-report. Re-running the check is worthless if the thing under test is not the thing that was merged; here the manager ran the right command in the right repository and still measured the wrong code. It only surfaced because the person watching ran the check themselves from a clean shell.

To the session's credit, once told, it owned the cause plainly, reinstalled from main, re-verified for real, and appended an honest correction rather than rewriting its earlier claim. The discipline held. The check did not.

What fixed looks like: a manager session's post-merge re-run proves it is testing the merged tree — the installed thing resolves to the repository it just merged into, not to any worktree — and a worktree is never removed while something still resolves through it.
acceptance: Given a lane that installed its work editable in its own worktree, when the manager session re-runs the check after merging, then the re-run resolves the installed thing to the merged repository and fails loud if it resolves anywhere else. Given the worktree is then removed, when the check is re-run from a clean shell, then it still passes.

title: CVG-046 goes red on main: the two new experience kits make it 7 of 7 aligned, and the row pins 5
description:
Contract: documents.v1 Core 5 ("The kit's rule table is numbered to these Core clause numbers, so a failing rule names the clause it breaks"). Ledger row CVG-046.

Measured in a scratch merge rather than guessed. lane/w8-step-regex merged into main at 1841b1b in a throwaway worktree, then the gate run there:

    uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py
      - CVG-046 expect NOT met (exit=0, stdout='KITS-ALL-NUMBERED-TO-CORE-CLAUSES=7')

The row expects `KITS-ALL-NUMBERED-TO-CORE-CLAUSES=5`. converge-f1l landed kits for experience.v1 and experience-collaboration.v1 (commits a693bcf, 5ae3d4e, 338b2e7), so there are seven kits now and all seven are aligned — the probe prints a count only when every kit is aligned, so 7 is the good answer, not the bad one.

This is drift TOWARD spec, and the row anticipated it in its own notes: "it goes red if any kit drifts, and it goes red if a sixth kit lands unaligned, which is the case that matters now that the experience family has three kits of its own."

Why it was filed rather than fixed by the lane that found it: ledger/ was lane w8-step-regex's file ownership, but that lane's tree has five kits, not seven. A row re-derived to pin 7 there would be red in that tree and green only after the merge — the same reasoning LEDGER-FORMAT and this ledger's own header apply to a SYNC pin: a lane whose tree holds the old bytes cannot honestly pin the new ones. It needs a tree that already has both kits.

Two things to check while re-deriving, not just the number: that all seven really are `aligned: True` (read documents kit rule 5b's own `observed` list, do not take the count on trust), and that the row's notes name which seven, as they name the five today.

title: The lock control's failure toast still says the app answers no lock route
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 §11 (the lock control) — and AGENTS.md §5, "never claim a result you did not observe", which cuts both ways: a screen may not claim a cause it did not observe either.

`app/static/js/actions.js`'s `sendLock()` catch reads:

    toast(`Nothing was locked — this app answers no lock route yet (${err.message}). Filed as converge-eci.`)

That was true while converge-eci was open. It is not true now: `POST /api/managers/{mid}/docs/{repo}/{doc}/lock` is answered by `app/serve.py` and written by `writes.lock_document()`, and the route refuses in plain words for real reasons — the document already carries a locking word, fewer than four conditions arrived, the document has uncommitted changes, it has no H1. Every one of those now reaches the steward under the wrong cause: they are told the app answers no lock route, when in fact it answered and refused, and it told them exactly why in `err.message`.

`app/static/js/actions.js` was outside this lane's ownership (writes.py, serve.py, api.js, render/direction.js, tests), which is why this is filed rather than fixed.

The fix is the catch body only — the success path is already correct and was measured working end to end. Something like: `toast(\`Nothing was locked — ${err.message}\`)`, so the server's own sentence is what the steward reads.
acceptance: GIVEN a document that already carries a locking word WHEN the steward forces the lock control THEN the toast carries the server's own refusal naming that word, AND it does not say the app answers no lock route; AND a successful lock still reports the document locked.

title: app/tests/test_tmux_send_keys.py stomps a parallel lane: fixed tmux socket 'cvsend' plus kill-server
description:
Contract: operation.v1 (a check that cannot run says so, rather than reporting a failure someone else caused).

This is the twin of converge-bdc / converge-791, in a file lane w8-tests-isolation did not own and so did not touch. Those two items fixed `app/tests/test_tmux_view.py` and `app/tests/test_tmux_rendered.py`, which now take a per-run socket (`cvtest-<pid>-<random>`, `cvrender-<pid>-<random>`). `app/tests/test_tmux_send_keys.py` still opens its server on the fixed, machine-wide socket `cvsend` (line 44) with fixed session names (typist, closer, shortest, bulk, router) and a module fixture that begins and ends with `tmux -L cvsend kill-server` (lines 71, 81).

Measured 2026-09-04, after the other two files were fixed. Two `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests` runs started 0.5s apart on one machine:

  run A: 6 failed, 144 passed, 88 skipped  — all 6 in test_tmux_send_keys.py
  run B: 12 errors, 138 passed, 88 skipped — all 12 in test_tmux_send_keys.py
  failures in test_tmux_view.py or test_tmux_rendered.py, either run: 0

So the whole-suite verdict is still unreliable while another lane is testing, and it still points the losing lane at a file it never touched — just now at one file instead of three.

Fix, matching what the two sibling files already do:
1. `SOCKET = f"cvsend-{os.getpid()}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"` at module import (needs `import os`, `import uuid`). The convention and the measurement behind it are written down in `app/tests/conftest.py`, whose session-scoped reaper already kills and unlinks any socket carrying this run's pid — so nothing further is needed for cleanup.
2. Replace the `kill-server` at fixture setup with a refusal: if `tmux -L <socket> ls` succeeds, `pytest.fail` naming the sessions found, rather than killing a server this run did not start.
3. Wrap the session creation and the `yield` in `try/finally` so a `check=True` failure cannot skip the teardown.
4. Update the module docstring (lines 9-10), which currently states the socket is `cvsend`.
acceptance: GIVEN two `pytest -q app/tests` runs started at the same time on one machine WHEN both complete THEN neither reports any failure or error in app/tests/test_tmux_send_keys.py, and neither kills the other's tmux sessions.

title: A lane cannot close its own infra ledger rows: the tool the error message names does not exist on this host
description:
Contract: operation.v1 (a wave leaves its host as it found it). Found 2026-09-04 by lane w9-queue-and-kits while tearing down the one server it had registered.

The lane registered its dev stub as the ledger asks:

    infra_ledger.sh <workspace> add server w9-stub-8799 "kill 2123521"
    ADDED: type=server id=w9-stub-8799 status=open destroy='kill 2123521'

It then stopped the server and confirmed it was gone (`kill -0` reports both pids gone; port 8799 free). But there is no verb to mark the row closed:

    $ infra_ledger.sh <workspace> done server w9-stub-8799
    ERROR: unknown command 'done' (want: add|list|sweep)

    $ infra_ledger.sh <workspace> sweep
    sweep is the MANAGER's batch-close verb and destroys EVERY open row.
    A lane tearing down its OWN rows must use the lane-scoped tool:
      .amplifier/evaluation/tools/lane_teardown.sh <workspace> <lane> teardown --yes

That path does not exist:

    $ ls /home/bkrabach/dev/hw-converge/.amplifier/evaluation/tools/lane_teardown.sh
    (no such file)
    $ find /home/bkrabach/dev/hw-converge -maxdepth 5 -name lane_teardown.sh   -> nothing
    $ find ~/.local/share/uv/tools/amplifier -name lane_teardown.sh            -> nothing

So the only verb a lane can reach is the one it is explicitly told not to use, because it would destroy every other live lane's rows as well. The two rows stay `open` against dead processes.

The cost is quiet and cumulative: infra.tsv already carries a long tail of `<unattributed:...>` open rows for servers that are long dead — visible in the sweep output — so the ledger reads as though this host is holding far more than it is, and a manager closing a batch cannot tell a leaked server from a stale row.

Either ship the lane-scoped tool the message names, or give `infra_ledger.sh` a row-scoped close verb (`done <type> <id>`) that refuses when the destroy command's process is still alive — so closing a row is evidence the thing is actually gone, not just a claim.
acceptance: GIVEN a lane that registered an infra row and has since stopped the process WHEN it runs the lane-scoped close the error message names THEN that row alone is marked closed, no other lane's open rows are touched, and the close refuses if the registered destroy command's process is still alive — checked with one live row and one dead one in the same ledger.

title: docs/work-items.json is stale, so the ledger's closed-cite tripwire is blind to converge-f1l
description:
Contract: documents.v1 (the kit's rule 9a reads the work queue through this export).

`ledger/checks/verify.py` carries a tripwire added by converge-0gb: no GAP/VIOLATION row may cite a work item that is already resolved, because "a reader who follows a closed cite lands on finished work and learns nothing about what would close the row". It reads `docs/work-items.json`, and an id absent from that export is reported as INFO rather than failed, on the stated ground that the export is a snapshot and a row may legitimately cite an item filed after it was taken.

That reasoning is sound and the export has now drifted far enough to defeat the tripwire in the other direction. Measured 2026-09-04 in this worktree:

  $ git log -1 --format=%ci -- docs/work-items.json
  2026-09-03 23:51:43 -0700
  $ python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/work-items.json')); print(len(d))"
  76
  converge-f1l -> "open" in the export; RESOLVED in the live queue since
                  2026-09-04T10:56:59Z

So for a whole day the five rows citing converge-f1l (CVG-104, 107, 108, 112, 113) named a resolved item as their fix, and the tripwire built to catch exactly that reported OK — because the export still said the item was open. It answered from a stale snapshot with full confidence. That is the same failure shape converge-0gb was filed for, one layer down.

converge-5yu has now moved all five rows off converge-f1l, so the immediate lie is gone. The blind spot is not: nothing refreshes the export, and nothing says how old it is.

Also measured, and the smaller half of this: the export predates every item filed on 2026-09-04, so 15 red rows now cite ids absent from it (was 7 before this pass — converge-9mq, converge-er6 and converge-scb are all newer than the snapshot). Those are correctly reported as INFO. They are noise rather than error, but they are 15 rows the tripwire is not actually checking.

Two things would fix it, and they are separable:

1. Refresh the export — `uv run scripts/export-work-items.py --project converge --out docs/work-items.json`. A one-command fix that lasts until the next item is filed.
2. Make the staleness visible rather than silent — have verify.py print the export's own age beside the closed-cite verdict, so "no red row cites a resolved work item" is never read as stronger than the snapshot it was computed from. A check that quietly covers less than it says is worse than one that is absent; that sentence is already in verify.py's own comments, about a different tripwire.

Filed rather than made: `docs/` and `ledger/checks/verify.py`'s behaviour beyond the rows were outside this lane's file ownership (converge-5yu owns `ledger/**` only, and this is a `docs/` refresh plus a checker change).
acceptance: GIVEN docs/work-items.json is the snapshot ledger/checks/verify.py reads WHEN `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` runs THEN the export reflects the live queue's statuses (converge-f1l reads resolved, and every item filed to date is present) AND the closed-cite verdict is printed together with the export's own age, so a reader can see how far the check can actually see.

title: Four offline/service-worker app tests fail on main, and they are not this lane's doing
description:
Contract: platform-web.v1 — the browser body must be honest about the one thing a web page cannot do, keep working while it is not running. These four checks are the ones that hold it to that, and four of them are red.

Measured 2026-09-06 on lane w14-run-the-app AND, as a control, on a clean detached worktree of main at 0fee668 with none of that lane's changes present. Identical result both times, so it is not that lane's doing:

    FAILED app/tests/test_direction_polish.py::test_offline_a_stored_document_carries_its_own_sync_moment[1280-800]
    FAILED app/tests/test_direction_polish.py::test_offline_a_stored_document_carries_its_own_sync_moment[390-844]
    FAILED app/tests/test_direction_polish.py::test_back_online_the_document_stops_claiming_it_is_a_stored_copy
    FAILED app/tests/test_web_polish.py::test_without_presence_js_in_the_cache_the_direction_surface_dies_offline
    4 failed, 19 passed (clean worktree of 0fee668)
    4 failed, 464 passed (whole app suite, same tree plus w14-run-the-app's changes)

They only run where Playwright and its Chromium are installed, which is why a green-looking suite elsewhere does not see them.

The fourth one is a tripwire on another test rather than a defect in the app, and it says so itself:

    assert not rendered["managerName"], (
      "the app came up offline without presence.js in the cache, so precaching
       it is not what the acceptance turns on and the test above proves less
       than it claims: {'managerName': 'Manager alpha', 'sections': 11}")

So one of two things is true and it is a judgment, not a typo: either the surface no longer depends on presence.js being precached (in which case the test above it is asserting something that no longer carries the acceptance, and both should be rewritten to name what actually does), or the eviction the test performs no longer evicts what it thinks it does.

The other three are about a stored copy naming its own sync moment. They need the same reading — whether the behaviour moved, or the check did.

Files: app/tests/test_direction_polish.py, app/tests/test_web_polish.py, and whichever of app/static/sw.js and the presence/offline JS they read. None of them was in lane w14-run-the-app's ownership.
acceptance: GIVEN a checkout with Playwright and its Chromium installed WHEN `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx --with playwright pytest -q app/tests/test_direction_polish.py app/tests/test_web_polish.py` runs THEN it reports 0 failed; AND each of the four checks asserts the offline behaviour that actually ships, rather than one that was replaced — for the presence.js one, either the surface genuinely dies offline without it in the cache, or both that test and the one it guards name what the acceptance really turns on.

title: Offline: the service worker precache list does not carry app/static/js/presence.js
description:
Contract: platform-web.v1 Core 10 (offline it reads what it last synced) — a browser that installs the service worker and goes offline before ever fetching presence.js cannot read the Direction surface at all.

`app/static/sw.js` is another lane's file, so this lane could not change it.

converge-wmh added `app/static/js/presence.js`, imported by `app/static/js/render/direction.js`. `PRECACHE` in `app/static/sw.js` lists every other client module by hand (`main.js`, `state.js`, `api.js`, `refresh.js`, `actions.js`, `offline.js`, and the four `render/*.js`) and does not list this one.

In practice the app is fine: `/static/*` is cache-first with runtime caching, so presence.js lands in the STATIC cache the first time it is fetched online, and `app/tests/test_offline.py` passes unchanged (verified 2026-09-04, 226 passed). The gap is the cold case the precache list exists for: a browser that installs the worker and goes offline before ever fetching presence.js would fail to import it, and direction.js would fail with it — taking the whole Direction surface down offline, not just presence.

Fix: add `'/static/js/presence.js'` to `PRECACHE` in `app/static/sw.js` (and consider whether the list should be derived rather than hand-kept, since this is the second module to be added since it was written).

Also noticed, same lane, same reason (not this lane's file): `app/tests/test_direction_writes_rendered.py`'s module docstring still says "Presence is this browser's own (converge-wmh). There is no channel that carries a second steward, so nothing here claims one." The first sentence is now false — the channel exists and `app/tests/test_presence.py` drives it across two browser contexts. The test body is unaffected and still passes.
acceptance: GIVEN a browser that has installed the service worker and never fetched /static/js/presence.js WHEN it goes offline and opens the app THEN the Direction surface renders, because presence.js was precached alongside every other client module.

title: The owner return log's 2026-09-06 entry carries no time away, and CVG-020 is red on it
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 10 — a return brief tells the steward what happened while they were away.

Measured on lane/w19-tidy, 2026-09-06:

    $ uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py; echo "exit=$?"
    ...
    FAILURES:

title: The app names no manager-session operation for any write, and states no limit for the two things it cannot do
description:
Contract: experience.v1 Core 8 (whatever you can do here, the manager session can do too) and Core 14 (where a body genuinely cannot do a thing, it says so in the app).

Two umbrella clauses about what the app *says*, both measured 2026-09-04 against the app at 127.0.0.1:8823 by `conformance/experience/run.py`. Both are the app's own surface to fix, and neither is this lane's file to touch.

**Core 8 — "Whatever you can do here, the manager session can do too."** Every write is meant to name the manager-session operation that does the same thing, so nothing the project needs is reachable only by a person at a screen. Rule 8 FAILs: this body offers four of the five writes (answer with a word · drop feedback · steer · ask for a proposal) and publishes no operation for any of them — no `data-manager-operation` attribute, no operations table in the client, no sentence naming one anywhere it serves. A reader cannot check the claim at all. (CVG-107 recorded the same gap from a hand-written probe; the superseded surface kit found the old app published this behind a Details fold, and the app that shipped does not.)

**Core 14 — "Where a body genuinely cannot do a thing, it says so in the app."** Rule 14 FAILs on two absences: there is no route for *raise or lower a priority*, and feedback is offered as text and as a screenshot but not as voice. The app says nothing anywhere about either — not what the limit is, not what to do instead. Silence is the only wrong answer the clause names.

The app already does this well elsewhere, which is why the rule can tell the difference: `render/direction.js` carries Details folds saying presence is this browser only and that restoring past the read point is not offered, each naming the item that would change it. The two absences above have no such sentence.

The priority write itself is a separate gap (Core 4, CVG-103, converge-6cc); this item is about the app being silent on it, not about building it.
acceptance: GIVEN the app is running WHEN `uv run conformance/experience/run.py <app>` is run THEN rule 8 PASSes — every write the body offers names the manager-session operation that does the same thing — AND rule 14 PASSes: for each thing the body cannot do, the app states the limit and what to do instead.

title: Rule 8a: no manager session names a steward — one field on the registration, in config.py and data.py
description:
`experience-collaboration.v1` Core 8 says whose word counts is settled when the manager session is registered, not inferred from whoever is signed in. `conformance/experience-collaboration/run.py` rule 8a reads `/api/boot` and looks for a key matching /steward/i on each manager. Measured live on 2026-09-04 against the app on 127.0.0.1:8846 with the collab router mounted: 8a is the only FAIL left in the kit (pass=11 fail=1 skip=2), reading "no manager session names a steward, so whose word counts is inferred from whoever is looking (this target answers as 'bkrabach')".

Lane w8-collab-bridge could not make this change: `app/config.py` and `app/data.py` are outside its file ownership. What it did instead is make the field the whole of the remaining work — `app/collab.py`'s `steward_of(mc)` already reads `getattr(mc, "steward", "")` and never falls back to the reader, and `app/tests/test_collab.py::test_one_steward_per_session_needs_one_field_on_the_registration` runs the contract's own kit over a boot payload carrying `steward` and shows 8a PASSing.

The change, in three places:

1. `app/config.py`, `ManagerConfig`: add `steward: str = ""`.
2. `app/config.py`, `_manager_from_table`: add `steward=str(table.get("steward") or "").strip(),`.
3. `app/data.py`, `manager_payload`: add `"steward": mc.steward,` to the returned dict.

Then one `steward = "<name>"` line per `[[managers]]` block in `~/.amplifier/converge-app.toml`, and a sentence in `app/README.md`'s "What it watches" paragraph naming the new key.

A manager block with no `steward` should keep answering with an empty string rather than guessing — an unregistered steward is a registration that has not been finished, and Core 8 is precisely about not inferring it.
acceptance: GIVEN a `[[managers]]` block carrying `steward = "wren"` WHEN `uv run conformance/experience-collaboration/run.py <app>` is run THEN rule 8a PASSes, reading that the manager session names exactly one steward settled at registration; AND GIVEN a block with no `steward` key THEN `/api/boot` answers with an empty steward rather than the signed-in reader's name.

title: CONTRACTS-README's index says ten experience-family contracts are 'Not yet written' — all ten exist

title: The first check-record entry and the first stamped call on this host — clauses 7, 8 and 11 go from unread to a verdict
description:
Contract: operation.v1 — Core 3, 7, 8, 11. Ledger rows CVG-017, CVG-018, CVG-021.

converge-blg and converge-5vz wrote down two conventions and taught them in `modes/converge-manager.md` (clauses 3, 8, 11) and `context/manager/wave-record.md`. Nothing on this host has followed them yet, because a lane cannot: both are the manager session's own to write.

1. **The check record.** After integrating a wave and re-running the check, append an entry to `docs/workflow/CHECK-RECORD.md` — the merges it covers, the command run, what it printed — and commit it on the integration branch in the manager session's own commit. Step (k) then reads the commit that introduced that entry and answers who verified. Today it says: "the record the manager session writes itself (docs/workflow/CHECK-RECORD.md) is not in this repository yet".

2. **The call stamp.** `- <ISO> CALL <ratify | irreversible | human check | priority> - <what is asked>. Parked: <items>. Continued: <what kept moving>.` in the plan record, at the moment of the call. Two of the four calls currently in HIGHWAY.md name which kind they are; the other two name none, which is why Core 11 is SKIP rather than a verdict.

Neither is new work in substance — clause 8 already says the verification is the manager session's own, and clause 11 already says exactly four calls reach the steward. What was missing was any trace afterwards, for somebody who was not in the session.

Verify with: `uv run evaluations/turnkey/run.py --env local --steps j,k --workspace ~/dev/hw-converge --repo <the integration checkout> --project converge`
acceptance: GIVEN a wave integrated on this host after the conventions landed WHEN turnkey steps (j) and (k) are re-run against this workspace THEN Core 7 and Core 8 carry a verdict on who re-ran the check, naming the commit that added the newest CHECK-RECORD entry; AND Core 11 either passes or names exactly how many recorded calls still say nothing about which of the four they are; AND `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` exits 0.

title: A lane merge reported carrying files it did not carry, and the lane branch was reset over the evidence
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §8 (integrate, verify, re-check — the manager session's own verification), with §7 (done requires commits beyond base and evidence on disk).

On 2026-09-04 lane w9-adopter committed 19 files for converge-4jva (commit 823ff7e, parent be59331): the onboarding audit, evaluations/adopter/** — harness, profile, scenarios, fixtures, RESULT.md — and the work-items export. Integration commit 09c83ef is titled "merge lane/w9-adopter: onboarding audit + adopter harness (converge-4jva); work-item export regenerated" and carries exactly one file: docs/work-items.json. The other 18 were dropped. lane/w9-adopter was then reset to 09c83ef, so the lane commit became unreachable from every live ref and only `git fsck` could still find it. The item was resolved describing artifacts that were, from that moment, in no branch.

Nothing caught it. The merge message asserted the contents; no step compared the message against the diff, and no step compared the merged tree against the acceptance clause naming the paths ("GIVEN git diff --stat THEN only docs/workflow/ONBOARDING-AUDIT-2026-09-04.md, evaluations/adopter/** and docs/work-items.json changed"). A resolution was accepted while `git diff --stat main..HEAD` was empty — the §7 "marker on an unchanged branch is stuck" condition, met and unnoticed.

This is the second recorded instance of a lane losing its deliverable in two days; the first is why the lane brief now carries the COMMIT RULE. That rule guards the worker's side (commit your files). It does not guard the integrator's side, which is where this one was lost. The window is narrow: after a reset, the only copy is a dangling object subject to gc.

Recovered by this session from 823ff7e and landed on lane/w9-adopter; the work itself was never at fault.

Done looks like: an integration step that refuses to accept a lane as merged when the merged diff does not contain the paths the lane's acceptance names, and refuses to accept a resolution when the branch holds no commits beyond base — both failing loud, naming the missing paths, before any branch is reset.
acceptance: GIVEN a lane whose acceptance names file paths, WHEN its branch is merged and the merged diff does not contain those paths, THEN integration stops and says which paths are missing, instead of reporting the merge as carrying them. GIVEN a lane branch with no commits beyond its base, WHEN a resolution is offered for its item, THEN it is refused as stuck. GIVEN a lane branch about to be reset or deleted, WHEN it holds commits not reachable from the integration branch, THEN the reset is refused until those commits are merged or explicitly abandoned by name.

description:

title: Offline, a document's sync moment is in the banner and not on the document
description:
platform-web.v1 §10 says the helper "serves the documents already fetched, each marked with the moment it came from."

converge-719 delivers the moment for every stored payload, but shows it in one place: the offline banner, as a row of chips reading "vision as of 03:09 AM", "direction as of 03:09 AM", and so on. Measured 2026-09-04 in a rendered browser with the network off, at 1280 and 390. The acceptance line for converge-719 — "a visible 'as of <time>'" — is met.

What is not done is the stronger reading of §10: the mark beside the thing it is about. A steward reading a document offline sees the document, and has to look at the banner at the bottom-left to learn how old it is. On a phone that is a different part of the screen entirely.

The fact is already on the wire and needs no new plumbing: `sw.js` puts `X-Converge-Synced-At` on every stored payload and re-serves it with `X-Converge-Offline: 1`, and posts `{type: 'converge-offline-read', path, syncedAt}` to the page for each one. Anything that renders can read it.

Owner: whoever owns `app/static/js/render/*.js` and `app/templates/direction.html`. The converge-719 lane owns neither, so this is written down rather than made.
acceptance: GIVEN the app with the network off WHEN a stored document is read THEN the moment that document was fetched is shown on the document itself, not only in the offline banner, at 1280 and at 390.

title: app/tests/test_tmux_view.py stomps a parallel lane: fixed tmux socket plus kill-server
description:
Contract: operation.v1 (a check that cannot run says so, rather than reporting a failure someone else caused).

Measured 2026-09-04 in lane w8-ask-route. Two runs of `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests` in this worktree reported failures inside `app/tests/test_tmux_view.py` — first 15 setup errors, then 2 assertion failures — while nothing in the run touched tmux code. Four later runs of the same command, and two runs of that file alone, all passed (15 passed, twice). The suite is green here.

The cause is shared state, not flakiness in the app: the module's autouse fixture runs `tmux -L cvtest kill-server` and then creates sessions named `colors`, `long`, `alt` on that same fixed socket. Every lane worktree runs the same command against the same socket, so two lanes testing at once kill each other's sessions mid-run. Ten lanes make this likely rather than rare.

The failure is worse than noise: it points a lane at a file it did not touch, and the honest reading ("someone else's run") is only available to someone who already knows the fixture uses a fixed socket.

Two ways out, both in the fixture: name the socket per-run (e.g. `cvtest-<pid>`), or refuse to run when a `cvtest` server is already up rather than killing it. The first keeps parallel runs independent; the second reports a collision instead of causing one.
acceptance: GIVEN two `pytest -q app/tests` runs in different worktrees at the same time WHEN both reach test_tmux_view.py THEN neither kills the other's tmux sessions and both report their own result — and no run reports a failure caused by another run.

title: Core 11 still reads SKIP: two pre-convention park entries in HIGHWAY.md name no call type, and converge-0l8 closed without moving the reading
description:
Contract: operation.v1 — Core 11. Ledger row CVG-021.

converge-0l8 was resolved at 2026-09-04 with "every CALL line in the plan record names one of the four". Step (j) re-run live after that resolution still says otherwise, because it counts recorded CALLS, not only stamped `CALL` lines:

    Core 11 (CVG-021) SKIP: 4 of 6 recorded call(s) name which of the four they
    are (ratify: 3, irreversible: 1); the other 2 name none, so this run cannot
    say the calls that reached the steward were the four.

The two that name none are both from the 2026-09-03 wave, read from the step's own `park_events` evidence:

    2026-09-03T08:17:33Z  "Parked: protocol-terms."
    2026-09-03T08:29:04Z  "protocol-terms parked on lane/w6-protocol-terms for the steward."

Both are park sentences with no call word in them; the loose form the reading accepts elsewhere supplies what CONTINUED, never which of the four the call was. So this is not a defect in converge-0l8's work — the four stamped/inferable calls do name their kind — it is that two older entries record a call to the steward and say nothing about its type, and the reading refuses to claim the calls were the four while any recorded call is unclassified.

Two ways to close it, and the choice is the manager session's, not a lane's:
1. Name the type of those two entries in place (both look like `ratify` — protocol-terms was parked as a ratify card in the entries either side of them), which turns the reading PASS.
2. Decide that pre-convention entries are out of scope for the reading, and change what step (j) counts — evaluations/ is not this lane's, so that is a filed change, not an edit.

Until then CVG-021 stays GAP and cites this item. Its predecessors are all resolved: converge-5vz (wrote the stamp convention), converge-aaw (first stamped calls), converge-0l8 (stamped the older CALL lines).

Verify with: `uv run evaluations/turnkey/run.py --env local --steps j --workspace ~/dev/hw-converge --project converge`
acceptance: GIVEN turnkey step (j) reading the plan record on this host WHEN every call it records names which of the four sanctioned calls it is — or the step is changed by decision to count only entries written under the convention — THEN the Core 11 reading reports PASS rather than SKIP; AND ledger row CVG-021 is re-derived against that reading in the run's own words; AND `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` exits 0.

    by this harness, which is the post-merge gate and not the manager session;
    and on whose verification it was — [the same unattributed reading]

So the missing observation is now precise, which it was not before: a wave whose newest record of a check run was written by the manager session itself, rather than arriving through a lane merge. On this host the ledger is edited in lanes and merged, so the commit that carries the newest check record is a lane's — which is exactly the condition the step reports, and it is not a defect in the step.

1. The manager session records its own post-merge check somewhere the step can read (a stamp it writes after integrating, attributed to its own commit). That makes the clause observable on every wave, and changes what a manager session must do.

2. The step reads attribution from a driven turnkey run instead, where the harness controls who commits what. That measures the fixture rather than this host, which is the harness's usual bargain.

Also unclosed and worth carrying: steps (j) and (k) have only ever run in observed mode. A driven container has never carried them.
