title: Nothing checks that an amended contract records its amendment anywhere
description:
Contract: documents.v1 §4 — Changelog only if amended.

The documents kit treats Changelog as an optional section, so a contract that was amended and carries no record of it passes rule 4 today. Four contracts are in exactly that state: experience.v1, experience-direction.v1, experience-operation.v1 and experience-collaboration.v1 were all amended on 2026-09-06 by commit d45918a, all four carry no Changelog section, and all four still say "content owner-ratified 2026-09-03" in their first line. Nothing in the suite noticed.

The proposal contracts/documents.v1-candidate.md (this lane) asks the steward to settle what records an amendment when the changelog will not fit — the archived proposal plus an `amended <date>` in the H1. It deliberately adds no kit assert for that, because applying it puts documents.v1 at exactly 100 lines and there is no line left in its Conformance kit asserts section to hold one. So the rule, if ratified, arrives uncheckable.

This item is the assert, and it survives whichever shape the steward picks: an amended contract must carry a record of the amendment — a changelog row, or an H1 date, or both — and the kit must be able to tell. Doing it needs a line back in documents.v1's asserts section, which is itself a proposal.

Wait for the steward's word on documents.v1-candidate.md before starting; the wording of the assert follows the answer.

title: The turnkey harness's step (i) reads the whole return log for the five parts, so any prose anywhere satisfies it
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 10 — "A brief on every return."

`evaluations/turnkey/run.py` step (i) (`step_brief`, ~line 1590) lowercases the entire `docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md` and asks whether each of `["time away", "finished", "stuck", "needs you", "quietly broken"]` appears **anywhere in the file**. Dates and sentence counts are also file-wide. Three consequences, all measured 2026-09-04:

1. **Any prose satisfies it.** A header, a footnote, or an unrelated paragraph containing those five words passes the check with no brief present. converge-823 had to deliberately *not* write the five labels into the log's new header for this reason — the header would have flipped the check from red to green without a single entry gaining a part. That constraint should not exist; the check should be per-entry.

2. **It cannot see an unbriefed return.** Counting parts across a file says nothing about whether each return got one — which is the whole of what the clause asks. The mode now stamps each return in its entry heading (`## <date> <HH:MM> — …`), so the harness can now compare the two, as converge-4xg's probe does.

3. **This repo's own log reads red for the wrong reason.** Measured on the log as it stands: parts present `['time away','finished','needs you']`, missing `['stuck','quietly broken']` — because nine well-written briefs say "nothing stopped" and "nothing broke" in their own words rather than in the check's. Per-entry labelled parts (which clause 10 now requires) make that judgment exact instead of lexical.

Not fixed by converge-823: that lane owns `modes/converge-manager.md` and `docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md` only.
acceptance: GIVEN evaluations/turnkey/run.py WHEN step (i) judges a return log THEN it counts the five parts within a single dated entry rather than across the file, and reports stamped returns against completed briefs; a log whose header alone carries the five words FAILS, and a log with one stamped return missing one part FAILS naming the part. Falsified if a file-wide substring read still passes on a log with no complete entry.

title: The mode's first wake: investigate, then propose — both paths, keyed to ratified Core 14

title: The operation page shows six of the eight things surface.v1 Core 9 puts in view
description:
Contract: surface.v1 — Core 9, "The whole operation in view. Lanes running against lanes intended, with the fill control · running against waiting-on-you · truly ready against waiting on you · the plan in order with reasons".

Measured 2026-09-04 by running the shipped surface kit's rule 9b against the app's own rendered /operation page — the same subject and the same import path tests/test_plain_words_on_the_surface.py uses for rule 8c, the kit read from where it lives at conformance/_superseded/surface/run.py and never reimplemented:

             (truly ready: False, waiting on you: False);
             the plan in order, with reasons (no plan is in order on the page)
    RULE 9a: SKIP — the lanes cannot be read in this target, so the gauge states
             no number to check against the fill control

Six of the eight are on the page. Two are not, and they are two different absences: the queue's two numbers (truly ready against waiting on you) are never stated, and the plan is not rendered in order with its reasons.

This row (CVG-038) named converge-fmz as its fix. converge-fmz is finished, and closed with a resolution that says the opposite of what the page now measures: "Against the app: PASS, 'all 8 parts of the operation are on one page, and nothing on the board stops anything'". A reader following that cite lands on completed work whose text contradicts the row. The measurement above is what the kit actually reports today.

Rule 9a declines rather than fails, because the fixture project the kit is pointed at has no lanes directory — the gauge has no number to state. That is a subject problem, not a page problem, and closing it needs a project with lanes in it.

Two neighbouring items carry the same two absences against the experience family's own contracts and the other app: converge-q66 (queue numbers) and converge-lwa (the plan's reasons). Whoever takes this should check whether their work already puts these two on the page, and close this by re-running rule 9b rather than by reading their resolutions.

Discovered while re-deriving fifteen ledger rows for converge-0gb.

title: candidate-guard: false-positive 'no mounted tools visible' warning on every launch (validator trial-mount)
description: Contract: composition.v1 §6–7 (the guard's coverage and enforcement). Source: the steward's bug report /home/bkrabach/dev/vision-focused-team-ci/BUG-REPORT-candidate-guard-mock-mount-warning.md (2026-09-03). Quoted finding: 'Every amplifier start prints candidate-guard: no mounted tools visible at mount time … The hook's mount() checks coordinator.get("tools") and warns when empty … but before the real mount, amplifier-core's HookValidator trial-mounts every hook module against a bare MockCoordinator() that has no tools, so the check fires there.' title: app/tests/test_api.py: the document state read from the ledger comes back "draft" where the test asserts "gap", so the worst-honest-word rule is unproven
description:
Contract: experience.v1 §7 — "The app holds no data of its own. It shows the project's documents, code record, work queue, lanes, return log, and pending decisions. A second copy of the truth is a defect, not a cache." A document’s state word is the ledger’s reading of that document; falling back to the H1 status shows a second copy of the truth instead. §6 governs which words that reading may use.

Found by the scheduled reconcile of 2026-09-04 against target-repo @ a5c6c02, running the repository's OWN suite (`python3 -m pytest app/tests -q` -> 164 passed, 2 failed).

FAILING CHECK (run and observed, not read):

    python3 -m pytest app/tests/test_api.py::test_manager_lists_the_docs_with_a_state_from_the_ledger -q
    app/tests/test_api.py:305: AssertionError: assert 'draft' == 'gap'

The test builds a fixture repository with one CONFORMS row and one GAP row for the same document and asserts, in its own comment, "the worst honest word wins, so not kept" -- expecting the document to read `gap`. The app answers `draft`.

Two readings, and this item does not pick one:
  (a) the app stopped folding the ledger's rows into a document's state word and is
      falling back to the H1 status, in which case a reader is shown "draft" over a
      document the ledger says has a broken promise; or
  (b) the state vocabulary changed deliberately in a later wave and this test was
      not moved with it.

Either way the repository's own suite is red on main and the ledger-to-document state
path is currently unproven.

NOT covered by any existing ledger row: no row in ledger/rows.yaml cites this test or
this behaviour. Checked against the 41 open items in this project before filing -- no
open item names it.
acceptance:
GIVEN target-repo at the commit this is fixed on
WHEN `python3 -m pytest app/tests/test_api.py -q` is run
THEN it passes, AND the reason it passes is written down: either the app again derives a document's state from its ledger rows with the worst honest word winning (reading a), or the test asserts the state vocabulary the app actually implements and a note says which wave changed it (reading b).

title: Guard: an H1 status of "(RATIFIED <date>)" is not recognised as locked, while "**Status:** RATIFIED" is
description:
Contract: composition.v1 clause 7 (structural enforcement of the proposal route) and documents.v1 clause 6 (status lives in the H1 and nowhere else).

Measured on the committed tree with the SHIPPED behaviors/converge.yaml config, calling the module's own functions:

  frozen_marker_regex : (?im)^\*\*Status:\*\*\s*(?:RATIFIED|FROZEN)|^status:\s*FROZEN|^#.*\(FROZEN\b

The three branches disagree about RATIFIED. The body branch accepts "**Status:** RATIFIED"; the H1 branch accepts only "(FROZEN". So a document that moves its status into the H1 - exactly what documents.v1 clause 6 mandates - and whose word is RATIFIED rather than FROZEN, reads as UNLOCKED where the same word in the body read as LOCKED.

docs/PROTOCOL.md is the live instance. Before this lane it carried "**Status:** RATIFIED - 2026-08-29" (regex matched). After the ratified v3 pass its H1 reads "# ... - Protocol v3 (RATIFIED 2026-09-03)" and no body status line remains, so the regex no longer matches at all:

  docs/PROTOCOL.md  matches guarded_globs: False  frozen_marker_regex: True -> '**Status:** RATIFIED'   [before]
  docs/PROTOCOL.md  matches guarded_globs: False  frozen_marker_regex: False                            [after]

Nothing changed in practice, because docs/PROTOCOL.md is not in guarded_globs (contracts/*.md, contracts/**/*.md, docs/VISION.md, VISION.md) and so was never guarded either way. The exposure is latent: the day a RATIFIED-in-H1 document is added to guarded_globs, the guard silently declines to guard it - the same under-match failure mode that produced converge-diw / -9vw / -ksg, and the reason the module README gives for making the H1 branch deliberately loose ("over-matching only ever guards more, whereas a guard that under-matches fails silently").

Decide one of: (a) teach the H1 branch RATIFIED as well as FROZEN, in the module default and behaviors/converge.yaml together (the test asserting they cannot diverge already exists); or (b) rule that RATIFIED is not a lock word, and record that where readers meet it.

Note: this item was filed with malformed markup that leaked stray tags into its own text and lost its acceptance field. This edit restores both.
acceptance: GIVEN a guarded file whose H1 carries "(RATIFIED <date>)" and which carries no "**Status:**" line WHEN a write to it is evaluated by hooks-candidate-guard THEN the outcome is the decided one - denied as locked, or documented as deliberately not a lock word - and the module default and behaviors/converge.yaml agree, proven by the existing divergence test.

title: Surface kit checks the mockup's markup, so the server-rendered app fails rules 1a–1e, 3a and 4
description:
Running the shipped kit at a page rendered by the companion app —

  uv run conformance/surface/run.py <a page rendered by amplifier_converge.web>

— reports FAIL on 1a, 1b, 1c, 1d, 1e, 3a and 4 on every page, and PASS on 5.

The failures are not the app missing the promises. They are the kit looking for the *mockup's* way of keeping them: `data-goto` navigation, `#needCount`, `[data-answer]` controls, a `fillLanes` routine, a `#readiness` block, `#diffBtn`, `#filedList`, and script handlers wiring them together. The app keeps the same promises without any script at all — places are links to real routes, answering is a form POST that re-renders a shorter list, the lock control is a disabled button, what-changed is a rendered list of removed and added sentences, and every answer is written to the dated ratification record on disk. `tests/test_renders_at_both_widths.py::test_pages_are_server_rendered_with_no_script_at_all` asserts the app carries no script on purpose, so this is not something the app can satisfy by adding handlers.

Two rules also still SKIP with the reason "the app is not built yet (converge-2qh)", which is no longer true.

So a steward reading the kit's verdict on the app sees FAIL and cannot tell a real defect from a shape mismatch — which is exactly what a conformance kit exists to prevent.

Not attempted here: lane w3-app-vocab owns `src/amplifier_converge/**` only, and conformance/ is explicitly out of its scope.

Also open, from the same run: the verified mockup at /home/bkrabach/dev/vision-focused-team-ci/ai_working/converge-ux-mockups/index.html still FAILs rule 5 on "bundle" and "recipe" (four lines of card and lane copy, plus one promise sentence, named in converge-y7s). It lives in another repository, outside any file this lane may edit.

title: No write stamps a document locked, so the lock gate's control has no server half
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 §11 ("The lock control is gated on the four conditions... The control is live only when all four are met, and nothing locks on its own.")

converge-jdm built the gate in the browser: `app/templates/direction.html` shows the four Freeze Bar conditions, and `render/direction.js` keeps `#lockButton` inert until all four are met (three the steward's own word, one read from the document's ledger standing). What the gate reaches is `POST /api/managers/{mid}/docs/{repo}/{doc}/lock` — a route the app does not answer.

Measured 2026-09-04 against a live app: the app's own `/openapi.json` lists eight write routes and no lock among them, so the call 404s and the screen says so out loud rather than looking like it locked something (the same choice `ask` made before converge-ddt).

The server half is a document write and belongs with the others in `app/writes.py`: stamp `(FROZEN <date>)` into the document's own H1 the way `documents.v1` §6 puts status there and `writes.document_lock()` already reads it, commit it authored `<steward> via Converge`, and refuse when the document already carries a locking word. `app/serve.py` and `app/writes.py` were outside converge-jdm's lane, which is why this is filed rather than done.
acceptance: GIVEN a DRAFT document whose four conditions are met WHEN the steward uses the lock control THEN the app answers a lock write, the document's H1 carries `(FROZEN <date>)` in the file on disk, the change is committed in the steward's name, and re-opening the document shows it locked; AND the same write refuses a document that already carries a locking word, naming it.

title: Nobody has yet run the new composition rule 5b against the rewritten README — the two halves are on different branches
description:
Contract: composition.v1 Core 5 (ratified 2026-09-06 — one install command is the path an adopter takes)

The clause's two halves were built in parallel and have never been in one commit:

- `converge-xk2u` rewrote `README.md` to one named command plus an Advanced path, on its own branch (now merged to main at d2a6409). Its own resolution records residual 1: "The composition kit's NEW Core 5 rule does not exist yet … There was no branch to run it from."
- `converge-462l` added that rule — `conformance/composition/run.py` rule 5b — and ledger row CVG-300, on lane/w11-apply-ratified. In that tree README.md is still the old two-path section, so rule 5b reports FAIL there, correctly.

MEASURED SINCE FILING, and it answers the shape question this item was opened with. Rule 5b was run against main's README by extracting it to a scratch directory (`git show main:README.md`) and calling the rule on it:

    PASS — README.md:61 presents exactly one command as the adopter's path
    ('## Install'), 1 other install path(s) are marked advanced with who needs
    them, and nothing later recommends against it

The `### Advanced:` heading is read correctly: the rule's first form read a path lead as a bold line only and reported "no install command at all" about main's README; that was a rule defect, found before it shipped, and it now reads heading or bold lead or ordinary sentence, and tells a second install path from a check command by whether it invokes the same program.

So the expected answer is PASS. What is still owed is the real thing, not the proxy: the rule run from a tree that carries BOTH halves, its verdict pasted, and CVG-300 re-derived against it — the row is pinned to FAIL and will make verify.py red the moment they meet, which is the instruction to re-derive it.
acceptance: Given a branch carrying both the rewritten README.md and conformance/composition/run.py rule 5b When `uv run conformance/composition/run.py .` runs Then rule 5b's verdict is printed, and ledger row CVG-300 carries that verdict with its probe expect matching it — kept. Until the two halves are in one tree and the whole kit has actually been run there: not yet.

title: Manager sessions register themselves; the app discovers them — new and existing sessions show up on Home
description: Contract: experience.v1 Core 2 and Core 5 (the home shows every manager session you run; whatever you can do in the app the manager session can do too) and experience-operation.v1 Core 1 (one manager session per operation, found without configuration). Today the app lists manager sessions from a hand-written ~/.amplifier/converge-app.toml, so a new manager session — or an existing one on another project — never appears until a person edits a file. The steward's step 4: manager sessions, new AND existing, register themselves and show up on Home when the UX runs locally. Mechanism: on every wake the manager mode writes <workspace>/.converge/<manager-id>/registration.toml (name, steward, workspace root, repos with their paths and default branches, plan record path, tmux socket + session name, queue project, last-seen time); the app discovers registrations by scanning every workspace root it is told about (a list of workspace roots in converge-app.toml, default: the parent of the app's own repo) plus any path in CONVERGE_WORKSPACES, merges them with the hand-written managers (hand-written wins on conflict), shows last-seen and marks a manager 'Silent, may have died' when its heartbeat is older than 15 minutes; existing manager sessions register on their next wake because the mode writes the file unconditionally. Show the registration in the app's Details fold so a steward can see where a manager came from.
acceptance: GIVEN a manager session waking in the converge-manager mode THEN <workspace>/.converge/<manager-id>/registration.toml exists with the named fields and a fresh last-seen; GIVEN the app started with no hand-written managers and one registration under the default workspace root THEN Home lists that manager with its steward, repos and lane count, and /api/boot carries it; GIVEN a registration whose heartbeat is 16 minutes old THEN Home shows 'Silent, may have died' in plain words; GIVEN both a hand-written manager and a registration with the same id THEN the hand-written one is shown once with the registration's last-seen; GIVEN app tests THEN green including a test for each of the above.

title: No document tells an adopter how to start a manager session, or how to tell whether it took
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §1

The manager session is the product — README.md:16-20 describes it as the long-running session that runs a project's work on your behalf — and no document a reader can reach says how to start one.

Searched README.md, AGENTS.md, PINS.md and docs/*.md for "/mode" and for the mode-setting call: no match in any of them. The only amplifier commands in the whole reader-facing surface are the three install commands at README.md:56, :70 and :71.

modes/converge-manager.md is named in README.md:131 as "the manager-session mode". Its last line, :320-321, says to use /mode off when the project is handed off. That is the only mode syntax in the file: a reader is told how to leave a mode nobody told them how to enter.

The one sentence that names the mode as the thing to use is context/converge-awareness.md:34-35, which is context injected into a session — the model reads it, the human never does, and it names no command either.

Two further traps sit behind the missing sentence. Entering the mode is gated: evaluations/turnkey/manager-objective.md:15-17 tells its own agent the call is refused once and must be repeated. And behaviors/converge.yaml:124-141 records, measured, that a duplicate converge namespace makes the mode vanish silently, with or without the modes block (filed converge-348). So a person who guesses the name, types it once, and sees a refusal has no way to tell a gate from a broken install — and README.md's install section ends with no command to confirm the install did anything at all.

Found by the onboarding audit, docs/workflow/ONBOARDING-AUDIT-2026-09-04.md, findings b-1 through b-5.
acceptance: Given a person who has just run the install command and has read no other document, when they finish README.md's install section, then they have the exact command that starts a manager session in a project directory, the sentence that the first attempt may be refused and repeating it confirms, and one command that prints whether the install actually took. Given they run those three, when the third prints its output, then it distinguishes a working install from a silently absent one rather than exiting clean either way.

title: README's 'What ships' calls src/amplifier_converge/ the app, while the app a reader is told to run is app/
description:
Contract: composition.v1 Core 5's shape — one command, and nothing later telling the reader they should have typed the other — applied to running the app rather than installing the bundle; and documents.v1's "a document says what it means".

Two different web bodies live in this repository and README.md names both as "the app", in two different places, with two different commands:

* `README.md`'s "What ships" list: "`src/amplifier_converge/` — the companion web page (the two halves). Run it beside a project with `amplifier-converge web --repo .`; it listens on loopback by default, on purpose."
* `app/` — the FastAPI app with Home, the six surfaces, PAM sign-in and registration discovery, served on 8788 by `scripts/run-app.sh`, documented in `app/README.md`. This is the one the new "Run the app" section under "Start your first manager session" tells a reader to run (converge-sf1u), and the one `app/converge-app.service` runs on this host.

Both trees are real and both have been committed to recently (`git log -- src/amplifier_converge` → 4d91de6, e0277a9, 05b3f09; `git log -- app` → 9e9ccb8), so this is not dead code somebody forgot to delete — it is two live things sharing one name in the reader's document.

Lane w14-run-the-app changed exactly one line, the "Where everything lives" row, which now reads `app/`, started by `scripts/run-app.sh`. The "What ships" bullet was outside its ownership and still says the other thing, so the README currently answers the question "where is the app?" two different ways depending which section you read.

title: No section contract tags a behavior with one of the four words, and none places one against the three surface classes
description:
Two umbrella clauses that are promises about how the family is **written**, not about the app. Measured 2026-09-04 by `conformance/experience/run.py` reading `contracts/` directly.

**Core 9 — "Every behavior carries one of four words."** Rule 9 FAILs: `experience-collaboration.v1.md` tags 0 of its 10 Core clauses and `experience-console.v1.md` tags 0 of its 10. (`experience-direction.v1` and `experience-operation.v1` tag every clause, so the shape is already established and two contracts are simply missing it.) Required, idiom, optional and excluded are how a body knows what its own absence means; an untagged behavior means nothing either way, and a platform contract cannot be written against it. CVG-108 recorded this from a hand-written probe.

**Core 13 — "Three surface classes … every behavior placed against all three."** Rule 13 FAILs harder: *none* of the four section contracts so much as names `quick-access`. The five platform contracts do name it; the sections, where the behaviors actually live, do not. So "nobody thought about the widget" can still pass as a decision, which is the exact failure the clause exists to stop. CVG-112 recorded this.

Both are contract-authoring work, and `contracts/` is outside the lane that found them. Both contracts are `(DRAFT)`, so neither guard blocks the edit today — but if either has locked by the time this is worked, it takes a `<contract>.vN-candidate.md` proposal beside it (AGENTS.md rule 2), not an edit.

Note the two clauses interact: once a behavior carries one of the four words, placing it against full app · quick-access · notification is the same sentence's other half, so doing them together is cheaper than doing either twice.
acceptance: GIVEN the repository WHEN `uv run conformance/experience/run.py <app>` is run THEN rule 9 PASSes — every Core clause of every `experience-*.v1` contract carries `(REQUIRED)`, `(IDIOM)`, `(OPTIONAL)` or `(EXCLUDED)` — AND rule 13 PASSes: every section contract places its behaviors against full app, quick-access and notification.

title: The priority route landed but the tripwire test that told the next lane to retire it is still asserting the route is absent
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 Core 14 (the five writes the app offers, said out loud on the surface). Found on 2026-09-04 while running the app suite for converge-1sfp, on lane/w9-queue-and-kits at commit ed9f83f.

    FAILED app/tests/test_writes_named.py::
      test_the_two_things_this_body_cannot_do_say_so_and_say_what_to_do_instead
    1 failed, 294 passed, 148 skipped

The assertion, and its own instructions, verbatim:

    assert "priority" not in offered, (
        "the app now answers a priority route - this assertion has fired: replace
         it with one about the write working, and delete the limit sentence from
         shell.html (converge-a5g)")
    E  assert 'priority' not in {'ask', 'decision', 'feedback', 'priority', 'steer'}

This is a tripwire doing exactly what it was built to do. converge-a5g asked for the fifth write, the route landed, and the assertion fired to say so. What did not happen is the second half: converge-a5g is RESOLVED, and the assertion it names — plus the limit sentence in app/templates/shell.html that says the app has no priority control — are both still there. So the suite is red on a green outcome, and the app's own words still deny a control it now offers.

Two things to do, both named by the test itself. Replace the negative assertion with one about the write working — that a steward can raise or lower a priority and the write lands where the queue reads it, which is what converge-a5g's own acceptance asks for. And delete the limit sentence from shell.html, because Core 14 asks the surface to say what it offers, and it now offers this.

Confirmed pre-existing, not caused by the lane that found it: the same test fails at ed9f83f with this lane's working tree stashed, and this lane touched no app route, template, or test.

Filed rather than fixed: app/tests/** and app/templates/** are not in lane w9-queue-and-kits's ownership (docs/work-items.json, app/static/dev/stub_server.py, conformance/experience-direction/**, evaluations/turnkey/**).

title: The adopter harness judges three of its rows on the wrong evidence, so two reds overclaim and one measures nothing
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §7 (done means the check was re-run, and a marker is a claim)

Found by running evaluations/adopter/ for the first time on 2026-09-04. Recorded in evaluations/adopter/RESULT.md under "Limits of this run"; the harness was deliberately left as it ran so that document describes the code that produced it.

Three defects, all in how the harness judges rather than in what it drives.

One. Both scenarios share one container, in order. Converge is installed by scenario 1's AI user, so by the time scenario 2 starts it is already there and S2.1 measures nothing about scenario 2's own install. Only S1.1 is a real install result. Each scenario needs its own fresh container.

Two. The queue probe looks for the amplifier-work-tracker CLI on PATH and then says, in its missing line, that no item can exist. That is more than it measured. README.md:90 promises the app behavior gives the session its work_* filing tools, which is a different thing from a CLI binary, and scenario 2's AI user reported filing item sensorlog-9ge under a new sensorlog project through exactly that path. So the CLI was genuinely absent and whether a queue held items is simply unproven. The probe has to read the queue the way an agent writes it.

Three. The manager-session probe captures the tmux pane once, at the end. In scenario 1 the AI user restarted its session twenty-eight seconds before the budget cut, so the capture caught a blank pane and the row reported that the prompt "never shows [converge-manager]". An empty pane is not evidence of absence. The pane has to be sampled through the scenario, not once after it.

None of these is a reason to distrust the passes: every pass was read off a file or a live pane. They are reasons to distrust two of the three reds, which is worse, because a red that names the wrong cause sends the next reader to the wrong place.
acceptance: Given the harness runs both scenarios, when the run finishes, then each scenario's install step was measured in a container where Converge was absent at launch. Given a scenario in which an agent filed a work item through its session tools and no CLI is installed, when the queue step is judged, then it finds that item and passes, rather than reporting the CLI's absence as proof that no item exists. Given a scenario in which the manager mode was active at some point and the session is restarted before the end, when the manager-session step is judged, then it reports that the mode was seen, and an empty capture is reported as "could not tell" rather than as absence.

title: experience.v1 and experience-collaboration.v1 have no conformance kit
description:
Contract: experience.v1 §5, §8, §9, §13, §14 ("Conformance kit asserts" — seven bullets) and experience-collaboration.v1 (same section, seven bullets).

Seeding the ledger for the experience family (converge-pq2) built three kits — `experience-direction`, `experience-operation`, `experience-console` — because those three contracts have a body to judge. Two of the family's contracts got none, and the ledger rows say so clause by clause rather than leaving the silence unexplained.

Where a clause of `experience.v1` is kept by a section contract, its ledger row cites that section's kit rule and inherits its verdict. The clauses left over are the umbrella's own, and nothing asserts them:

- Core 4, "Exactly five writes" — countable from the app's own `/openapi.json`, unasserted.
- Core 5, "At most five things ask for your word at once … every answer lands in a dated ratification record" — the first half is countable from `/api/needs/{mid}`; the second is a file check.
- Core 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 — every behavior carries one of four words, per surface class; idioms satisfy behaviors and never subtract them; a body may exceed in idiom, never in features. These are readable from the contracts themselves (a REQUIRED/IDIOM/OPTIONAL/EXCLUDED tag per clause, and a placement against full app · quick-access · notification), and no kit reads them.
- Core 14, "Where a body genuinely cannot do a thing, it says so in the app" — measured today: the app offers feedback as text and a screenshot and not as voice, and says nothing about the limit anywhere.

For `experience-collaboration.v1`, clauses 4, 5, 6, 7 and 9 need a repository host with a second party on it; only a live host settles them. Its rows are NOT-ASSERTABLE with that reason, which is a different answer from this one — those need a subject, these need a kit.

Not built here: this lane's brief named three kits, and building a fourth and fifth would have made none of them good.

Ledger rows this closes: CVG-104, CVG-107, CVG-108, CVG-112, CVG-113. Grouped by cause and component on 2026-09-04 by docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md, which is where the whole mapping of rows to items is printed. The rows already named this item as their fix; what was missing was the list, written down here.
acceptance: GIVEN the experience family WHEN a kit for experience.v1 runs against the app THEN Core 4, 5, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 each have a rule with a negative fixture — or each is recorded can't check with a reason that names what a machine cannot settle; AND the ledger rows citing this item are re-derived against those verdicts.

title: Direction › Changes: align by git hunks, edit-in-place, persistent Keep/Restore, since-you-last-read (steward feedback 2026-09-03)
description: Contract: experience-direction.v1 (the Changes view; granular accept/revert constructing 'ratified with edits'; direct edits where legal, proposals when locked) and documents.v1 §8. Source — the steward's feedback on the running app at http://spark-1:8788 (build b7ed3f0, 2026-09-03), quoted: 'The diff is misaligned, we should actually leverage git diff under the hood to get that right. Many of the Before/Now are currently off by one, where one of the Now items was new and so then the next Now was lined up w/ the previous Before and so on. Also, we should have the opportunity to edit the value we want instead of only having a before/now. Also, all entries in the changes list say "vision: principle 8" - I guess maybe that is right though? I marked all "Keep this change", but leaving the change page to read and back and they are all reset - there seems to be no save.' Read against the code: (1) app/data.py pairs before/now sentences positionally after a sequence diff, so an insertion shifts every later pair — the fix is git's own hunks (git diff <since>..HEAD -U0 --word-diff=porcelain) mapped to sentences, with pure insertions shown as New and pure deletions as Removed; (2) no edit affordance exists — the mock never had one; (3) every entry's label is the commit subject 'vision: principle 8 …' because all changes come from one commit AND the label shows source where the section belongs — the section should be the heading path plus list-item number, the source the commit subject + short sha + date; (4) Keep/Restore were toast-only in the mock and were ported as such — nothing persists. Root cause under (1),(3),(4): the app diffs 'the last two commits' instead of 'since you last read' and keeps no per-steward read state, so there is nothing to save Keep against.
acceptance: GIVEN a document changed by an insertion between two commits WHEN Changes renders THEN every Before/Now pair is aligned by git hunk and the inserted sentence appears as New with no Before (fixture-tested); GIVEN a change card WHEN the steward chooses Edit and saves new wording THEN a DRAFT document gets a real commit authored to the steward and a locked document gets a <doc>.vN-candidate.md with the fenced before/after, and the card shows the result; GIVEN Keep is pressed WHEN the steward navigates away and back or reloads THEN the change stays kept (server-side per-user state); GIVEN 'Mark all as read' THEN the doc's since-you-last-read point advances and the changes list empties; AND each card shows section = heading path (+ item number) and source = commit subject · short sha · date.

title: The shell rail still says the app has no priority control and answers no route that would write one, and the tripwire guarding that sentence has fired
description: Contract: experience.v1 Core 14 — "Where a body genuinely cannot do a thing, it says so in the app." converge-a5g added the priority write, so two files now say something untrue and neither is in that lane's ownership. 1. `app/templates/shell.html:90-92` — the "Say it to the manager session instead" fold carries `Raise or lower a priority — not here` and the sentence "This app has no control that raises or lowers a priority, and answers no route that would write one. … Filed as converge-a5g." title: The umbrella kit's copy of clause 6's lane vocabulary drops three words, so a correct app is reported as wrong
description:
Contract: experience.v1 Core 6 (plain state words everywhere).

Measured 2026-09-06 against the app at 127.0.0.1:8788 while building docs/workflow/LOCK-SHEET-2026-09-06.md.

conformance/experience/run.py rule 6a reports:

    [FAIL] 6a  the app serves state words outside the three vocabularies this
               clause fixes: a lane's state: 'Silent - may have died' (4x).

The clause it judges says, at contracts/experience.v1.md line 36:

    Lanes: *Working - Quiet - Silent - may have died*.

so the word the app serves is verbatim what the clause names. The kit's own copy of that vocabulary, at conformance/experience/run.py line 180, is:

    "lanes": ("Working", "Quiet", "Silent"),

Three words are missing after the dash, and rule 6a compares by exact match, so the app can never satisfy it. Read live from the app to be sure the value is not something else that merely looks similar:

    GET /api/managers/converge/operation
    lane statusLabels served: ['Silent - may have died']

So the app is right, the clause is right, and the kit's transcription of the clause is short. This is the case conformance/README.md's rule about not tuning a finding away does not cover: nothing about the target is wrong, and the check disagrees with the contract it quotes rather than with the target.

Two consequences worth stating separately, because they need different care:

1. The umbrella reads as six failing rules where five are real. Anyone judging whether experience.v1 is close to a lock is being told the app is one problem further away than it is.
2. The same shape could be anywhere the kits hard-code a clause's words rather than reading them. The remedy is not only the one constant: a test that the kit's PLAIN_WORDS agree with the clause they claim to quote would keep the next transcription honest, and documents.v1 clause 10 carries the same three vocabularies for the same reason.

Note the neighbouring kit does not have the fault: conformance/documents/run.py keeps its lanes comment as "Working - Quiet - Silent - may have died" and matches on machine tokens rather than on the plain phrase, so it never needs the full phrase to be right.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN the app serves a lane state whose words are exactly those experience.v1 clause 6 names WHEN conformance/experience/run.py runs against it THEN rule 6a passes; AND GIVEN the kit's copy of any vocabulary that clause fixes WHEN the kit's own tests run THEN a test compares that copy against the clause's text and fails if they disagree. FALSIFIED IF rule 6a still reports a value the clause names verbatim as outside the vocabulary, or if the kit's list can drift from the clause with nothing failing.

title: CVG-020 is still 0 of 0 in this tree: converge-8er closed saying a return was stamped, and the probe counts none
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 10 — a brief on every return. Ledger row **CVG-020**.

MEASURED 2026-09-04 by the scheduled reconcile against target-repo @ a5c6c02, by running the row's own probe:

    python3 ledger/checks/return_log_ratio.py
    CLAUSE-10-STAMPED-RETURNS=0 BRIEFED-RETURNS=0 UNBRIEFED=0        (exit 0)

The probe meets its expect, so the row is honest: the mechanism is encoded and the comparison is computable, but nothing has been counted, and a ratio with no returns in it is not evidence that the clause is kept.

WHY THIS IS FILED. CVG-020 cited converge-8er, RESOLVED in the live queue — a red row citing finished work (LEDGER-FORMAT §2). More than that: converge-8er was closed with the resolution "The manager session stamped a return in docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md with the five labelled parts (51da070); CVG-020's probe now has a stamped, briefed return to count." Read against this tree, that is not so — the probe run above counts zero on both sides. Whatever landed in 51da070 is not in target-repo @ a5c6c02, so the denominator the item was closed on does not exist here.

That makes this the same shape as converge-vtnm and converge-j0u5, and worth its own item rather than a re-point: a resolution that contradicts the row it closed is the exact failure the live-work tripwire was added for, and it was invisible because docs/work-items.json is a stale 76-item export of a 217-item queue.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS, unchanged from converge-8er and repeated so the reader need not follow a closed cite:
  1. A manager session runs a real return in THIS tree — stamps it, then writes the five parts under it. The probe then reads STAMPED-RETURNS=1 BRIEFED-RETURNS=1, its expect fails loudly (the count is the pin), and CVG-020 is re-derived to Kept on a measured pairing. This needs no code; it needs a wave.
  2. The steward ratifies, in writing, that the clause is kept by the mode's standing instruction plus the log rather than by a countable pairing.

The honest limit, carried forward: a return the manager session never recorded at all leaves no trace on either side of the ratio.
acceptance: GIVEN this tree WHEN `python3 ledger/checks/return_log_ratio.py` is run THEN it reports STAMPED-RETURNS above zero with BRIEFED-RETURNS equal to it and UNBRIEFED=0 — or the steward has ratified in writing that the clause is kept by the mode plus the log; AND ledger row CVG-020 is re-derived from that run, quoting it. Falsified if CVG-020 is moved to Kept while the count is still 0 of 0.

title: Surface: three clause-halves have no check now that the app ships (ledger rows CVG-038, CVG-057, CVG-066)
description:
The companion page now ships (commit 05b3f09) and its 116 tests pass, so most surface.v1 clauses moved to CONFORMS in ledger/rows.yaml. Three halves have no check at all against the shipped app:

- Core 9, "The whole operation in view" — lanes running against lanes intended with the fill control, running against waiting-on-you, the plan in order with reasons, each lane's state and evidence with drill-in, your limits, the feedback drop, "tell all". tests/ has a file per clause for 1-7 and 10; there is none for 9. - Core 8, second half — no equivalent of the surface kit's rule 5 (internal vocabulary outside a Details fold) runs against the shipped app. The kit reads an HTML file or a directory with index.html; the app is server-rendered and there is no wiring between them. `test_technical_words_stay_behind_a_details_fold` asserts the fold exists; nothing scans the app's own words for terms a non-engineer would have to look up. acceptance: GIVEN the shipped companion app WHEN its tests run THEN surface.v1 Core 9 has at least one assertion, the required state vocabularies are asserted, and the internal-vocabulary scan runs against the app's own rendered words; AND ledger rows CVG-038, CVG-057 and CVG-066 move off "not yet".

same contract. Filed so the debt is visible in one place, and parked in the

title: main is red: 42 GAP rows cite work items the export now says are resolved, and CVG-051 misses its expect

title: main.js still toasts "The console is read-only in this version" — unreachable today, false whenever it surfaces
description:
Contract: experience-console.v1 Core 3 and Core 9.

Discovered while closing converge-55b, which named this exact line as work outside its own file ownership. Lane w8-hygiene owns `app/templates/console.html`, `app/static/js/render/console.js` (note + disabled attribute), and `app/tests/test_console_input.py` only — `app/static/js/main.js` is another owner's file, so this is filed rather than fixed.

WHAT IS THERE, `app/static/js/main.js:149`:

    $('consoleForm').addEventListener('submit', (e) => { e.preventDefault(); toast('The console is read-only in this version.'); });

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT. It is unreachable. `app/static/js/render/console.js`'s `wireFurniture()` binds a `keydown` handler on the field (Enter, no Shift) and a `click` handler on the submit button, and both call `preventDefault()` before calling the console's own `sendLine()`. Neither path reaches a form submit, and those two handlers are wired unconditionally, not only when typing is live. Verified in a real browser at 1280 and 390 on 2026-09-04 against the app on 127.0.0.1:8873: typing is live, the send button is live, and the footer reads "not a chat — this pane is the manager session itself" at both widths.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS. The sentence is now false. The app has taken keystrokes since converge-tfu — `POST /api/tmux/{socket}/{session}/keys` answers, and `conformance/experience-console/run.py` rule 3 passes on it. Any future change that removes one of console.js's two `preventDefault()` calls, or that lands a submit path console.js does not own, surfaces a toast telling a steward the console is read-only while it is typing into their manager session. It is a false statement kept alive only by an accident of event ordering.

THE FIX, one line, either way:
- delete the handler outright (the two live handlers already cover Enter and the button), or
- make it call the console's own send instead of toasting.

Prefer deleting it: a second, differently-behaved submit path is the thing that would make this misfire in the first place.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS ITEM: grep for "read-only in this version" in `app/static/js/main.js` returning nothing.
acceptance: GIVEN app/static/js/main.js WHEN the console form's submit handler is read THEN it does not toast that the console is read-only — either the handler is gone, or it calls the console's own send; AND `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests` stays green; AND `uv run conformance/experience-console/run.py <running app>` still reports rule 3 and rule 9 PASS.

title: app/README.md still tells stewards an older snapshot cannot be restored
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 §6.

`app/README.md`, under **History: restoring, at four scopes**, says:

    **Which snapshot a restore reaches, and which it cannot.** It reaches exactly
    one: the wording as it stood at **your own read point**, because that is the
    only earlier wording the server can still find. Restoring to any other row in
    the history list is **not offered**. The app answers no route that reads a
    document at an arbitrary commit, so a control for it would look like time
    travel and not be one; the panel says so in its own Details, and the gap is
    filed as `converge-4pq`. Only the sentences in this reading can be put back.

Every sentence of that paragraph is now false. converge-4pq landed: `app/serve.py` answers `GET .../docs/{repo}/{doc}?since=<sha>` and takes `since` in an edit's or restore's body, bounded by `snapshot_or_refusal` to commits in that document's own history. Picking any row in the History list reads the document back at that commit and restores the wording that stood there.

converge-4pq's own design field flagged this: "app/README.md ('History: restoring, at four scopes') names converge-4pq as the open gap, so this item's id is load-bearing in shipped documentation and in the screen's own words. Whoever closes this updates both." The screen's words are updated; the README is the half that could not be.

Filed rather than fixed: `app/README.md` is not in lane w8-direction-restore's ownership (app/writes.py, app/serve.py, three JS files, one template, one new test file).

What is true now, for whoever writes the replacement:
- The `now` row is the steward's own reading, not a snapshot — between HEAD and HEAD there is nothing to put back — so the panel on first open is unchanged.
- Reading a snapshot never moves the read point. Looking at history is not reading.
- The bound reads deeper than the eight rows the view shows, because a whole-document restore commits once per sentence and would otherwise push its own snapshot out of range partway through.
- A commit that never touched this document is refused in plain words: "<sha> is not a commit in this document's history. The snapshots this document offers are: …".

Measured against this repository's own docs/VISION.md on a live server, 2026-09-04:

    read at afd83c8b -> 200,  1 sentence(s) restorable
    read at c2420ce3 -> 200, 17 sentence(s) restorable
    read at e1747ba5 -> 200, 40 sentence(s) restorable
    read at deadbeefcafe -> 400, "…is not a commit in this document's history…"
    read point afterwards: afd83c8 (was afd83c8) — UNMOVED
acceptance: GIVEN app/README.md at a commit where converge-4pq has landed WHEN a reader reads "History: restoring, at four scopes" THEN it says restoring reaches any snapshot in the document's own history, AND it no longer says an older snapshot is not offered, AND it no longer names converge-4pq as an open gap.

title: Experience kit rule 14: a body that merely says "voice is not offered" reads as offering voice
description:
Contract: experience.v1 Core 14 ("Where a body genuinely cannot do a thing, it says so in the app") and experience-operation.v1 clause 10 (feedback as text, a screenshot, or voice).

Rule 14 is coarse in BOTH directions, and each half was measured on this tree on 2026-09-04 while closing converge-9mq.

**1. A sentence saying voice is NOT taken reads as an offer.** The kit decides which feedback forms a body offers with FEEDBACK_FORMS — `("voice", re.compile(r"\bvoice\b|audio/\*|MediaRecorder"))` — matched against `served_text(snapshot)`, the shell plus every client asset. It cannot tell an OFFER from a STATEMENT OF ITS ABSENCE. Before converge-9mq, rule 14 reported `cannot_do: ['raise or lower a priority (priority)', 'feedback as voice']`; after adding the Core 14 sentence "a voice note is not recorded here", the word `voice` appears in what the app serves, so the form stops being counted absent at all and rule 14 reports `cannot_do: ['raise or lower a priority (priority)']`. The kit now has no rule that would notice voice going missing, and a body could satisfy the detector by writing the word `voice` in a comment. `<textarea` and `accept="image` are offer-shaped markers; a bare `\bvoice\b` is not.

**2. Any negation near the word counts as saying the limit.** `says_so()` passes if `\bnot\b|\bno\b|cannot|can't|does not|isn't|unavailable|not offered|not yet` appears within 220 chars of the thing's last word. Measured: with the whole limit sentence deleted from `app/templates/shell.html` — "This app has no control that raises or lowers a priority, and answers no route that would write one." — rule 14 still PASSed, satisfied by the surviving heading "Raise or lower a priority - not here". The clause asks for two things ("what the limit is, and what to do instead") and the rule reads only the first, loosely. `app/tests/test_writes_named.py` fences both halves for this body and does fail on that deletion; the kit should too, or the app half is the only thing holding it.

Not this lane's file (`conformance/` is owned elsewhere), so both are filed rather than fixed. A fix probably reads offer-shaped markers only for the forms (`audio/*`, `MediaRecorder`, a file input accepting audio), and asks `says_so` for a statement about the thing plus a second sentence naming what to do instead. The app's real voice gap is converge-rj1 and its real priority gap is converge-a5g; both should stay visible to some rule after this change.
acceptance: GIVEN the experience kit's rule 14 WHEN it is run against a body that merely writes the word voice in prose THEN voice still counts as a form that body does not offer, because only an offer-shaped marker (a control, an audio MIME filter, a recorder) counts as offering it — AND a body that names a limit without naming what to do instead fails, because the clause asks for both halves. Falsified if deleting the app's limit sentence and leaving its heading still passes, or if the app's own voice gap (converge-rj1) and priority gap (converge-a5g) stop being visible to any rule.

title: The vision's lock entry was written as a table row inside a bullet-list changelog, and the app drops it
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 Core 2 (documents render properly — tables among them) and documents.v1 clause 7 (a vision carries a dated changelog whose entries carry evidence).

docs/VISION.md's Changelog is a bullet list. The lock on 2026-09-06 appended its entry as a markdown TABLE ROW instead:

    - **2026-09-03 — v1 (DRAFT), amended.** Principle 8 rewritten …
    - **2026-09-02 — v1 (DRAFT).** From the ratified rules …

    $ uv run conformance/experience-direction/run.py http://127.0.0.1:8788
    [FAIL] 2b  the_render_carries_what_the_documents_contain: the render drops a
               table (source has it, the render does not: ['docs/VISION.md'])
    VERDICT: FAIL  (pass=12 fail=1 skip=0)

Measured on this tree and on a clean checkout of the same commit: the kit fails identically with this lane's changes stashed, so this is not a defect this lane introduced. It arrived with d7d87dd, the lock commit, and nothing caught it — the documents kit's rule 7b only asks that a dated changelog entry exists, and the two bullets above satisfy it.

title: lane-brief genre: an evidence-printing criterion must state the falsity condition, not only the presence condition
description:
Serves documents.v1. Ruled a brief defect (not a lane defect) by converge:protocol-authority, 2026-09-03, on review of lane w4-doc-kit-2's close.

WHAT THE BRIEF SAID

Lane w4-doc-kit-2's acceptance criterion 4 read, verbatim:

  "4. Both items resolved; each stored reason printed via work_list read-back."

WHAT HAPPENED

Both items were resolved and both reasons were printed — so the criterion was met exactly as written. But one of the two stored reasons contained a false paragraph, and the tracker will not let a resolution be corrected once an item closes (filed as work_tracker item work_item_pipeline-03c). The lane superseded the record and disclosed the defect, and the criterion still read PASS.

That produced a genuine, repeated disagreement about whether the lane had met its goal: the criterion's literal text was satisfied while its evident purpose — trustworthy evidence — was not. Under PROTOCOL.md section 7 the literal reading governs, because re-reading a briefed criterion at grading time to mean something stricter is a self-ratified amendment of the brief, which is forbidden to lanes and to the orchestrator alike. So the lane closed as SUCCESS-with-residual, correctly, and the ambiguity survived.

THE DEFECT

PROTOCOL.md section 4 requires a lane brief to carry an honesty gate: name what "not proven" looks like before work starts. Criterion 4 named what ABSENT evidence looks like — a reason not printed — and never named what FALSE evidence looks like. That omission is why the two readings could diverge at all.

THE CHANGE

The lane-brief genre should require that any criterion whose evidence is an artifact the lane itself authors states both conditions:

  - the presence condition: the artifact exists and is shown
  - the falsity condition: what makes the shown artifact unsound, and what the lane must do if it discovers its own artifact is wrong after it is written

Criterion 4 would then have read something closer to: "Both items resolved; each stored reason printed via work_list read-back; if a printed reason is found to be false, the correction must be reachable from the reason itself, not only from a linked item."

Applies to future briefs. It does not regrade w4-doc-kit-2, which finished against the version it was briefed on (PROTOCOL.md section 5).

The skill to change is skills/lane-brief.
acceptance: GIVEN the lane-brief skill WHEN an author writes a criterion whose evidence is an artifact the lane itself produces THEN the skill requires them to state what makes that artifact unsound, alongside what makes it present; AND it says what a lane must do when it finds its own evidence wrong after writing it; AND a worked example shows a criterion written both ways, so an author can see which one survives a lane that made a mistake and caught it.

title: contracts/documents.v1-candidate.md is a ratified, applied and archived proposal still sitting beside the contract it changed
description:
Contract: documents.v1 Core 8 — "A proposal is `<contract>.vN-candidate.md` … The original stays the law until ratified."

The Core 4 proposal against documents.v1 was ratified in round 3 today ("2) ratified", docs/workflow/owner-ratifications-2026-09-06.md), applied to contracts/documents.v1.md (its H1 now reads `amended 2026-09-06`), and archived at docs/workflow/documents.v1-candidate.core4.ratified.md. The working copy in contracts/ was not removed.

Measured on lane/w19-tidy, 2026-09-06:

    $ ls contracts/*-candidate.md
    contracts/documents.v1-candidate.md
    $ diff contracts/documents.v1-candidate.md docs/workflow/documents.v1-candidate.core4.ratified.md
    196a197,198
    > **Ratified 2026-09-06.** Word given on the tidy card: "2) ratified". Applied exactly; ...

So the two files are the same proposal, and the one in contracts/ is the pre-ratification copy. Every other ratified candidate this week was moved out of contracts/ and into docs/workflow/ — composition.v1, experience.v1, and the four experience-* files are all archived and none has a working copy left behind. This one is the exception.

Two costs, both small and both real:

1. A reader opening contracts/ sees an open proposal against documents.v1 that is not open. It is the only candidate file in the folder, so it reads as the one thing waiting for a word.

2. `.githooks/pre-push` lets a push through when the diff carries a sibling `*-candidate.md`. documents.v1 is a DRAFT today so nothing is being held back, but if documents.v1 is ever locked, this leftover keeps that escape hatch open for it without anyone deciding to.

---

CORRECTION, 2026-09-06, BY THE LANE THAT FILED THIS (w19-tidy) — THE FILING SAW ONLY PART OF THE PICTURE, AND THE PART IT MISSED POINTS THE OTHER WAY.

This item was filed against lane/w19-tidy, whose base predates three commits that were already on `main`. One of them is directly about this question:

    $ git log --oneline HEAD..main
    2b64e13 Merge pull request #54 from microsoft/integration/round-3
    c9f2258 the ratified vision candidate stays beside docs/VISION.md: the
            pre-push guard reads the sibling at the tip as the licence for the
            edit it ratified
    353ee89 check record: round 3 — four locks, two proposals applied, queue swept

    $ git show --stat c9f2258
     docs/VISION.md-candidate.md | 156 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

So a ratified candidate being KEPT beside the document it changed is not an oversight on this project — on `main` it is a deliberate act with a stated reason, taken the same day, for `docs/VISION.md`.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION, AND IT IS A QUESTION RATHER THAN A DEFECT. The reason given in c9f2258 is specific to a LOCKED document: the pre-push guard admits an edit to a frozen file only when a sibling candidate rides at the tip, so the candidate has to stay or the ratified edit cannot be pushed at all. `contracts/documents.v1.md` is a DRAFT, and no guard is holding anything back for it, so that reason does not reach it. Which leaves two readings and no way to tell them apart from the tree: the copy beside documents.v1 is a leftover nobody swept, or it is the same practice applied uniformly.

Cost 2 above still stands either way, and is the part worth settling: if documents.v1 is ever locked, whether this file is a licence or a leftover decides whether the guard's escape hatch is open for it on purpose.

WHAT THIS ITEM SHOULD NOT DO: delete the file on the strength of the original filing. That recommendation was made without c9f2258 in view.
acceptance: GIVEN contracts/ and docs/ WHEN a reader finds a `*-candidate.md` beside a document whose proposal has already been ratified THEN the project says in one place which of the two it is — a licence the pre-push guard needs at the tip (c9f2258's reason, for a locked document) or a leftover to sweep — and contracts/documents.v1-candidate.md is disposed of according to that answer. FALSIFIED IF the file is deleted without that answer being written down, or kept with no reason recorded anywhere a reader will find it; and falsified if the answer is written for locked documents only, leaving the draft case exactly as ambiguous as it is today.

title: The adopter proof run against today's tree: both scenarios, ledger rows for Core 14, njaj

title: Two lanes running at once were given the same two files: w8-lock-write and w8-direction-polish
description:
Contract: operation.v1 — Core 6 ("Width is a collision decision"). Ledger row CVG-016.

Found by turnkey step (j) while it ran against this host's W8 wave on 2026-09-04, and reported in its own words:

    Core 6 (CVG-016) FAIL: 2 pair(s) of lanes running at once were given
    overlapping paths: w8-lock-write and w8-direction-polish both own
    'app/static/js/render/direction.js'

Read back from the two briefs in ~/dev/hw-converge/goals/:

- w8-lock-write: "**File ownership — edit ONLY:** `app/writes.py`, `app/serve.py` (one new route), `app/static/js/render/direction.js` (the lock control's call only), `app/static/js/api.js` (one function), `app/tests/test_lock_write.py` (new file only)."
- w8-direction-polish: "**File ownership — edit ONLY:** `app/static/js/render/direction.js`, `app/static/js/actions.js`, `app/static/js/api.js`, `app/static/js/offline.js`, `app/templates/direction.html`, `app/static/css/direction.css`, `app/tests/test_direction_polish.py` (new file only)."

Both live at read time. Two files are declared by both — `app/static/js/render/direction.js` and `app/static/js/api.js` — so the second to merge inherits a conflict, and each lane's own green predates the other's code in exactly the files they share. Clause 6 says lanes fill only with items that provably touch different files, and adjacent items run as one lane.

The narrowing in the first brief ("the lock control's call only") is a plan for how they will not collide, not proof that they did not: clause 6's test is whether the paths are disjoint.

What this needs is a decision, not a code change: merge the two lanes' work in a chosen order with the post-merge gate run afterwards (clause 8), or record why running them at once was the right call.
acceptance: GIVEN two lanes that were live at once with two declared files in common WHEN both have landed THEN the plan record says which order they were merged in and that the post-merge gate ran on the pair, or records why the overlap was accepted; AND a re-run of turnkey step (j) against this workspace no longer reports a live pair sharing a path.

title: app/static/dev/verify.py asserts the console footer says "read-only in this version" — that wording is gone
description:
Contract: experience-console.v1 Core 9.

Discovered while closing converge-55b. `app/static/dev/verify.py` is outside lane w8-hygiene's file ownership, so this is filed rather than fixed.

WHAT IS THERE, `app/static/dev/verify.py:108`:

    check(f"[{view}] read-only note visible", "read-only in this version" in page.text_content(".console-footer"))

WHAT CHANGED UNDER IT. converge-55b replaced that wording in both places it is produced:
- `app/templates/console.html` now serves `not a chat — this pane is the manager session itself`;
- `app/static/js/render/console.js` sets the same string when a manager session is attached, and `not a chat — no manager session on the other end to type into` when one is not. Neither state says "read-only in this version" any more, because the app has taken keystrokes since converge-tfu.

So this assertion now fails for a page that is correct. It is a dev script driven against `app/static/dev/stub_server.py` by hand, not part of `app/tests`, so nothing in the suite caught it — `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests` is 153 passed / 88 skipped with the new wording in place.

THE FIX, one line: assert on `not a chat` instead — the words rule 9's own regex looks for, and the words both live states now carry. Checking for the *claim* rather than one exact sentence also stops this assertion from breaking the next time the wording is tuned.

Worth a glance while there: the same file's other console assertions were written against the read-only era and may make the same assumption.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS ITEM: grep for "read-only in this version" in `app/static/dev/` returning nothing.
acceptance: GIVEN app/static/dev/verify.py driven against app/static/dev/stub_server.py WHEN its console checks run against the current markup THEN they pass — the footer assertion looks for "not a chat" rather than "read-only in this version", and no assertion in that file expects the read-only wording.

title: This repository's own .gitignore does not carry the .converge/ line its workspace template now ships
description:
Contract: documents.v1 §13 — "Converge is self-hosting … its own repository passes the same kit."

Found 2026-09-05 on lane/w9-where-it-starts while closing converge-36vm. The lane added docs/workspace-template/gitignore-addendum.txt, whose one line is `.converge/`, and modes/converge-manager.md clause 5 now says a manager session's record and lanes live at <workspace>/.converge/<manager-id>/ and that the workspace git-ignores that directory.

A project with no workspace around it has its repository root AS the workspace root, so `.converge/` can appear inside this repository itself. This repository's own .gitignore does not carry the line:

    $ cat .gitignore
    .DS_Store
    ._*
    __pycache__/
    .venv/
    uv.lock
    !modules/hooks-candidate-guard/uv.lock

So the repository ships a template line it does not itself apply, which is the self-hosting gap clause 13 names. The fix is one line appended to .gitignore. It was left undone because the root .gitignore is outside lane/w9-where-it-starts's file ownership, which named only modes/, context/manager/, README.md, docs/workspace-template/ and AGENTS.md.

Cost if left: a manager session run against this repository directly (no workspace manifest above it) leaves an untracked .converge/ directory of worktrees and logs showing in every `git status`, and the first person to see it will not know whether it is content.
acceptance: Given this repository's .gitignore, when a manager session creates .converge/ at the repository root, then `git status --short` shows nothing from it — the ignore line is present and matches the line shipped in docs/workspace-template/gitignore-addendum.txt. Kept when both files carry the same line and the status output is empty; not yet while .gitignore lacks it.

title: infra_ledger.sh has no way to mark a registered server stopped, so every finished lane leaves an "open" row
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 5 (lanes are real sessions, launched through the parallel-lane tooling) — named because the infra ledger is part of that tooling and no contract in contracts/ holds the highway script itself; today it cannot record that a lane's server was stopped, so a reader cannot tell a live server from a dead row.

Found while finishing lane w8-tag-candidates (work item converge-er6).

The ten-lane-highway skill's `infra_ledger.sh` accepts `add|list|sweep` and nothing else. A lane is told to register its server on start and stop it before DONE, but there is no verb that records "stopped". Measured 2026-09-04:

    $ infra_ledger.sh <batch> done server w8-tag-candidates-app-8811
    ERROR: unknown command 'done' (want: add|list|sweep)

So `list` shows seven rows all marked `open`, six of them from lanes that have already finished and whose processes are gone. My own row reads `kill 2821616` and 2821616 no longer exists:

    2026-09-04T09:26:20Z  server  w8-examples-app-8811              open  kill 3066868
    2026-09-04T11:55:58Z  server  w8-tag-candidates-app-8811        open  kill 2821616

Two costs, both real. A reader cannot tell a live server from a dead row, which is the one question the ledger exists to answer. And a stale row carries a bare PID as its destroy command — PIDs are recycled, so acting on an old row can kill an unrelated process.

`sweep` may already be the intended answer, but it is undocumented at the call site and a lane cannot run it safely: it is not obvious whether it would touch other lanes' live servers, so the cautious lane leaves the row instead. Whatever the fix is — a `done`/`close` verb, or `sweep` documented as safe and called by the lane — the lane instructions in the ten-lane-highway skill should name it, because today they say "stop it before DONE" and give no way to say so.

Outside this lane's file ownership (contracts/*-candidate.md only), and outside this repository — the script lives in the installed amplifier app-cli skill data.
acceptance: GIVEN a lane has registered a server with `infra_ledger.sh add server <id> "kill <pid>"` WHEN the lane stops that server and records it THEN `infra_ledger.sh list` shows the row as no longer open, AND the ten-lane-highway lane instructions name the exact command that does it.

title: Rule 8a reads the steward KEY, not its value — an unfinished registration still passes
description:
Contract: experience-collaboration.v1 Core 8 (one steward per manager session, settled when the session is registered, not inferred from whoever is looking) — the check that guards it reads the steward key and never its value, so a registration naming nobody reports the promise kept.

`conformance/experience-collaboration/run.py`'s `check_one_steward` finds a steward with

    named = [m.get("id") for m in managers if any(STEWARD_FIELD.search(k) for k in m)]

which tests the manager card's KEYS for /steward/i and never looks at what the key says. Since converge-9ox, `app/data.py`'s `manager_payload` always carries `"steward"` — a name when the `[[managers]]` block registered one, and an empty string when it did not, which is the honest payload shape (a reader can tell "nobody named" from "key missing", and it is never the signed-in reader's name).

The consequence is that a manager session whose registration names NOBODY now satisfies rule 8a. Measured on 2026-09-04 against a real app whose block carries no `steward` line:

    /api/boot (nobody named): user='tester' manager[0].steward=''
    8a PASS  (nobody named) 1 manager session(s) each name exactly one steward, settled at registration

The app is answering correctly there — the empty string IS "nobody is registered". It is the check that cannot tell the two apart, so it reports a promise kept that is not.

The fix is one line in the kit: read the value, not just the key —

    named = [m.get("id") for m in managers
             if any(STEWARD_FIELD.search(k) and str(m[k]).strip() for k in m)]

and the same for the `snapshot.manager()` branch below it, which today searches the joined KEY NAMES of the manager card (`" ".join(manager)`) and has the same blindness.

`conformance/` is not lane w8-steward-name's file to edit, so this is filed rather than made. `app/tests/test_steward_name.py::test_rule_8a_reads_the_key_and_not_its_value` characterises the current behaviour and its docstring says to delete it along with this item.
acceptance: GIVEN a manager card carrying `steward: ""` (a `[[managers]]` block with no `steward` line) WHEN `uv run conformance/experience-collaboration/run.py <app>` is run THEN rule 8a FAILs, reading that no manager session names a steward; AND GIVEN a card carrying `steward: "wren"` THEN 8a still PASSes; AND `app/tests/test_steward_name.py::test_rule_8a_reads_the_key_and_not_its_value` is deleted rather than left asserting the old bar.

title: experience.v1 Core 4, second half: ten routes beyond the five write something
description:
Contract: experience.v1 Core 4 — "Exactly five writes. … Nothing else, in any body, writes anything."

Measured 2026-09-04 by `uv run conformance/experience/run.py http://127.0.0.1:8788` (ledger row CVG-103, converge-yjn):

    [FAIL] 4b  10 route(s) beyond the five write something:
               /api/collab/webhooks/host, /api/collab/{mid}/pulls/{number}/answer,
               /api/collab/{mid}/pulls/{number}/comments,
               /api/managers/{mid}/docs/{repo}/{doc}/changes/{id}/edit,
               .../keep, .../restore, .../lock, .../read,
               /api/managers/{mid}/presence, /api/managers/{mid}/presence/queue

The kit names the disagreement precisely, and it is not the app's to settle alone: editing, restoring and per-change choices are experience-direction.v1 clauses 5, 6 and 8 — i.e. section contracts in the same family ASK for writes the umbrella's Core 4 says may not exist. The read point is the umbrella's own open question (ledger row CVG-106 / converge-71q). The collaboration routes and the lock are named by no contract at all (the umbrella's rule 12 fails on six of them; converge-slpj holds that).

So this is a contract-vs-contract disagreement inside one family, and the steward's word is what settles it. Three shapes it could take, none of which a lane should pick unilaterally:
  1. Core 4 is amended to name the section contracts' writes (a CANDIDATE amendment against a frozen clause).
  2. The section contracts' writes are withdrawn from the app.
  3. Core 4 is read as "five writes the STEWARD makes", with document mechanics set aside — which is a reading change, and therefore still an amendment.

converge-a5g holds the other half of Core 4 (the absent `priority` write). This item holds only the surplus. Both must land before ledger row CVG-103 can go green.
acceptance: GIVEN the app is running WHEN `uv run conformance/experience/run.py <app>` is run THEN rule 4b passes — no route beyond the writes the family's contracts name writes anything — OR a ratified amendment records the steward's settled reading, and ledger row CVG-103's assertion is re-derived against that run.

title: verify.py's live-work tripwire reads a stale export, and reported green over 28 red rows citing resolved items
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §8 — "Integrate, verify, re-check … then the contract check, before the next brief." The contract check here is the ledger, and `docs/LEDGER-FORMAT.md` §2 and §6.3 say every row that reads Not yet or Broken must carry a LIVE work ref.

MEASURED 2026-09-04 by a scheduled reconcile against target-repo @ a5c6c02.

`ledger/checks/verify.py:101` reads `docs/work-items.json`. That export holds **76 items** (mtime 2026-09-04T07:51:12). The live queue holds **202** (28 open · 0 held · 4 deferred · 170 resolved). The tripwire is therefore judging a snapshot, and it printed:

    [OK  ] no GAP/VIOLATION row cites a resolved work item (46 red rows read against docs/work-items.json)

That is a false green. Resolved against the LIVE queue instead, every one of the 11 distinct refs cited by the rows that remain red after this run is already closed:

    REF              EXPORT SAYS    LIVE QUEUE
    converge-2ro     ABSENT         resolved
    converge-f1l     open           resolved
    converge-6mi     ABSENT         resolved
    converge-jdm     open           resolved
    converge-lwa     open           resolved
    converge-7ym     ABSENT         resolved
    converge-8er     ABSENT         resolved
    converge-do8     ABSENT         resolved
    converge-d3n     open           resolved
    converge-tfu     open           resolved
    converge-719     open           resolved

Six read `open` in the export and are closed live. Five are ABSENT from the export entirely — and verify.py reports an absent id as [INFO], not a failure, so those five could never have failed this rule no matter how stale they got.

28 red rows are affected: CVG-008, 009, 012, 013, 014, 016, 017, 018, 019, 020, 021, 022, 023, 038, 104, 107, 108, 112, 113, 114, 122, 130, 141, 142, 143, 162, 201, 210.

Note the arithmetic: the ledger currently holds 46 red rows, and 18 of them turn out to be un-drifted (their named defect is fixed and the kit now passes) — so the true count of red-rows-citing-dead-work is 28, not 46. Both numbers are wrong in the export's telling, which reported zero.

converge-vtnm names this same defect at a measured scope of three rows. The scope is 28, and the cause is the export, not the three rows.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE 28 ROWS: this is the tripwire whose whole purpose is to stop a reader following a cite into finished work. It was added on 2026-09-04 by converge-0gb precisely because the rule had been enforced by hand three times. It now cannot fire, because the file it reads is refreshed by a separate manual command (`uv run scripts/export-work-items.py`) that nothing in the gate runs. Until this is fixed the ratchet will keep reporting green over exactly this failure.
acceptance: GIVEN a red ledger row whose work ref is resolved in the live queue WHEN `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` runs THEN that row FAILS the live-work tripwire by name; AND an id the checker cannot resolve at all is not silently downgraded to [INFO]; AND the check does not depend on a manually-refreshed snapshot being current, or the gate refreshes it itself before reading it.

title: Locking a document rewrites lines below the H1, and a check written for the old behaviour now fails

  Left contains 4 more items, first extra item: ''
