That is what wave 13's "the freeze is one edit: a lock and its record land together or not at all" (6eb550b) deliberately changed - the H1 stamp and the Changelog entry now land in the same write, because split across two the second is refused. The behaviour is the one that was chosen; the check still asserts the behaviour it replaced.

So one of the two is wrong and it is a judgment, not a typo: either the check should assert "the H1 is stamped AND exactly one Changelog entry is appended, and nothing else moves", or the write should stop appending. The rest of the app suite is green (458 passed, 1 failed, playwright installed).

Files: app/tests/test_direction_final.py and whichever of app/writes.py does the lock write. Neither is in lane w14-registration's ownership.
acceptance: GIVEN the app test suite with playwright available THEN test_direction_final.py::test_locking_stamps_the_document_and_says_so passes; AND the check it makes describes the freeze-is-one-edit behaviour that shipped, naming both the H1 stamp and the changelog entry, rather than asserting nothing below the H1 may move.

title: Direction: no lock gate, one copy control, no zoom
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 §3, §11.

Measured 2026-09-03 by `uv run conformance/experience-direction/run.py http://127.0.0.1:8788`:

- rule 11 FAIL — no lock control, and none of the four conditions appears anywhere the app serves. Nothing gates a document being locked, and a steward reading a DRAFT contract is never shown why it is not yet lockable. `grep -rniE "\block\b|freeze" app/templates app/static/js` returns nothing.
- rule 3 FAIL — the clause names five reader abilities: copy as rendered, copy as source, download the source, zoom, and page width or full screen. The app offers one copy control (`#copyRendered`, which in fact copies the *source* — `copyText(data.doc.raw)`), download and width. There is no zoom, and the two copy abilities are not distinguishable.

Note: rule 3 counts copy controls rather than matching them by id, precisely because a single control called `copyRendered` cannot stand for both abilities.

Owner: whoever owns `app/`. This lane owns `ledger/` and `conformance/` only.

Ledger rows this closes: CVG-122, CVG-130, CVG-201. Grouped by cause and component on 2026-09-04 by docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md, which is where the whole mapping of rows to items is printed. The rows already named this item as their fix; what was missing was the list, written down here.
acceptance: GIVEN the running app WHEN `conformance/experience-direction/run.py <app>` runs THEN rules 3 and 11 report PASS: two copy controls plus download, zoom and width; and a lock gate stating all four Freeze Bar conditions with a control beside them whose state tracks them.

title: Five of six proposal files carry no `target:` line, so the guard cannot unlock the contract they amend
description:
Contract: composition.v1 §7

`modules/hooks-candidate-guard/amplifier_module_hooks_candidate_guard/guard.py:464-498`
(`_find_ratified_candidate`) requires two things of a proposal before it will let a
write through to the locked contract it amends: a `target:` line naming that
contract (read by `_extract_field`, guard.py:455-461, regex `^target:\s*(.+?)\s*$`),
and the steward's ratified stamp. Its own docstring says so in as many words: "The
`target:` line is required under BOTH names: the guard never infers which contract a
proposal amends from its filename alone."

Measured on this tree, 2026-09-05:

    $ for f in contracts/*-candidate.md; do grep -qiE '^target:[[:space:]]*.+' "$f" \
        && echo "HAS target: $f" || echo "no target: $f"; done
    HAS target: contracts/composition.v1-candidate.md
    no target: contracts/experience-collaboration.v1-candidate.md
    no target: contracts/experience-console.v1-candidate.md
    no target: contracts/experience-direction.v1-candidate.md
    no target: contracts/experience-operation.v1-candidate.md
    no target: contracts/experience.v1-candidate.md

Five of the six carry no such line. Nothing catches this today: every contract in
`contracts/` is a draft, so the guard is not yet refusing writes to any of them, and
neither `conformance/documents/run.py` rule 8 (which checks the three parts) nor
`conformance/composition/run.py` rule 7 (which checks the guard's own config) reads
a proposal for its target line. The bite arrives later, at exactly the wrong moment:
the day one of those contracts is locked and its proposal is ratified, the guard will
not find the proposal, and the ratified change cannot be applied through the sanctioned
escape hatch.

The fix is one line per file plus, so it does not drift back, a check that reads it.
`skills/proposing-a-change/SKILL.md` already tells an author to write the line
("Name the file it targets in one line at the top"); nothing verifies they did.

Found while writing `contracts/composition.v1-candidate.md` for converge-279a, which
carries the line.
acceptance: Given the five proposal files that carry no `target:` line, when each names the contract it amends on a line the guard's `_extract_field` can read, then a check in the repository's own kit reads every proposal for that line and says plainly whether it is there — kept when all of them carry it, not yet while any is missing. Given that check exists, when a new proposal is written without the line, then the check says not yet rather than staying quiet. What would falsify this: the guard resolving a proposal to its contract with no `target:` line present, or the check passing on a tree where one is absent.

title: The webhook's shared secret is a plain header, not the HMAC over the body that GitHub actually sends
description:
Contract: experience-collaboration.v1 Core 6 — webhooks where the host offers them, polling as the honest fallback.

converge-7cs made `/api/collab/webhooks/host` reachable without a cookie, so the route's own shared-secret check is now the ONLY thing standing between the open internet and that write. That raises the bar the check has to clear, and today it does not clear GitHub's.

What ships: `app/collab.py` reads a secret from `~/.amplifier/converge-app.webhook-secret` and compares it to an `X-Converge-Secret` header with `!=`. What GitHub actually sends is `X-Hub-Signature-256` — an HMAC-SHA256 over the request body, keyed with the secret. A GitHub webhook configured against this app would carry no `X-Converge-Secret` at all and be refused 403, so the door is open but GitHub cannot walk through it. Any host that can be told to send an arbitrary header can; GitHub cannot.

Two things to settle, and both are the steward's:
- whether to accept `X-Hub-Signature-256` (HMAC over the body, compared with `hmac.compare_digest`) as well as or instead of the plain header. HMAC also fixes two smaller things for free: the comparison stops being timing-variable, and the signature covers the body, so a captured header cannot be replayed against a different payload.
- whether the plain header stays for hosts that are not GitHub.

Named in converge-7cs's own description as one of two things "worth deciding at the same time"; filed here so it is not lost with that item.
acceptance: GIVEN a GitHub webhook configured with the shared secret WHEN it POSTs to /api/collab/webhooks/host carrying only X-Hub-Signature-256 THEN it is accepted, the signature is verified over the body with a constant-time comparison, and a request whose body has been altered after signing is refused.

title: A refused ask still blames the missing route: actions.js says "this app answers no proposal route yet" and names converge-ddt
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 §9.

`app/static/js/actions.js:413` (the catch in `sendAsk`) says:

    toast(`Nothing was asked — this app answers no proposal route yet (${err.message}). Filed as converge-ddt.`);

converge-ddt landed. The route exists and answers. So every refusal now blames a
gap that is closed and names work that is done, while carrying the real reason
in parentheses where it reads like a detail.

Measured 2026-09-04, driving a real browser against the real app (an ask sent at
a scope the server does not accept):

    the app said when the write was refused: Nothing was asked — this app answers
    no proposal route yet (an ask covers one of all, document, paragraph — not
    sideways). Filed as converge-ddt.

The refusal itself is honest in the way that matters — it claims no proposal,
and nothing was written (proposal byte-identical, document byte-identical,
working tree unchanged, all verified) — so this is a wording defect, not a
silent-failure one. The fix is to lead with the server's own sentence and drop
the converge-ddt attribution.

Filed rather than fixed: `app/static/js/actions.js` is outside this lane's file
ownership (lane w8-ask-test owns only
`app/tests/test_direction_writes_rendered.py`).

The rewritten ask test deliberately does NOT pin this sentence — it asserts that
the refusal carries the server's reason and does not claim a proposal — so
correcting the wording will not turn that test red.
acceptance: GIVEN an ask the server refuses WHEN the screen reports it THEN the message leads with the reason the server gave, and names no work item that has already landed.

title: operation.v1 has no clause for a project's first wake, so nothing can key a path from a blank repository
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §1

All thirteen clauses govern a project already under way: derive from a contract gap (§1), show the plan (§2), fill lanes (§6), re-run the check (§7), brief on return (§10). None covers the first wake — drafting a vision, deriving the first contracts, seeding the ledger, or adopting a repository that already has code.

The consequence is visible in the mode. modes/converge-manager.md:293 heads its operating loop "on every wake" and starts at heartbeat, then status, then refill to width — every step presupposing contracts, a ledger, a queue and a lane width that a new project does not have. Clause 1 then forbids improvising: "If you cannot name the contract, you do not have a work item — you have an opinion" (modes/converge-manager.md:42-50). On a blank repository there are no contracts, so a conforming manager session correctly does nothing.

This is not a mode defect. The mode is keyed clause by clause to this contract and states that it adds nothing a clause does not say (modes/converge-manager.md:35-37). Writing a day-one section into the mode without a clause behind it would break that rule. So the clause has to come first.

This is a steward's decision, not a lane's work: it is a change to a contract, which reaches the steward as a ratify call.

Found by the onboarding audit, docs/workflow/ONBOARDING-AUDIT-2026-09-04.md, findings c-3, c-4, and "Two things no contract covers", 2.
acceptance: Given a steward reading operation.v1, when they reach the clause list, then one clause says what a manager session does on a project that has no contracts yet — for a blank repository and for a repository that already has code — and says where its work comes from when no gap exists to derive from. Given that clause exists, when someone reads modes/converge-manager.md, then a first-wake section is keyed to it, so the mode still adds nothing its contract does not say.

title: W7 turnkey: a fresh DTU, one --app install, a manager session that is not me runs two real lanes
description: Contract: operation.v1 'Conformance kit asserts — Turnkey' (RED today) and §5, §12. The operation half has never run end-to-end through Converge without this session driving it by hand. Make evaluations/turnkey/ green or leave it honestly red with each failing step named: fresh DTU (amplifier-digital-twin profile under evaluations/turnkey/), the Gitea mirror re-synced to origin/main first (amplifier-gitea mirror-from-github <instance-id> --github-repo … ; the CLI wants the instance ID, not its name), one 'amplifier bundle add …behaviors/converge.yaml --app', scripts/install-check.py green, then a headless 'amplifier run' under the converge-manager mode against a fixture project (a small repo with a vision, two contracts, and a deliberate gap) that must: derive items into a work-tracker project, show the plan, launch two REAL lanes (tmux -L <socket> sessions + worktrees, verified from outside), judge by evidence, integrate, re-check the contracts, and write a return brief. Every step PASS/FAIL/SKIP with the evidence it read (RESULT.md). Fix what is fixable inside the mode/scripts/install-check; anything else becomes a named residual.
acceptance: GIVEN a fresh DTU WHEN evaluations/turnkey/run.sh runs THEN RESULT.md shows each of the nine steps with a verdict and evidence; lanes are proven as tmux sessions + worktrees from outside the manager session; no work item was held by an in-session sub-agent; the ledger re-check ran; a return brief exists — and the overall verdict is GREEN, or RED with every red step naming its cause.

title: candidate-guard does not honor the new proposal name <contract>.vN-candidate.md
description:
documents.v1 §8 (ratified DRAFT) names the proposal artifact `<contract>.vN-candidate.md`. W1 rewrote skills/candidate-amendment and agents/amendment-drafter to instruct that name (legacy CANDIDATE-*.md still described as honored).

hooks-candidate-guard's defaults today match ONLY the legacy name. In modules/hooks-candidate-guard/amplifier_module_hooks_candidate_guard/guard.py:
  - line 65:  always_allow_globs default = ["**/CANDIDATE-*.md"]
  - line 101: candidate_glob      default = ["**/CANDIDATE-*.md"]
  - line 441: the denial message tells the author to write "CANDIDATE-<topic>.md"

Consequence, both directions: writing `contracts/foo.v1-candidate.md` beside a locked contract is not covered by always_allow_globs, and a ratified proposal under the new name is invisible to the escape hatch (_find_ratified_candidate), so the ratified change can never land. The agents and skills now point authors at a name the guard does not recognize.

modules/ is outside W1's file ownership (skills/** and agents/** content only), so this was not fixed in-lane.
acceptance:
GIVEN a locked contract contracts/foo.v1.md
WHEN an author writes the sibling proposal contracts/foo.v1-candidate.md
THEN the guard allows the write (always_allow_globs covers both the new and the legacy name)
AND GIVEN that proposal carries a target: line and the steward's ratified stamp
WHEN the locked contract is then edited
THEN the escape hatch finds the ratified proposal under the new name and allows the edit
AND the denial message names `<contract>.vN-candidate.md` as the form to write.

title: W3 upstream + mirror: highway skill feedback filed; Gitea mirror re-synced
description: Contract: operation.v1 §5–6 (real lanes, width) and §12 (dependencies). Close-out: file upstream highway-skill feedback (refill enforcement, .width truth, the false 'todo board is the dashboard' claim, marker-outside-worktree, launcher refuses already-held items) with session evidence; re-sync the Gitea mirror used by the evaluations to origin/main.

title: Guard does not cover `amplifier tool invoke` — direct CLI dispatch bypasses tool:pre
description:
Observed 2026-09-02 while probing the candidate-guard for converge-1tx.

In a scratch repo holding a FROZEN `contracts/probe.v1.md`, running
`amplifier tool invoke write_file file_path=contracts/probe.v1.md content='hijacked' -b converge`
reported "Bundle 'converge' prepared successfully" and then WROTE the file
(8 bytes). The same module's `evaluate_tool_pre()`, called directly on the
byte-identical input against the same fixture, returns action="deny".

So the pure guard logic is correct; the gap is that direct CLI tool dispatch
appears to run outside the `tool:pre` hook pipeline the guard registers on.
This weakens composition.v1 clause 7 ("refuses every other write to a locked
contract, by person or agent") on that path.

Not fixed here: the hook module owns no wiring, and the cause is plausibly an
upstream app-CLI property (hooks are session-scoped) rather than a bundle
defect. Documented as non-coverage in modules/hooks-candidate-guard/README.md
"Known gaps".

Note for whoever picks this up: the shared `converge` bundle registration
points at a concurrent lane's worktree and flipped from present to absent
mid-session, so re-probing needs its own stable registration.
acceptance: GIVEN a repo with a FROZEN contracts/x.v1.md and the converge bundle composed WHEN `amplifier tool invoke write_file file_path=contracts/x.v1.md content=...` runs THEN the write is denied by the candidate guard, OR the non-coverage is confirmed as intended upstream behavior and recorded as such in the spec's §2.9 threat notes.

title: composition.v1's new kit-assert bullet has no kit rule and no ledger row
description:
Contract: composition.v1 §Conformance kit asserts, bullet 5 — the bullet the steward's ratified Core 4 amendment added says the kit asserts something the kit does not assert, and no ledger row covers it either.

The amendment (PR #25, commit 0b00fda, steward's word "ratified, and go ahead w/ that PR, merge it") added this bullet to composition.v1's "Conformance kit asserts" list:

    A step that declares its own helpers resolves them from that closure, not
    from the calling session: the recipe validates at `schema_version: 2` and its
    plan names every helper against the dependency that supplies it.

Found 2026-09-04 by the mandatory SYNC re-review in converge-g82 (LEDGER-FORMAT section 4), which is the only thing that looks at newly added contract text — the quote tripwire cannot see a promise nobody wrote a row for, and nothing looks wrong.

Two halves are missing, and they are different asks:

1. No kit rule. conformance/composition/run.py's rule table runs 1a-7b. Rule 4 was rewritten in the same commit to follow the amended Core 4, but it reads only README.md's host sentence; nothing in the kit reads recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml or runs the recipe runner. So the sentence "the kit asserts this" is not true today.

2. No ledger row. composition.v1's other kit-assert bullets carry rows (CVG-008 for bullet 2, CVG-009 and CVG-071 for bullet 3). Bullet 5 has none, which is the same invisible gap converge-bv7 wrote CVG-071 for: a missing row looks exactly like a kept promise.

The FACT the bullet describes does hold on this host, measured 2026-09-04 from the repository root:

    $ recipe-runner validate recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml
    status: ok
    schema_version: 2

    $ recipe-runner plan recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml
    dependencies (2):
      - ...amplifier-foundation@main#subdirectory=bundles/anchors/bundle.md [bundle]
      - ...amplifier-bundle-converge@v0.1.0#subdirectory=behaviors/converge.yaml [behavior]
    agents (12): each named against the dependency that supplies it

So this is not a broken promise about the recipe; it is a promise nobody checks.

One design call belongs to whoever takes this, and is why the row was filed rather than written during the reconcile: `recipe-runner plan` resolves its dependencies, which can mean a network fetch on a cold cache. A ledger probe or kit rule that needs the network makes the whole gate flaky on a fresh checkout. Both halves are answerable offline if the check is written carefully — `validate` alone is local and fast (0.27s measured) — and whether that is enough to assert the bullet is the judgment being asked for.

Filed by lane w9-reconcile-4. conformance/composition/ is not this lane's file, and adding the ledger row without settling the network question would have put a possibly-flaky probe into a gate that had just been made green.
acceptance: Given composition.v1's Conformance kit asserts list, whose last bullet says a step that declares its own helpers resolves them from that closure, when the composition kit is run against this repository, then some rule in it reads the recipe and reports on that bullet rather than the list containing a promise the kit never checks; and the conformance ledger carries a row for that bullet, as it does for the other bullets in the same list, with a disposition earned by running the check and not by reading this item; and the row's assertion still answers the same way on a checkout with no network access, or the row says in plain words that it does not.

title: Documents: contract clause 4 is silent on whether a contract may carry an EXTRA section
description:
Surfaced while building the documents.v1 conformance kit — an interpretive gap the kit refused to decide on the steward's behalf.

documents.v1 Core 4 says: "The same sections, in the same order, every time. Purpose -> Core (the teeth) -> What v1 deliberately does NOT freeze (with promotion triggers) -> Conformance kit asserts -> Reserved / open questions -> Changelog only if amended."

It fixes PRESENCE and ORDER. It does not say whether a SEVENTH section is permitted.

contracts/operation.v1.md carries one: "## Declared dependencies (checked at install)", between Core and "What v1 deliberately does NOT freeze".

Two readings, both defensible:
  (a) "the same sections ... every time" fixes the SET — an extra section is a violation, and operation.v1 should fold that content into an existing section.
  (b) The clause fixes order and required presence only — an extra section is fine, and the kit should stay quiet.

The kit implements neither ruling. Rule 1b asserts only what the contract unambiguously fixes (presence and order) and REPORTS any extra section in the row's detail, so the fact is visible without inventing a rule:

  contracts/operation.v1.md -> all five required sections, in order
    (also carries: ['Declared dependencies (checked at install)'])

Deciding this is a documents.v1 amendment (a clarifying sentence in clause 4), not a code change. If reading (a) wins, rule 1b tightens to fail an extra section and operation.v1 needs an edit; if (b) wins, clause 4 should say so explicitly so the next reader does not re-derive this question.

Reproduce:
  uv run conformance/documents/run.py . --json-only | python3 -c "import json,sys;[print(f['file'],'->',f['detail']) for x in json.load(sys.stdin)['results'] if x['rule']=='1b' for f in x['files']]"
acceptance: GIVEN documents.v1 clause 4 WHEN a reader asks "may a contract carry a section beyond the six listed?" THEN the clause answers it in one sentence — and if the answer is no, conformance/documents rule 1b fails an extra section and contracts/operation.v1.md no longer carries one.

title: One lane state word is off the contract's vocabulary (experience.v1 Core 6, kit rule 6a)
description: Contract: experience.v1 Core 6 (the app serves state words only from the three fixed vocabularies: contracts Kept · Not yet · Broken · Pinned open · Can't check; work Truly ready · Waiting on you · Working · Stuck · Done; lanes Working · Quiet · Silent). The umbrella kit's rule 6a reads FAIL on the app: a lane's state is served as 'Silent — may have died' (1×), which is not in the vocabulary as the kit reads it. Decide from the contract's own words which form is the vocabulary (the mode and earlier tests wrote 'Silent, may have died'; the contract's Core 6 list is the authority — quote it) and make app/data.py's LANE_WORD, the four test modules that assert the phrase, the experience-operation kit and the mode's vocabulary line agree with the contract; if the contract itself carries the long form, make the kit read it that way instead and say so. Rule 6a must PASS on the app afterwards.
acceptance: GIVEN uv run conformance/experience/run.py http://127.0.0.1:8788 --cookie <c> THEN rule 6a PASS; GIVEN app/tests THEN green; GIVEN the experience-operation kit THEN PASS; GIVEN grep for the old phrase across app/, conformance/, modes/, context/ THEN one form remains everywhere; GIVEN git diff --stat THEN only the named paths.

title: The ledger self-check exits 1 at HEAD on four rows, and did not on 2026-09-06
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §8 — integrate, verify, re-check.

`uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` exits 1 on this tree at commit 1323788. Four failures:

  CVG-066 expect NOT met (exit=0, stdout='SURFACE-RULE-8C-NOT-ASSERTED-AGAINST-THE-APP')
  CVG-038 expect NOT met (exit=1, stdout='', stderr='')
  CVG-057 expect NOT met (exit=0, stdout='SURFACE-STATE-VOCABULARY=8-OF-8 PAGE-WALK-ASSERTED=0')
  every indexed ref path exists on disk ([('CVG-039', 'tests/test_renders_at_both_widths.py')])

Everything above them passes: 179 rows, all fifteen contract hashes in sync, 178 of 178 quotes verifying byte-for-byte, the five red rows read against the live queue.

Two facts about when this started. Commit d45918a (2026-09-06) reports "ALL LEDGER SELF-CHECKS PASS (179 rows)" in its own message, and PINS.md records the same at 175 rows on 2026-09-05. So this is a regression that arrived at or after wave 16, not a long-standing gap.

It was not caused by lane w17. Run with and without that lane's two new files, the verify output is byte-identical; both are markdown proposals no ledger row references. ledger/ was outside that lane's ownership, so this is filed rather than touched.

CVG-039's ref is the simplest of the four: it names tests/test_renders_at_both_widths.py, which is not on disk. Note also that `pytest tests/` reports 137 passed and 1 skipped here, where d45918a reports 187 passed — worth checking whether the same removal explains both.

GIVEN each of CVG-066, CVG-038, CVG-057 and CVG-039 THEN either the row is re-derived against what is actually true now, or the thing it asserts is repaired — never the check weakened to make it green. Falsified by a row whose expectation was relaxed rather than re-read.

title: Operation: the plan, the brief and the timeline do not carry their reasons or their parts
description:
Contract: experience-operation.v1 §2, §3, §4.

Measured 2026-09-03 by `uv run conformance/experience-operation/run.py http://127.0.0.1:8788`:

- rule 2b FAIL — all 11 waves carry no reason. Every wave's `title` is its own lane names joined by commas ("w1-composition, w1-guard, w1-documents"), which is a list of members, not a statement of what the batch is for. Nothing shows why the plan was redrawn either.

Ledger rows this closes: CVG-141, CVG-142, CVG-143. Grouped by cause and component on 2026-09-04 by docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md, which is where the whole mapping of rows to items is printed. The rows already named this item as their fix; what was missing was the list, written down here.

title: Steward decision: one word on the composition.v1 Core 4 amendment (contracts/composition.v1-candidate.md)
description:
Contract: composition.v1 Core 4, its "What v1 deliberately does NOT freeze" list, and its conformance-kit asserts.

The proposal is written and sitting in `contracts/composition.v1-candidate.md` (converge-qwk, 2026-09-04). What is left is not work — it is a decision, and AGENTS.md rule 4 reserves it to the intent steward. This item exists so that decision stays visible in the queue instead of disappearing with the lane that wrote the proposal.

THE DECISION, in one sentence: may an automated step declare the closure it resolves its helpers from, rather than only using helpers already present in the session it runs in?

THE OPTIONS AND WHAT EACH COSTS:

- **ratified** — Core 4's second sentence names the two cases; the "Automated steps that bring their own helpers - when the engine supports it" line leaves the not-frozen list; one assert is added. Then `conformance/composition/run.py` rule 4's HOST_SENTENCE_TESTS must be updated to read the new claim, and README.md's host-requirement sentence restated to match. Until that kit change lands, rule 4 asserts a sentence the contract no longer says.
- **ratified with edits** — same, with the steward's wording.
- **declined** — composition.v1 stands. README.md keeps the sentence it has now, which names the clause as unamended (converge-yj3), and the recipe keeps working in a way the contract does not describe. That gap stays open and honest rather than closing.
- **later** — same as declined for now; the candidate stays where it is.

RECOMMENDED: **ratified**. The condition the not-frozen list itself set - "when the engine supports it" - has been met and reproduced on this tree twice, by two different tools, on 2026-09-04. Leaving it unratified means the one recipe this project ships behaves in a way its own composition contract does not describe.

WHAT TO DO WITH THE ANSWER: record the one word in `docs/workflow/owner-ratifications-<date>.md`, the same place every other answer lands. If it is `ratified` or `ratified with edits`, converge-yj3's README sentence and `conformance/composition/run.py` rule 4 both become follow-on work and should be filed together, because a README restated without the kit is a green rule asserting something the contract does not say.

Evidence, options and "what does not change" are all in the candidate file; nothing needs to be reconstructed to answer this.

title: The documents kit's workspace-template rule checks five hardcoded files, so three could vanish unnoticed
description:
Contract: documents.v1 §12

conformance/documents/run.py:258-264 holds WORKSPACE_TEMPLATE, a list of five paths, and rule 12b reports "all 5 workspace-template file(s) present" against it. Measured 2026-09-05, docs/workspace-template/ holds eight kit files — plus an index README added by lane w10-adoption-docs on the same day, which is not itself part of the kit. The three kit files the rule never looks at are GOAL-FILE.md.template, converge-dir-README.md.template and gitignore-addendum.txt.

The consequence is that the kit would keep reporting the participant kit complete if any of those three were deleted — the same undercount as the prose in docs/CONTRACTS-README.md:154, in the one place that exists to catch prose being wrong. A check that cannot notice an absence is not checking for it.

Whoever takes this should decide between two shapes and say which: either the rule reads the directory and asserts every file in it carries a documented destination, or the list stays explicit and gains the three missing entries plus a rule that fails when the directory holds a file the list does not name. The second keeps the check honest about additions; the first keeps it honest about deletions only.

Found while writing the adoption docs in lane w10-adoption-docs, which owns neither conformance/ nor docs/CONTRACTS-README.md. docs/workspace-template/README.md now carries the index of all eight kit files as prose.
acceptance: Given docs/workspace-template/ and the documents kit, when any one kit file is removed from that directory and the kit is run, then rule 12b names the file that went missing rather than reporting the participant kit complete. Given a file is added to that directory with no entry anywhere, when the kit is run, then that is visible too. Falsified if the rule still measures a fixed count of five while the directory holds eight kit files.

title: PINS.md and AGENTS.md still say the ledger and the kits do not exist — both have for four waves
description:
Contract: documents.v1 Core 12 (the participant kit carries what a session needs) — and PINS.md's own standing rule, which is the point of this item: "Every line here is a fact you may rely on. If a line here is wrong, sessions act on it anyway — fix it the moment it drifts."

Found 2026-09-04 by converge-dgc while reading the standing rules before its first edit, as AGENTS.md asks.

PINS.md, "Where things are" table, reads today:

    | Conformance ledger | `ledger/rows.yaml` — **not seeded yet** |
    | Conformance kits | `conformance/<contract>/run.py` — **not built yet** |

AGENTS.md section 3 reads today:

    **Neither the ledger nor the kits exist yet** — they are the next wave of
    work. Until they do, a claim that a contract is kept is an opinion, and must
    be labelled as one.

Both are false, and have been for several waves. Measured on this tree:

    $ uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py
    ALL LEDGER SELF-CHECKS PASS          (175 rows, 14 contracts, exit 0)
    $ ls conformance/
    composition  documents  experience-console  experience-direction
    experience-operation  _superseded
    $ uv run conformance/documents/run.py .
    VERDICT: PASS  (pass=18 fail=0 skip=9)
    $ uv run --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest -q conformance -c conformance/pytest.ini
    73 passed

conformance/README.md already documents five runnable kits and how to run them, so the two pages that a session is told to read FIRST are the two that are wrong.

WHAT IT COSTS, concretely: a session that believes AGENTS.md will label a checked, ledgered claim as "an opinion", and one that believes PINS.md will not run the check that would have caught its drift. This lane read both pages before touching anything and had to go and look to find out they were stale — the exact cost PINS.md's own rule exists to prevent.

THE FIX IS TWO EDITS, and neither is this lane's file to make (converge-dgc owns ledger/** and one candidate):
- PINS.md: drop "not seeded yet" and "not built yet"; point the kits row at conformance/README.md, which lists the five by name.
- AGENTS.md section 3: replace the "neither exists yet" paragraph. The three rules under it (a check that cannot run reports "Can't check"; do not weaken a check to make it green; drift is caught in both directions) are all live and correct — they are written as future-conditional ("Rules for the check itself, once it exists") and should read as present.
acceptance: GIVEN PINS.md and AGENTS.md WHEN a session reads them before its first edit THEN neither says the ledger or the kits are absent, and the kits row points at conformance/README.md. Falsified if either page still carries "not seeded yet", "not built yet", or "Neither the ledger nor the kits exist yet" while `ledger/checks/verify.py` and `conformance/documents/run.py` both run.

title: Rule 9a reads GAP out of a filename, so any item that cites the gap-analysis document fails on a word it never used as a state
description:
Contract: documents.v1 Core 9 ("defines done in plain words") and Core 10 (plain state words, not machine tokens) — the rule that enforces them flags a machine token that is part of a longer filename.

Measured on 2026-09-04, on this tree, running conformance/documents/run.py before and after converge-68f5's migration moved twenty-four items' acceptance text into the field it belongs in:

    (before, against the committed export)
    [PASS] 9a  work_item_names_a_contract: all 177 work item(s) name a contract and define done
    VERDICT: PASS  (pass=18 fail=0 skip=9)

    (after, same rule, same tree)
    [FAIL] 9a  work_item_names_a_contract: 1 of 187 work failed — converge-823:
           defines done with machine state word(s) ['GAP'], not in plain words
    VERDICT: FAIL  (pass=17 fail=1 skip=9)

The span it is reading, verbatim from converge-823's acceptance:

    Grouped by cause and component on 2026-09-04 by
    docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md, which is where the whole
    mapping of rows to items is printed.

The token is the first word of a real file's name. Nobody used GAP as a state here — the sentence cites a document that exists in this repository. MACHINE_STATE_RE wraps each token in word boundaries, and a hyphen is a non-word character, so `\bGAP\b` matches inside `GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md`. Any item that cites that document by name fails the same way, and that document is exactly the one items are supposed to cite when they say which ledger rows they close.

Two costs. The verdict is wrong about converge-823 — its definition of done is the GIVEN/THEN sentence above the citation, and that sentence is in plain words. And because the failure is real-looking, the cheapest way to clear it is to reword a legitimate citation, which is the reshape-the-subject-until-it-passes move scripts/export-work-items.py's own docstring says to refuse.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW, which is the part worth keeping. `_done_definition` returns the acceptance FIELD in full, plus any single LINE elsewhere in the item that carries a done phrase. While converge-823's acceptance was stranded in its description (converge-68f5), only the GIVEN/THEN line was scanned; the citation sat on a different line and was never read. Moving the text into its field brought the whole paragraph under the rule for the first time. So this is not a regression the migration introduced — it is a reading the queue's own shape had been hiding, and it appeared the moment the shape was corrected.

Two candidate fixes for whoever takes it, and they are not equivalent. Narrow the token match so a token that is part of a longer hyphenated word is not a state claim (the rule keeps its teeth; a bare GAP in prose still fails) — this is the one to prefer, because it fixes every future citation at once. Or wrap the path in inline code in converge-823 alone, which `strip_inline_code` already honours — one item green, the next citation red again.

Filed rather than fixed: conformance/documents/** is not in this lane's ownership (conformance/experience-direction/** is). converge-823's acceptance text was deliberately left word for word as its filer wrote it, which converge-68f5's acceptance requires.
acceptance: GIVEN a work item whose definition of done cites `docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md` by name and uses no machine state word as a state WHEN `uv run conformance/documents/run.py .` is run THEN rule 9a passes that item, AND an item that does write a bare machine state word into its definition of done still fails — checked with one of each, so the narrowing is shown not to have removed the rule's teeth.

title: The scheduled reconcile is configured to file into a work-tracker project "e2e-converge" that does not exist
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §12 — "The queue is the shared one, with custody. Atomic claim, heartbeat while held, resolution written for whoever asked." A reconcile pointed at a project that does not exist is not on the shared queue at all.

Found 2026-09-04 by the scheduled reconcile itself, against target-repo @ a5c6c02.

The reconcile run was told: *Tracker project: e2e-converge*. There is no such database:

    work_stats(project="e2e-converge")
    ERROR: could not read items of database 'e2e-converge' over SQL:
    Error 1049 (HY000): database not found: e2e-converge

The project this repository's ledger actually rides on is **converge**, and that is not a guess — the repository says so itself, in two places:

    conformance/README.md   uv run scripts/export-work-items.py --project converge
                            --out docs/work-items.json
    the app's own config     tracker_project = "converge"

Every `work:` ref in `ledger/rows.yaml` is a `converge-*` id; the four items this reconcile had to reference rather than duplicate (converge-nn6, converge-71q, converge-rgs3, converge-lhkf) live there; and `ledger/checks/verify.py`'s live-work tripwire resolves refs against an export of that same project.

WHAT THE RECONCILE DID, and why: it filed into **converge**. Filing into a freshly-created `e2e-converge` would have produced refs that `verify.py` cannot resolve — and it reports an unresolvable ref as `[INFO]`, never a failure (see converge-j0u5), so every newly filed item would have been invisible to the very tripwire that exists to catch a red row with no live work. Two queues, one ledger, and a gate structurally unable to tell the difference.

This is recorded rather than silently normalised, because the next scheduled run will be handed the same configuration.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: either the reconcile's configuration names `converge`, or — if an isolated queue is genuinely wanted for harness runs — the export script, the app config, and the ledger's existing refs move together, and the ledger is understood to cite one project only.
acceptance: GIVEN the scheduled reconcile's configuration WHEN it names a tracker project THEN that project exists and is the same one `scripts/export-work-items.py` exports and `ledger/rows.yaml` cites; AND no run of the reconcile writes a `work:` ref into the ledger that `ledger/checks/verify.py` cannot resolve against the export.

title: No contract clause says where an operation's state may land, so the workspace-root rule is a mode convention with nothing behind it
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §5 — "**Lanes are real sessions.** A lane is a worker session's own working copy, branch, and terminal session, launched through the parallel-lane tooling."

Found 2026-09-05 on lane/w9-where-it-starts while closing converge-36vm. That item's own description cites "composition.v1 §2 (nothing lands outside the project)". Checked against the file, composition.v1 clause 2 reads:

    2. **Automated steps use only the lean base's helpers** — a reader for
       read-only steps, a builder for writing, a git helper for version control.

It says nothing about where anything lands. Grepping every contract for "outside", "home directory", "workspace" and "side effect" returns two hits, both about vocabulary in Details folds:

    contracts/experience.v1.md:88:- No machine vocabulary outside a Details fold.
    contracts/surface.v1.md:71:- No internal vocabulary outside Details folds.

So the nearest law is composition.v1's PURPOSE sentence — "sit lightly on a host … and never a side effect on work that isn't its own" — which is prose above the teeth, not a numbered clause a check can read. operation.v1 §5 names a lane's own working copy but not its location.

The lane wrote the rule anyway, because thirteen batch directories under ~/dev were the measured cost, and labelled it honestly in both modes/converge-manager.md clause 5 and context/manager/where-you-run.md: a mode convention, not a contract quotation. AGENTS.md rule 1 says a missing contract is the steward's decision, not a promise a session invents — hence this item rather than a candidate written on the lane's own authority.

The decision for the steward: either operation.v1 §5 gains a sentence saying an operation's state lives inside the project or workspace it serves, or composition.v1 gains a clause promoting its purpose sentence into teeth, or the location stays a convention with no check behind it and this item is declined with that recorded.
acceptance: Given a reader asking which clause forbids an operation's state landing outside the project, when they open contracts/, then either a numbered clause answers them, or a declined record says the location is deliberately a convention. Kept when one of those two exists; not yet while the only answer is a purpose sentence and a mode file; can't check by any kit until the clause exists, since no kit can read a promise nobody wrote.

title: Locking a document says \"Locked: FROZEN\" where it should refuse out loud
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 Core 11 (the lock control is gated on the four conditions, and nothing locks on its own) — the gate itself holds; the sentence after it reports a lock that was never written.

Found on 2026-09-04 by lane w8-words-readme while running the full app suite for converge-6my / converge-u2y. It is a residual: nothing in that lane's ownership (`app/data.py`, `app/static/js/render/operation.js`, `app/README.md`, `app/tests/test_words_readme.py`) touches locking, and the failure reproduces on a clean tree with that lane's changes stashed.

Measured on this tree at HEAD 09bcea3, twice — once with the lane's changes present, once with `git stash -u` applied so the tree was pristine — identical both times:

    $ uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx --with playwright pytest -q \
        "app/tests/test_direction_final.py::test_locking_says_out_loud_that_no_write_answers_yet"
    [lock] toast: Locked: FROZEN
    E   AssertionError: the refusal was swallowed: 'Locked: FROZEN'
    E   assert 'Nothing was locked' in 'Locked: FROZEN'
    1 failed in 3.31s

Everything before that point in the test passes: the four lock conditions are checkable, the gate enables, the confirmation dialog opens with the title `Lock this document` and carries all four answers. Only the outcome sentence is wrong.

The test's own name says what it is defending: locking has no write behind it yet, and the surface is supposed to SAY so rather than report a success that did not happen. Today it reports `Locked: FROZEN` — a steward reading that toast would believe the document is locked when nothing was written. That is the exact failure mode `AGENTS.md` §5 and the honesty clauses exist to prevent, which is why this is worth an item rather than a note.

Two ways it could be wrong, and they need different fixes — whoever owns this should decide which:

1. **The write really does not exist**, and the toast is lying. Fix the outcome sentence to say nothing was locked, and say why.
2. **The write now exists** (something landed since the test was written), and the test is stale. Then the fix is the test, and the surface is right — but somebody must confirm the document is actually written before that call is made, not assume it from the toast.

Full-suite context from the same run, so the scale is on the record: `1 failed, 360 passed, 32 warnings in 322.13s`. This is the only failure.

Owner: whoever owns the lock flow — `app/static/js/direction.js` and `app/writes.py` for (1), `app/tests/test_direction_final.py` for (2). Lane w8-words-readme owns none of them and did not touch them.
acceptance: GIVEN the Direction view with a document whose four lock conditions are all answered WHEN the steward clicks `Lock it` THEN the outcome sentence tells the truth about what was written — either it names the refusal in plain words (no write answers yet, so nothing was locked), or a document was genuinely written and re-reading the file from disk shows the locking word in its first heading. FALSE IF the toast reports a lock while the document on disk is unchanged.

title: Nine operation.v1 clauses are encoded in the manager mode and observed nowhere: the turnkey steps that would judge them are not in this tree
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 11, 12, 13. Ledger rows **CVG-012, CVG-013, CVG-014, CVG-016, CVG-017, CVG-018, CVG-021, CVG-022, CVG-023** (nine rows).

      r"\[(PASS|FAIL|SKIP)\] \((?P<letter>[a-i])\) ..."

The step letters it can parse are `[a-i]`. Step (j) cannot be read at all. `evaluations/turnkey/RESULT.md` carries no (j) or (k) section either — its last amendment is "step (i) now reads one entry, not the whole file". <parameter name="acceptance">GIVEN the turnkey harness can read the steps that judge operation.v1 Core 2/3/4/6/7/8/11/12/13 WHEN it is run against a real wave on this host THEN each of those nine clauses gets a PASS or FAIL with the evidence it read named; AND ledger rows CVG-012, CVG-013, CVG-014, CVG-016, CVG-017, CVG-018, CVG-021, CVG-022 and CVG-023 are each re-derived from that run, quoting it; AND no row among them still asserts only that the mode file mentions its clause.

title: Documents: six kit rules assert less than their clause text says (ledger rows CVG-058/059/061/063/064/065)
description:
Contract: documents.v1. Six documents-kit rules assert less than their clause text says; tighten each rule to its clause or record an honest SKIP with the reason. Follow-up to the w3-doc-kit lane — same ownership (conformance/documents/**).

>>> THE RESOLUTION ON THIS ITEM IS FALSE IN ONE PARAGRAPH AND CANNOT BE EDITED.
>>> READ converge-xm5 INSTEAD — it supersedes this item and carries the corrected
>>> reason in a resolution field. The supersedes edge is live in both directions.

title: The only written adoption path is "copy the five files by hand", and the existing-project path the steward has driven twice is written down nowhere
description:
Contract: operation.v1 §1

docs/CONTRACTS-README.md:151-156, "Taking this to your own project", is the entire adoption procedure in the repository: copy the templates, fill in the placeholders, enable the hook. It starts no manager session, investigates no repository, drafts no vision, derives no contract, seeds no ledger and files no work.

Set that beside README.md:5-8 — "the work of getting there is planned, run, and checked for you" — and the promise and the procedure describe two different products. The adopter is asked to do by hand exactly the work the manager session exists to do.

The chain has the same hole from the other end. README.md:127-130 describes recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml as the one recipe, and it derives the ledger from a target repo's contracts. So of blank repo, vision, contracts, seed, queue, only the seed step has a documented mechanism, and the two steps that must run before it have none: the recipe cannot run until something produces contracts, and nothing written down produces contracts.

For an existing project it is worse, because the path exists and is simply unrecorded. The steward has driven it by hand twice, in cortex-core and drumbeat — pause the work in flight, investigate the code that is there, propose a vision and contracts, wait for the steward's word, seed the ledger, file the items that bring the repo into line. Neither run left a procedure here: no adopt recipe, no adopt skill (the five in skills/ are all mid-project procedures), and no section in the mode. The word "adopt" appears once in the reader-facing surface, README.md:151, pointing at a template directory.

Note the ordering: this needs converge-jyg0 answered first, because a documented path with no clause behind it is the thing modes/converge-manager.md:35-37 forbids.

Found by the onboarding audit, docs/workflow/ONBOARDING-AUDIT-2026-09-04.md, findings c-1 and c-5.

---

WHAT LANDED ON 2026-09-05, AND WHY THIS ITEM IS STILL OPEN (lane w10-adoption-docs)

converge-jyg0 was answered that day with contracts/operation.v1-candidate.md, proposing Core 14, "The first wake is investigate, then propose". That unblocked the writing half of this item, and the writing half is done:

docs/ADOPTING.md, section "The first wake, on either kind of project", now carries both paths in the order the proposed clause names them. Adopting a repository that already holds code: the work in flight pauses; it reads what is there before proposing anything; it proposes a vision and first contracts as drafts and stops for the steward's word; on that word the ledger is seeded; the queue is derived from the gap, every item naming its contract. A blank repository is the same five steps with nothing to read first, beginning at the vision. The page also says the drafts are written from the shipped templates, so the adopter reads drafts rather than filling in blanks — the "no step that asks the adopter to hand-copy a template" half of this item's acceptance, for everything except the pre-push guard, which is theirs to install. README.md:10 and the reading order at README.md:277 send a reader there, so the path is no longer only in one person's memory.

Two things remain, and neither was this lane's to do:

1. THE CLAUSE IS PROPOSED, NOT RATIFIED. The page says so plainly, and modes/converge-manager.md still carries no first-wake section, because a section keyed to an unratified clause is what modes/converge-manager.md:35-37 forbids. That section is the mechanism half of this item and it cannot be written until the steward answers.

2. NO RUN HAS BEEN PERFORMED AGAINST THE WRITTEN PATH. This item's acceptance is about what following the path actually produces — an investigated repository, drafts that waited for a word, a seeded ledger, a queue naming contracts. That is evidence from a run, not from a file, and evaluations/adopter/ is the harness that asks it. The audit records the cost as about an hour of wall time and two long provider sessions per project. Closing this item on the strength of a well-written page would be exactly the unchecked claim this repository refuses.

Released rather than resolved for those two reasons. Whoever takes it next: the writing is in place, so what is left is the steward's word, then the mode section keyed to Core 14, then a run of evaluations/adopter/ against both scenarios with its result recorded.

---

WHAT LANDED ON 2026-09-06, AND WHY THIS ITEM IS STILL OPEN (lane w11-first-wake-mode, under converge-dnip)

Reason 1 above is cleared. The steward ratified Core 14 on 2026-09-06 -- word "ratified, please continue", recorded in docs/workflow/owner-ratifications-2026-09-06.md -- so the clause is law and the mechanism half could be written. It now is:

- modes/converge-manager.md carries "## Clause 14 - The first wake is investigate, then propose" at line 349, before "## The operating loop - on every wake" at line 397, and the loop's own opening now says it does not apply on a first wake. The section names both paths: adopting a repository that already holds code (pause the work in flight and say so in the plan record; investigate what is there; propose a vision and first contracts as DRAFT; park with a CALL ratify line carrying Parked and Continued; on the word seed the ledger; file the alignment items), and starting a blank one (the same five steps, beginning at the vision).
- context/manager/first-wake.md is new, and the mode's frontmatter loads it. It carries the plain-word shape of the investigation -- four questions answered in sentences, change nothing while reading -- and of each draft: the vision from VISION.md.template, each contract from CONTRACT.md.template, one promise apiece, every one carrying (DRAFT) in its first heading until the steward's word.
- docs/ADOPTING.md no longer says the clause is proposed. It names the ratification, points at the mode section, and says plainly what is still unproven.

THE EXACT MISSING OBSERVATION -- reason 2 above, unchanged. This item's acceptance asks what following the path actually produces on a run: a manager session that investigated the code before proposing anything, a vision and at least one contract that were drafted and waited for the steward's word, a seeded ledger, and a queue whose items name the contracts they serve. No such run has been recorded. evaluations/adopter/RESULT.md remains the only recorded result and it reads RED -- 12 pass, 3 fail, 0 skip, run 2026-09-04T14:19:11+00:00 on adopter-20260904141911 -- which predates every file named above. Closing this item on the strength of a written path and a mode section would be exactly the unchecked claim this repository refuses.

WHAT IS LEFT, EXACTLY: run ./evaluations/adopter/run.sh against both scenarios (it needs AMPLIFIER_EVALUATION_SRC and a DTU; the onboarding audit records the cost as about an hour of wall time and two long provider sessions per project), and record its result. Nothing else in this item is outstanding -- the writing and the mechanism are both in place and both are checkable in the tree today.

---

THE RUN HAPPENED ON 2026-09-06, AND THIS ITEM IS STILL OPEN — NOW ON MEASURED ABSENCE, NOT ON "NOBODY HAS RUN IT" (lane w12-adopter-proof, under converge-himk)

Reason 2 above is discharged. The harness was run end to end against the tree an early adopter meets today — README sha 53c2885…, matching origin/main, bundle_commit f6b5e30, so the rewritten README, docs/ADOPTING.md and the mode's Clause 14 section were all in it. Both scenarios ran, each in its own fresh container, and the result is recorded in evaluations/adopter/RESULT.md: RED, 17 pass · 2 fail · 0 can't tell · 0 skip, run 2026-09-06T03:50:03Z.

WHAT THE RUN SHOWED, AGAINST THIS ITEM'S OWN ACCEPTANCE:

Blank repository (scenario 1, the mdstrip CLI) — the whole chain, measured in that container afterwards. A live manager session, docs/VISION.md, contracts/conversion.v1.md, a seeded ledger/rows.yaml with real checks beside it, and a queue item (mdstrip-c9t) naming conversion.v1. Ledger row CVG-301 moved from Not yet to Kept on that reading. This half of the acceptance is met.

Existing repository (scenario 2, the sensorlog CLI) — two of four, and the last two measured absent:
  - investigated the code before proposing anything — SHOWN. The manager read src/sensorlog/ and its tests before drafting.
  - a vision and a contract drafted, waiting for the steward's word — SHOWN. Both were drafted, reviewed, and explicitly ratified before anything was locked.
  - the ledger seeded — NOT SHOWN. There is no ledger/rows.yaml in that project. (RESULT.md, S2.5, FAIL.)
  - a queue holding items that name the contracts they serve — NOT SHOWN. There is no queue store anywhere in that container, and the queue CLI was on PATH, so this is absence looked for where it would be. (RESULT.md, S2.6, FAIL.)

THOSE TWO STEPS ARE EXACTLY WHAT THIS ITEM STILL WAITS ON.

WHY THEY DID NOT HAPPEN, WHICH MATTERS FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS NEXT. The steward ratified. The session then locked the vision by freezing its H1, and tried to add the changelog line recording that ratification as a second, separate edit — which its own locked-document guard refused, leaving VISION.md half-frozen. It recognised the sequencing bug, tried to recover, and then made no progress for over twenty minutes without declaring itself stuck. Everything after the lock — ledger, queue, alignment items — was never reached. Filed as converge-p17d (the guard trap) and converge-4vf6 (the silent stall).

DO NOT RE-RUN THE ADOPT SCENARIO BEFORE converge-p17d LANDS. The trap is structural, not a slip: a document is locked by editing its own text, and the record of the lock is more text in the same file, so whichever edit goes second is refused. Any session that locks a document the way this one did hits it, and an adopt run costs about an hour of wall time and a long provider session. These are linked as relates-to rather than blocks, because the other half of what is left here is not blocked by it — see below.

THE THIRD THING THIS ITEM WANTS AND NO RUN CAN CURRENTLY SHOW: "the work in flight pauses first". The harness has no step that looks for work in flight being stopped before a direction is proposed, so no run answers it either way. That is a gap in the harness, and it can be closed independently of converge-p17d.

WHAT IS LEFT, EXACTLY: (a) converge-p17d fixed, then one adopt-scenario run that reaches a seeded ledger and a queue naming its contracts; (b) a harness step that can see the pause. Ledger row CVG-302 carries the same reading and stays Not yet against this item.
acceptance: Given someone with a repository that already has code and no vision, when they follow the written adoption path end to end, then a manager session investigated the code before proposing anything, a vision and at least one contract were drafted and waited for the steward's word, the ledger was seeded, and the queue holds items that name the contracts they serve — with no step that asks the adopter to hand-copy a template. Given someone with a blank repository, when they follow the same path, then it takes them from nothing to that same state. Given both, when a reader looks for the path, then it is where the README sends them, not in one person's memory.

title: Split CVG-051 — clause 9's two halves no longer share a disposition after wave 4
description:
Serves documents.v1 Core 9. Found while working converge-12o, which owned the four red rows (CVG-052/053/057/066) and the stale `indexed` refs, and deliberately did not guess at this fifth re-derivation.

CVG-051 is one GAP row quoting the whole of clause 9: "**A work item names its contract** in one line, defines done in plain words, and quotes the feedback or gap it came from." Before wave 4 that was right — rule 4 SKIPped because "work items live in the work queue, not in the repository", and nothing asserted any part of the clause.

Wave 4 replaced that with two rules, and they are no longer the same kind of thing (RAN 2026-09-03, `uv run conformance/documents/run.py . --json-only`):

  9a  work_item_names_a_contract   SKIP  "no work-item export at docs/work-items.json
      and none named with --work-items — work items live in the work queue, not in
      this tree, so the kit has nothing to read"
  9b  work_item_quotes_its_source  SKIP  "measured against this repository's own
      queue: the literal test — a blockquote or a quoted span — passes 7 of 24 real
      items, and most of the 17 it fails do point at their origin … Telling a
      quotation of feedback from a quoted filename needs a reader."

9a is a plain GAP: the check exists, it is mechanical, and it SKIPs only because this repository exports no queue. Supply `docs/work-items.json` (or `--work-items`) and it runs. 9b is a MEASURED refusal — the same shape as rule 7d, which is exactly why converge-jc9 moved CVG-063 to NOT-ASSERTABLE rather than leaving it GAP.

A row whose two halves carry different dispositions is one this ledger splits, quoting a disjoint sentence for each (CVG-059 → CVG-067 in wave 4; CVG-052 → CVG-068 in converge-12o). The likely shape: CVG-051 keeps "**A work item names its contract** in one line, defines done in plain words," as GAP against rule 9a, and a new id takes "and quotes the feedback or gap it came from." as NOT-ASSERTABLE against rule 9b's measurement.

Worth deciding in the same pass: whether exporting the work queue to docs/work-items.json is work this repo wants, since that alone would let 9a actually run and could move the GAP half.

converge-12o updated CVG-051's `indexed` ref from the stale `(rule 4)` — which after the renumber names `contract_section_order` under Core 4 — to `(rules 9a, 9b)`, and re-derived its notes against the run above. The disposition was left at GAP, which under-claims rather than over-claims, and is honest for the row as it currently stands.
acceptance: GIVEN the documents kit as merged at wave 4, WHERE rule 9a SKIPs for a missing export and rule 9b SKIPs on a measurement, WHEN CVG-051 is split so each half quotes its own disjoint sentence of clause 9 and carries the disposition its own rule supports, THEN `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` prints and exits 0 with clause 9 still cited, each new row carries a RAN line naming the rule and verdict it was derived from, and the can't-check half carries a justification quoting rule 9b's own measured reason. Falsified by: a disposition assigned without a run shown, overlapping quotes between the two halves, or a `work` ref left on a row that is no longer red.

title: Pinned open: does an off-by-default drafting session count as the manager session in the hot path? (CVG-186)
description:
Contract: experience-collaboration.v1 Core 7 — "**The manager session is not in the hot path.** A write made in the app goes through the ordinary repository and proposal mechanism directly; the manager session learns of it as an event and folds it into its next turn."

Measured 2026-09-04 (converge-dgc, the reconcile after wave 8). `app/writes.py` now has two `subprocess.run(` sites, not one:

  line 258  ["git", *args]                                    — the repository write
  line 451  ["amplifier", "run", "--mode", "single", ...]      — draft_with_amplifier, DRAFT_TIMEOUT = 240.0

The second is reached from `record_ask()` only when `drafter == "agent"` (app/writes.py:656), and the only caller sets it from `ASK_DRAFTER = os.environ.get("CONVERGE_ASK_DRAFTER", "fixture")` (app/serve.py:38). So it is OFF as shipped, and ON with one environment variable — at which point the ask write blocks on a headless Amplifier session for up to four minutes before the proposal file is written.

Neither of the two readings converge-76y named is clean, which is why CVG-186 was re-derived to OPEN-PINNED rather than forced either way:

(a) KEPT, probe too narrow. A headless `amplifier run --mode single` is not *the* manager session: it is unregistered, has no steward (Core 8), and is discarded after one turn. Textually the clause is about the manager session, and no manager session is reached.

(b) BROKEN. The property the clause exists to protect is in its own kit assert — "A write made in the app lands through the repository mechanism without waiting for a manager turn." With the switch on, the ask write waits on an agent turn. Whether that agent is called the manager session is a naming question; the waiting is real.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS, in one sentence: does clause 7 forbid *the manager session* in the write path, or *any* agent turn a write waits on? If the former, CVG-186 becomes CONFORMS and clause 7 should say so explicitly, because the current wording cannot be read off the code. If the latter, either the drafter goes or clause 7 gets a CANDIDATE amendment permitting an explicitly-switched-on, timeout-bounded drafting session whose failure still lands the write.

Not settled here because this lane owns `ledger/**` and `contracts/experience.v1-candidate.md` only — clause 7 lives in experience-collaboration.v1, whose candidate this lane may not author, and `app/writes.py` is another lane's file. CVG-186 asserts the current behaviour without forging the decision (PROTOCOL §3.3 OPEN-PINNED); its probe flips red if the default flips to "agent", if the gate disappears, if a third process appears, or if the second process stops being the drafting session — each break observed firing on a scratch copy 2026-09-04.

Related: converge-76y (the red-on-main report this answers).
acceptance: GIVEN the steward's ruling on which reading of clause 7 stands WHEN CVG-186 is re-derived THEN it carries Kept or Broken rather than Pinned open, and the clause wording (or the app's write path) has moved so the disposition can be read off the code without the ruling. Falsified if CVG-186 is moved off Pinned open with no ruling recorded and no change to either the clause or the code.

title: The fixture generator's restore wiring cannot name a snapshot, so a regeneration turns the direction kit's new rule 6b red on sample-good
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 Core 6 ("Restore a wording, a paragraph, a section, or the whole document" — restoring FROM a point in history).

converge-899y split the direction kit's rule 6 into 6a (restore reaches a write) and 6b (that write can name WHICH snapshot). 6b needs `fixtures/sample-good` to model a build that keeps the whole clause, so sample-good's restore wiring now carries a snapshot:

    export function restoreScope(scope, snapshot) {
      const since = snapshot || readPoint();
      return post(`${docBase(...)}/changes/${scope}/restore`, since ? { since } : {});
    }

`conformance/experience-fixtures/make_fixtures.py` still emits the older shape — `api.ask(state.managerId, { scope: btn.dataset.restore, intent: 'restore this wording' })` — which reaches a write (6a passes) but names no snapshot (6b fails). So re-running the generator as it stands reverts sample-good and turns the kit's own `test_sample_good_passes` red.

Measured 2026-09-04 on lane/w9-queue-and-kits, running the kit against the hand-corrected sample-good and against the same fixture with the snapshot removed:

    sample-good          6a PASS   6b PASS    VERDICT: PASS (pass=13 fail=0 skip=0)
    sample-one-snapshot  6a PASS   6b FAIL    VERDICT: FAIL (pass=12 fail=1 skip=0)

The second is the generator's current shape, kept deliberately as the kit's negative fixture for this clause.

This is loud rather than silent — a regeneration fails a named test with a named rule, and the kit's README carries a "before you regenerate" note pointing here — but it is still a trap for whoever regenerates next, and the honest fix is for the generator to emit a body that keeps the clause.

Two things for whoever takes it. The GOOD actions.js template is shared by the console, operation and collaboration kits as well, so the change wants checking against all four kits' self-tests, not only this one. And the generated `sample-bad` should keep failing 6b — it already does, and `test_every_rule_has_a_negative_fixture` will say so if that ever stops being true.

Filed rather than fixed: `conformance/experience-fixtures/**` is not in lane w9-queue-and-kits's ownership (`conformance/experience-direction/**` is).
acceptance: GIVEN `conformance/experience-fixtures/make_fixtures.py` has been re-run WHEN the four experience kits' self-tests are run THEN all four pass, and the direction kit's rule 6b PASSes on the regenerated `sample-good` — AND still FAILs on `sample-bad` and on `sample-one-snapshot`, so the rule keeps a build it can fail on.
