title: Lane brief for converge-c9p named the wrong two files as its ownership
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 5 - a lane brief carries the file-ownership split.

The brief written for converge-c9p (lane w8-brief-convention) said: "File ownership - edit ONLY: `modes/converge-manager.md`, `docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md` (header/convention text only, not entries)."

Those are converge-823's two files. The item's own description says so in its last line: "Not fixed by converge-823: that lane owns `modes/converge-manager.md` and `docs/workflow/OWNER-RETURN-LOG.md` only." And converge-c9p's acceptance is entirely about a third file the brief never named: "GIVEN context/manager/return-brief.md WHEN a manager session reads it THEN ...". The ownership block was copied from the upstream lane rather than derived from this item.

The two named files needed no change: clause 10 already carried the stamp and the labels, and the log header already pointed at the other two files for them (measured - 14 shape elements compared between clause 10 and the convention after the fix, 0 mismatched). So obeying the brief literally would have produced a lane that could not satisfy a single acceptance line while editing only files that were already correct.

The lane edited `context/manager/return-brief.md` instead, and recorded the deviation in the commit message, the marker file, and the resolution. No other live lane owned that path (checked across the seven lanes with a GOAL.md at the time: app/**, ledger/**, evaluations/turnkey/** only), so there was no collision - but that was luck, not the brief's doing.

What to change: when a brief is written for an item whose acceptance names a file, the ownership list must contain that file. A brief whose ownership cannot satisfy its own acceptance is checkable before the lane launches.
acceptance: GIVEN a lane brief whose work item's acceptance names a file path WHEN the brief is written THEN its file-ownership list contains that path, and a brief that fails this is caught before the lane launches rather than by the lane. Falsified if a brief can still ship an ownership list disjoint from the paths its own acceptance names.

title: operation.v1 Core 13: three recorded wave closes name only what finished, so the live clause reading is red (CVG-023)
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 13 — hand off when done; a manager session says so, writes a hand-off a fresh session can resume from, and stops.

Discovered from converge-1nb4 while re-deriving CVG-023 from the live reading rather than the block pasted into evaluations/turnkey/RESULT.md.

WHAT THE LIVE READING SAYS. Run from the repository root on 2026-09-06:

  uv run evaluations/turnkey/run.py --env local --workspace /home/bkrabach/dev/vision-focused-team-ci/.converge/converge --project converge --steps j

  Core 13 (CVG-023) FAIL: 3 of 6 recorded close(s) say only what finished and never what remains, so a fresh session has nothing to resume from

The three that fail are the W8, W11 and W12 closes in the plan record. The reader judges content, not existence: a close is resumable only if it also says what REMAINS — residuals, what is parked, what is still live, what is open, what is next, what is blocked or pending. Three closes in the same record do say that and pass, so the difference is what was written, not what the reader can see.

The newest close is one of the three that fail, which is the worst position for this clause to be in: the entry a fresh session would read first is the one with nothing to resume from.

WHY IT MATTERS. This clause is the one that makes a manager session replaceable. A close that lists only what landed reads like success and hands the next session nothing.

Manager session, 2026-09-06 10:06: the W14 close and hand-over addenda for W8/W11/W12 were appended to the plan record in the Core 13 shape (LIVE / REMAINS / CAVEAT / CHECK). The live reading still counts the three original bare lines because it judges every recorded close ever written; a record is never edited, so this row stays not yet until the reader either honours an addendum or reads only closes since the convention landed — decide which in the fix.
acceptance: GIVEN the live step (j) reading taken from the repository root THEN Core 13 (CVG-023) no longer reports any recorded close that says only what finished; AND GIVEN ledger row CVG-023 THEN it is re-derived from that reading and its work ref is dropped when it goes green.

title: The checked-in work-item export is stale, so documents rule 9a and ledger CVG-051 report a failure the live queue no longer has
description:
Contract: documents.v1 §9

Corrected 2026-09-05 by the lane that filed it. The first version of this item blamed the reconcile run for filing items in machine words. Measured against a fresh export, that premise is wrong, and the real finding is smaller: the export committed in the tree is out of date.

Measured in this working copy on 2026-09-05, clean tree at b2be22d:

    $ uv run conformance/documents/run.py .          # reads docs/work-items.json as committed
    [FAIL] 9a  work_item_names_a_contract: 1 of 226 work failed — converge-w4j7:
               defines done with machine state word(s), not in plain words
    VERDICT: FAIL  (pass=17 fail=1 skip=9)

    $ uv run scripts/export-work-items.py --project converge --out /tmp/w10-work-items.json
    $ uv run conformance/documents/run.py . --work-items /tmp/w10-work-items.json
    [PASS] 9a  work_item_names_a_contract: all 230 work item(s) name a contract and define done
    VERDICT: PASS  (pass=18 fail=0 skip=9)

Same tree, same kit, same rule: red on the committed export, green on a fresh one. converge-w4j7 was filed 2026-09-05 22:31 and updated 00:23; the fix is in the queue and not in the file. The tree's export holds 226 items, the queue holds 230.

The ledger follows the export by the same path. `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` reports CVG-051's expect not met, reading FAIL-ITEMS=1 from that same stale file. The row's own notes say the count follows the export by design and is re-read on merge, never bumped blind — so this is the row working, pointed at a file nobody refreshed, not a new defect in the row.

AGENTS.md:88 already warns about exactly this: "The documents kit's rule 9a reads the work queue, which is not a file in this tree — refresh its export before you trust that rule's verdict." The warning exists and the stale file still ships, so every lane that runs the suite reads a red it did not cause and has to re-derive this from scratch.

`docs/work-items.json` and `ledger/rows.yaml` both belong to other lanes, so this lane wrote the fact down rather than making the change.

Discovered by lane w10-propose-first-wake while running the two suites for converge-jyg0. Not caused by it: its only change is a new proposal file, and the red was printed before that file existed.
acceptance: Given a clean tree, when someone refreshes docs/work-items.json with `uv run scripts/export-work-items.py --project converge --out docs/work-items.json` and runs `uv run conformance/documents/run.py .`, then rule 9a reads green against the committed export — kept. Given that refresh, when `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` runs, then CVG-051 is re-read against the refreshed count rather than bumped, and the ledger's self-checks pass — kept. Falsified if the export is refreshed but CVG-051's pinned count is edited to match without re-reading the row, or if rule 9a is still red against the committed export.

title: CVG-114's probe asserts the absence of two file names; after ratification it must be re-derived
description:
Contract: experience.v1 §15 (ledger hygiene for the row that carries it).

Ledger row CVG-114 asserts, by probe, that `contracts/platform-browser.v1.md` and `contracts/platform-web-app.v1.md` are both absent, expecting the output `CLAUSE-15-NAMED-PLATFORM-CONTRACTS: ABSENT,ABSENT`.

That probe is written against the clause's *current* wording. If the steward ratifies `contracts/experience.v1-candidate.md` (clause 15 names `platform-web.v1` instead), the two files stay absent forever and the probe keeps passing — while asserting the absence of two names no document mentions any more. A row that passes for a reason nobody holds is a stale check, not a kept clause.

Done in plain words: after the steward answers on the clause-15 candidate, CVG-114 is re-derived from the ratified clause text — its quote refreshed, its probe checking that every `platform-*.v1` the clause names exists in `contracts/`, and the SYNC row's hash for `contracts/experience.v1.md` re-pinned. If the steward declines instead, the row stands as it is and this item closes with that note.

Discovered by lane w8-clause15 while working converge-d3n. `ledger/` is outside that lane's file ownership, so it is filed rather than made.
acceptance: GIVEN the steward has answered on contracts/experience.v1-candidate.md WHEN CVG-114 is re-derived from the clause as it then reads THEN the row's quote matches the ratified text, its probe checks that each platform contract the clause names exists, and the SYNC row's hash for contracts/experience.v1.md matches the file on disk.

title: Locking a vision half-freezes it: the guard refuses the changelog edit that has to follow the freeze
description:
Contract: documents.v1 Core 6 (status lives in the H1 parenthetical and nowhere else), and the locked-document guard that enforces it.

Caught by the adopter harness run of 2026-09-06T03:50:03Z, scenario 2 (`evaluations/adopter/RESULT.md`, container adopter-20260906035003-s2). It is the reason that scenario is RED.

What happened, in order. The steward ratified the drafted vision. The manager session locked it by editing the H1 to `# sensorlog — Vision (FROZEN 2026-09-06)`. It then made a SECOND edit to add the changelog line recording that ratification — and its own locked-document guard refused that edit, because by then the file said FROZEN. The vision was left half-frozen: the status word landed, the record of why it landed did not. The session never recovered; nothing after this step ran.

The trap is structural, not a slip. A document is locked by changing its own text, and the record of the lock is more text in the same file. If the guard reads the file as locked the instant the H1 changes, then the freeze and the record of the freeze can never both land — whichever goes second is refused. Any session that locks a document the way this one did hits it.

What fixed looks like: freezing a document and writing the changelog entry that records the ratification land as ONE change, or the guard admits the second half of a freeze it just saw; and a document can never be left with a FROZEN heading and no changelog line naming the word that froze it.
acceptance: Given a drafted vision or contract and a steward's word, when a manager session locks it, then the H1 status and the changelog entry recording that ratification both land, and no guard refusal leaves the file half-frozen. Given the adopter harness re-run on the existing-project scenario, then the run reaches the ledger and queue steps rather than stopping at the lock.

title: "Copy the five files" names five of the six templates, and the hook's rename step is documented only inside the script
description:
Contract: documents.v1 §12

documents.v1 §12 says every converged repository carries the participant kit, so a colleague or a coding agent can take part. The instruction for doing that is wrong by one file.

docs/CONTRACTS-README.md:154 says "Copy the five files" and names five: a vision template, a contract template, an AGENTS.md addendum, a pins template, and the pre-push scan. docs/workspace-template/ holds six. The unnamed sixth is GOAL-FILE.md.template. A reader who follows the instruction leaves one behind and is not told which, and the directory has no index of its own to correct the count.

The same sentence says "enable the hook with git config core.hooksPath .githooks", but the file shipped is docs/workspace-template/pre-push-scan.sh and the hook has to end up at .githooks/pre-push. That rename is documented only inside the script's own comments, at docs/workspace-template/pre-push-scan.sh:18-20 — a place the reader has not been sent. Following the sentence alone sets core.hooksPath to a directory with nothing in it, and the guard silently does not run.

Both are cheap to fix and both are the kind of error that only shows up as a guard that never fires.

Found by the onboarding audit, docs/workflow/ONBOARDING-AUDIT-2026-09-04.md, finding c-2.
acceptance: Given a reader following "Taking this to your own project" with no other document open, when they finish the steps as written, then every file in docs/workspace-template/ is accounted for — either copied or explicitly named as not needed — and the pre-push scan is at .githooks/pre-push and executable. Given they then push an edit to a locked contract with no proposal beside it, when the push runs, then it is refused, which is how they learn the hook is really installed.

converge-er6 held exactly this and is resolved; neither reading moved. Whatever it did, rule 9 and rule 13 report the same thing today as when it was filed. Re-run both before assuming any of it is done -- do not read its resolution and conclude.

Both are edits to frozen-family text, so whether this is a convergent fix or needs a CANDIDATE amendment is the first question to settle, not the last.

title: A return was stamped in the log on 2026-09-06 12:00 and never briefed
description:

title: The ledger's pin on operation.v1 has drifted on main — the contract moved a bold marker, and section 4 asks for a re-review, not a bump
description:
Contract: docs/LEDGER-FORMAT.md section 4 (the SYNC row pins each contract's content hash; a mismatch triggers a mandatory full-ledger re-review, never a silent hash bump).

Main is red on its own ledger gate today, and has been since the contract was edited. Measured 2026-09-04 against main, read out of git, nothing written:

    SYNC pin on main matches main's contract: False
      pinned  db74407c8c792e9bda473f6e74132919983a5544b5f9419df10cdbfd0a2f6064
      main    22bcecd30c261abb11e11111221ad4ba7761d74824995de811e6471bc0eb4c07
    CVG-010 quote on main verifies on main : False

Both come from one edit. `contracts/operation.v1.md` line 77 carried an unbalanced bold — `**First green 2026-09-04 — nine of nine steps…` with nothing closing it — and main closed it early: `**First green 2026-09-04** — nine of nine steps…`.

The quote half is fixed by converge-0gb, which narrowed CVG-010's quote to the longest run of bytes both readings carry. Verified in a scratch merge of that lane into main: 174 of 174 quotes verify, 89 executable refs each meet their expect, and the only failing line left is this pin.

Nobody can close the pin half by editing a number. Section 4 exists because a hash bump is the cheapest possible lie: it says every row still reads its clause correctly, which only a person re-reading them can say. What makes this one nearly done is that most of the re-review has already happened — converge-0gb re-derived thirteen of the fifteen rows quoting this contract on 2026-09-04, converge-nf4 re-derived CVG-020 the same day, and CVG-010 itself was re-read in full. What is left is to confirm those readings against the changed bytes and then re-pin, in one change, with the confirmation written down.

Not done in converge-0gb, and this is the reason: that lane branched before the contract moved, so its working tree still holds the old bytes. Pinning main's hash there would have made the lane's own gate red and, worse, would have pinned a state that tree could not run — a claim made from a diff instead of from a run, which is the move CVG-051's notes already refuse by name.
acceptance: GIVEN main, where the ledger's pin on contracts/operation.v1.md no longer matches the file WHEN every row quoting that contract is re-read against its current bytes and the pin is updated in the same change THEN `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` exits 0 on main with no failing line, and the ledger says in its own words that the re-review happened and what it found.

title: A proposal against the vision has no named shape, so no check ever reads it
description:
Contract: documents.v1 §8 — a proposal is `<contract>.vN-candidate.md` and has three parts in order.

Clause 8 names the shape of a proposal against a *contract*. The vision is not a contract and its filename carries no version, so a proposal against it has no named shape. This lane wrote `docs/VISION.md-candidate.md`, the name the work item asked for. The documents kit's rule 8 matches proposals with the pattern `.*\.v\d+[^/]*-candidate\.md$`, which that name does not satisfy, so the file is invisible to the check.

Measured on this tree after the file was written: rule 8 reports "all 2 proposal(s) carry the three parts in order" and names `contracts/documents.v1-candidate.md` and `docs/PROTOCOL.v3-candidate.md`. `docs/VISION.md-candidate.md` is in neither list. It does in fact carry the three parts, in order — but nothing checked that, and nothing would have caught it if it did not.

Manager session, 2026-09-06 13:40: measured the other half of this. The pre-push guard (.githooks/pre-push) licenses an edit to a FROZEN file only while a <stem>*-candidate.md sits BESIDE it at the tip of the push; archiving the ratified candidate to docs/workflow/ in a later commit made the push of the ratified vision fix refuse. The candidate now stays beside docs/VISION.md (copy in the archive). A ratified proposal's resting place — beside the file it licensed, or archived — needs one rule that the guard, the documents kit and the archive convention all read the same way.
acceptance: GIVEN a proposal written against docs/VISION.md, under whatever name clause 8 settles on, THEN the documents kit's rule 8 lists that file and judges its three parts. GIVEN the current file docs/VISION.md-candidate.md THEN either it is renamed to the settled form or the kit's proposal pattern recognises it. Falsified if rule 8's file list still omits every vision proposal.

title: The app API contract names no Ask write, though two lanes were briefed from it
description:

title: composition.v1 Core 4 and its not-frozen list are behind the engine — the amendment is the steward's call
description:
Contract: composition.v1 Core 4, its "What v1 deliberately does NOT freeze" list, and its conformance-kit asserts.

Discovered while closing converge-4sr, whose acceptance ends: "Done also requires the steward's literal word on the composition.v1 Core 4 amendment." That word is not a lane's to give, and `contracts/` is outside this lane's file ownership, so this is filed as the standing decision rather than half-made.

THE EVIDENCE, measured on this tree 2026-09-04 — a cost actually paid, not a preference.

composition.v1 lists, under what v1 deliberately does NOT freeze:

    - Automated steps that bring their own helpers — when the engine supports it.

The engine supports it. `recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml` carries `schema_version: 2` and a dependency manifest (commit ac8d687), and both its `agent:` references now resolve from the declared closure rather than the calling session's agent map:

    $ recipe-runner validate recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml
    status: ok
    schema_version: 2

    $ recipe-runner plan recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml
    dependencies (1):
      - git+https://github.com/microsoft/amplifier-bundle-converge@main [bundle]
          -> 4507e462d1e801a2b0080c58417ec9647b313880
    agents (12): … anchors:explorer … converge:reconciler …
    steps: load-contracts, derive-rows, run-conformance, file-drift

    Amplifier recipes tool, validate:
      {"execution_mode": "runner-isolated", "schema_version": 2, "status": "valid"}

Worth noting, because older notes say otherwise: the Amplifier recipes tool now reports `runner-isolated`, not the in-session `v2-closed-world-legacy-engine` mode converge-4sr's acceptance predicted. The engine moved further than the item assumed, in the same direction.

The cost paid before that landed: on a host whose active bundle is not on the anchors base, the recipe failed at its first step with "Agent '...' not found in configuration".

WHAT THE AMENDMENT WOULD TOUCH, three places in one contract:

1. **Core 4** — "The host requirement is one sentence in the README. Steps can use only helpers present in the session they run in; Converge needs its own full setup or a host on the same lean base." The second sentence is what schema v2 changes: a step may now declare the closure it resolves from.
2. **The not-frozen list** — remove the "when the engine supports it" item, since the condition on it has been met.
3. **Conformance kit asserts** — Core 4's assert reads README.md for the host-requirement sentence. Whatever Core 4 becomes, `conformance/composition/run.py` rule 4 must read the new claim; it PASSes today on the old wording (kit VERDICT: PASS, 12/0/0), so an unamended contract with a rewritten README is a green rule asserting something the contract does not say.

THE SHAPE THIS TAKES. composition.v1 is `(DRAFT — content owner-ratified 2026-09-02)`, so neither guard blocks the edit. That is not permission. AGENTS.md rule 1 says work is derived from the gap between a contract and what exists, and rule 4 reserves ratifying a contract change to the steward. Writing the proposal is a lane's job; deciding it is not. title: CVG-000 has two `notes:` keys, so the ledger's entire re-review history is silently dropped by the YAML parser
description:

    python3 -c "import yaml; r=[x for x in yaml.safe_load(open('ledger/rows.yaml')) if x['id']=='CVG-000'][0]; print(len(r['notes']))"
    635

Not fixed here, on purpose: merging the two blocks means choosing folded or literal for text written for the other, which re-flows or un-re-flows a record written by earlier lanes. That is a change to their words and belongs to whoever owns it, not to a lane passing through. converge-462l's own re-review was written into the surviving block so it is at least readable.

title: CVG-019 pins a SKIP the reading no longer gives: Core 9 now answers both ways on a fixture
description:

  stuck and is not being relaunched.'; this reads that the stop was written down,
  not whether the cause it gives is the real one.    [step (j) PASS, exit 0]

  declared stuck: lumen-index — named, but no record says the lane stopped; the
  newest one naming lumen-index reads "cycle 1: launched lumen-units and
  lumen-index at width 2, …", which is a mention and not a declaration.
                                                      [step (j) FAIL, exit 1]

A DEFECT THE FIXTURE FOUND, AND THE READING NOW CARRIES A FIX. On its first run BOTH variants passed: the reading asked only whether some record NAMED the stalled lane, and the entry that LAUNCHED it names it — so does every refill line this workspace writes. `run.py`'s new `STALL_DECLARED` requires the record to say the lane STOPPED, in the same sentence as its name. The new readings are quoted in that file in PROSE (Amendment, 2026-09-04 — "Core 9 finally had a stall to judge"), which turnkey_step.py does not read. `ledger/checks/turnkey_clause.py` (live reading) is the other available route, as used for CVG-013/17/18/21.

WHAT A PASS ON THE FIXTURE DOES NOT PROVE, and what the row's `proves` should say: not that the cause a record gives is the real or an adequate one — the reading shows the words and a reader judges them; not that the lane had not already been retried, because clause 9's "across iterations" needs a count of attempts and nothing on disk records one; and not that a manager session ON THIS HOST would declare a stall. The fixture proves the reading answers in both directions when a stall is really there. This host's own habit is a separate observation and lands the first time a real lane here ends with an unchanged branch. Whether that is enough to move the disposition off GAP is the reconciler's call, not this item's.

SEPARATELY, AND NOT THIS ITEM'S DOING: `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` already exits 1 on main — 39 red rows citing resolved work items, and CVG-051's expect not met. Measured byte-identical with converge-wb0's changes stashed and applied.

`app/static/sw.js` names every client module by hand in `PRECACHE`, and that test derives what the app actually loads by walking `main.js`'s import graph -- so a new module is a new PRECACHE entry or it is a module a steward loses the moment they go offline, along with everything that imports it. `cache.addAll` is all-or-nothing and sw.js swallows its rejection, so the symptom would have been an app that silently stops opening offline.

`app/static/sw.js` was outside converge-rj1's file ownership, so the entry could not move with the module in the same change, and shipping the module without it would have traded a working voice note for a broken offline app. Folding it in kept both.

The split is one commit when the two files can move together: create `app/static/js/feedback_voice.js` from the section marked "Feedback as a voice note" in actions.js, import it there, and add `'/static/js/feedback_voice.js'` to PRECACHE in `app/static/sw.js`. `test_the_precache_list_carries_every_module_the_app_loads` and `test_every_precached_url_is_answered_by_the_app` are the two checks that say it was done right.
acceptance: GIVEN the voice half in its own client module WHEN `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests` runs THEN the precache check names `/static/js/feedback_voice.js` as present, and the app still opens with the network off.

title: The ledger cannot yet read the turnkey's clause steps: turnkey_step.py keys on [a-i], and ten rows still probe the mode file
description:
Contract: operation.v1 — Core 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13. Ledger rows CVG-012, CVG-013, CVG-014, CVG-016, CVG-017, CVG-018, CVG-019, CVG-021, CVG-022, CVG-023.

  CVG-014 Core 4  — live PASS. Phrase: "Core 4 (CVG-014) PASS"
  CVG-016 Core 6  — live PASS. Phrase: "Core 6 (CVG-016) PASS"

  CVG-013 Core 3, CVG-019 Core 9, CVG-021 Core 11 — still GAP, but the reason has moved: the harness now names the observation each waits on, in the step's own words, instead of the row naming a finished gate.
  CVG-017 Core 7, CVG-018 Core 8 — still GAP, and less of each is unmeasured: step (f)/(g)/(h) carry the artifact halves and step (k) reads WHO wrote the check record. On this host the newest record came in through a lane merge, so the attribution half reads SKIP with what it awaits.

title: Collaboration's host half is not built: no bridge to pull-request comments, no answer returning to its origin, nothing arriving without asking, and no steward named at registration
description:
`experience-collaboration.v1` fixes the seam between two parties: git is the protocol, the host carries the conversation, and Converge renders it. Half of that seam is kept today and half does not exist. Measured 2026-09-04 against the app at 127.0.0.1:8823 by `conformance/experience-collaboration/run.py` — PASS 7 · FAIL 5 · SKIP 2.

**Kept, and worth saying so:** every write reaches the repository through git and nothing else (Core 1); no route and no line of app code addresses a second manager session (Core 2); one review renderer lays out every proposal with the origin as a value rather than a branch (Core 3); the answer lands in the dated ratification record (Core 5a); no write goes through the manager session (Core 7); a ratification is an ordinary commit with a sibling `*-candidate.md` beside the document (Core 9); no second collaboration surface has grown (Core 10).

**The four that fail, all one missing half — Converge never reaches the host:**

- **Core 4a** — nothing can carry a question to the host as a comment. No route addresses a pull request or its comments; no code path posts one. A steward asking a question has to leave and say it somewhere else, which is the copying between tools the clause exists to stop.
- **Core 5b** — the steward's word is recorded but nothing posts it back where the proposal came from. A teammate who proposed on the host learns the answer only if a person copies it across.
- **Core 6a / 6b** — nothing brings an inbound change in on its own: no webhook route, no live stream, no timer that reloads the project's data. Freshness is the steward's job — they find out by reloading. And nothing on the surface names a mechanism either, so a reader cannot tell whether what they are looking at is current. (6b is derived from 6a: there is no mechanism to name.)
- **Core 8a** — no manager session names a steward, so whose word counts is inferred from whoever is signed in (this target answered as `bkrabach`). The clause asks for it to be settled when the session is registered; everyone else is a teammate, whose proposals get the same reading and none of the authority.

The two halves that genuinely need a second party on a live host — a teammate's reply coming back attributed (4b), and no second person's word reaching the record (8b) — SKIP with that reason stated.

4a, 5b and 6a are one piece of work: a path to the repository host. 8a is separable and much smaller — a field on the manager registration.
acceptance: GIVEN the app is running WHEN `uv run conformance/experience-collaboration/run.py <app>` is run THEN rules 4a, 5b, 6a, 6b and 8a each PASS: a question can reach the host as a comment, the steward's word is posted back to its origin, inbound changes arrive without the steward acting, the app names in plain words how it stays fresh, and each manager session names exactly one steward settled at registration.

title: Run the app: one command, in README and the agent context; managers appear by registration
description: Contract: experience.v1 Core 2 (the home shows every manager session you run) and platform-web.v1 Core 1 (one command runs the web body beside your project); composition.v1 Core 5 (one command, nothing else to know). The steward's step 4, second half: clear instructions on how to RUN the UX, in the agent context AND in README.md, so a steward who has just started a manager session can open the app and see it. Today app/README.md explains the app to a developer; README.md and the manager mode say nothing about starting the app; there is no single command. Deliver: (1) one command that starts the app from a checkout (`uv run --extra app python -m app.serve` wrapped as `scripts/run-app.sh` with sane defaults: bind 127.0.0.1:8788 unless --lan, print the URL and the sign-in method), (2) a 'Run the app' section in README.md under 'Start your first manager session' (the command, what you see, how managers appear — registration — and the systemd/launchd note pointing at app/README.md), (3) the agent context: context/converge-awareness.md gains a short 'The app' paragraph (how to run it, how a manager session shows up in it) and the manager mode's first-wake section tells the manager session to name the app URL in its first brief when the app is reachable, (4) app/README.md's operations section reconciled with (1). Also fold in converge-jcha (app/tests/test_direction_final.py::test_locking_stamps_the_document_and_says_so pins the pre-one-edit freeze behaviour and fails when Playwright is present — make it assert the one-edit truth).
acceptance: GIVEN a fresh checkout with uv installed WHEN the reader runs the one command README names THEN the app answers on the printed URL and the reader can sign in as the README says; GIVEN README.md THEN 'Run the app' sits under the start section and names one command, what appears, and how managers show up; GIVEN context/converge-awareness.md THEN a reader in any Converge session learns in one paragraph how to run the app; GIVEN app/tests with Playwright THEN test_direction_final.py is green; GIVEN the documents kit THEN PASS.

title: Six features the app offers are named by no contract in the family (experience.v1 Core 12)
description:
Contract: experience.v1 Core 12 — "a body may exceed this umbrella in idiom, never in features".

Measured 2026-09-04 by `uv run conformance/experience/run.py http://127.0.0.1:8788` (ledger row CVG-111, converge-yjn):

    [FAIL] 12  6 feature(s) this body offers are named by no contract in the
               family: /api/collab/webhooks/host,
               /api/collab/{mid}/pulls/{number}/answer,
               /api/collab/{mid}/pulls/{number}/comments,
               /api/managers/{mid}/docs/{repo}/{doc}/lock,
               /api/managers/{mid}/presence,
               /api/managers/{mid}/presence/queue
               A feature in one body and nowhere else is either a behavior that
               belongs in this family or it is debt — there is no third thing it
               can be.

Ledger row CVG-111 was green on this rule as recently as the 2026-09-04 export refresh, and it is red now. This is drift toward the red direction, caught by re-running the rule rather than by a row's own account of itself — LEDGER-FORMAT §3 says drift is bidirectional and this is the direction that usually goes unnoticed, because nothing fails loudly when a body grows a feature.

Three of the six are the collaboration bridge, which experience-collaboration.v1 governs but does not name as routes; the lock is experience-direction.v1 Core 11's control with no route named for it; presence is Core 10's courtesy presence, likewise unnamed. So the likely fix is in the CONTRACTS naming what the body already does — not in removing working features.

Related: converge-ism holds the neighbouring failure (rule 4b, ten routes beyond the five writes). The two overlap in the same routes but are different clauses — 4b is about who may WRITE, 12 is about what may EXIST.
acceptance: GIVEN `uv run conformance/experience/run.py <app>` THEN rule 12 passes — every feature the body offers is named by some contract in the family — AND ledger row CVG-111 is re-derived from that run.

title: Ten of fourteen contracts have no worked example, so none of them can reach the lock bar
description:

title: The candidate-file naming pattern is ambiguous: `<contract>.vN-candidate.md` reads both ways
description:
Contract: documents.v1 clause 8 ("A proposal is `<contract>.vN-candidate.md`") and composition.v1 Core 7 (the guard recognizes both proposal names).

The pattern `<contract>.vN-candidate.md` has two honest readings, and this repository currently uses one of them while its own examples and work items use the other.

READING A — vN is the version being amended. `<contract>` is the bare name, so a proposal against composition.v1 is `composition.v1-candidate.md`. Every candidate in `contracts/` today is this shape, six of them:

    contracts/experience.v1-candidate.md
    contracts/experience-collaboration.v1-candidate.md
    contracts/experience-console.v1-candidate.md
    contracts/experience-direction.v1-candidate.md
    contracts/experience-operation.v1-candidate.md
    contracts/composition.v1-candidate.md      (added 2026-09-04 by converge-qwk)

READING B — vN is the version being proposed. PINS.md's naming section gives the example `contracts/documents.v2-candidate.md`, and converge-qwk's acceptance asks for `contracts/composition.v2-candidate.md`.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A QUIBBLE. Both readings satisfy `.githooks/pre-push` (which looks for a sibling `*-candidate.md`), so nothing catches the disagreement. But an acceptance criterion naming a file that a lane then writes under a different name reads as a lane that missed its spec — measured here on 2026-09-04, converge-qwk's acceptance named `composition.v2-candidate.md` and the file written was `composition.v1-candidate.md`, matching the six siblings. A reader cannot tell "convention" from "mistake" without counting the folder.

Note the in-session guard is a third, separate problem already recorded in PINS.md: `hooks-candidate-guard`'s `candidate_glob` is `**/CANDIDATE-*.md` only and recognises NEITHER reading, though composition.v1 Core 7 says it must.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one sentence in documents.v1 clause 8 giving the reading with a worked example, and PINS.md's naming section corrected to match whichever is chosen. If Reading A is chosen, PINS.md's `documents.v2-candidate.md` example is wrong today. If Reading B is chosen, six existing files are misnamed and a rename pass is the fix. Either way it is one decision, made once.
acceptance: GIVEN documents.v1 clause 8 and PINS.md's naming section WHEN a session is about to write a proposal against a contract THEN one reading of `<contract>.vN-candidate.md` is stated with a worked example, PINS.md's example agrees with it, and every candidate file in contracts/ matches — or the ones that do not are listed with the rename that fixes them.

title: The work queue keeps a priority number and no command writes it, so the app's priority write records the call instead of setting the number
description:
Contract: experience.v1 Core 4 — "Exactly five writes. … raise or lower a priority …"

converge-a5g added the fifth write. `POST /api/managers/{mid}/priority` appends one attributed line to the batch's `HIGHWAY.md` weave-in log — the account the manager session reads before it briefs the next lane, the same destination and the same standing a steer has.

What it does NOT do is set the queue's own priority number, and that is a real gap rather than a design choice. The queue keeps one: `amplifier_work_tracker.adapter` orders ready work `ORDER BY priority ASC, created_at DESC`, so the number is exactly what decides which item is claimed next. Measured 2026-09-04 by reading `--help` on every write verb the CLI has — `add`, `edit`, `defer`, `block`, `dep`, `resolve`, `reopen`, `erratum`, `move`, `unclaim` — and `adapter.Beads.edit_item`, which amends title/description/acceptance/design and nothing else: not one of them accepts a priority. `create` takes `-p` and only at creation.

So a steward raising an item here moves the manager session, and the manager session moves the queue. The app says so plainly on the Operation surface and in the write's own answer (`queueNumberUntouched`, `queueNote` in `app/writes.py`) rather than implying a number changed.

Closing this means one of: a `priority` verb on `amplifier-work-tracker` (an upstream ask, since this repository may not speak to `bd` directly), or a decision by the steward that the weave-in log is where a priority belongs and the queue number is the manager session's to set.
acceptance: GIVEN a steward raises an item's priority in the app WHEN the queue is read back THEN that item's own priority number has moved and the queue orders it accordingly — or the steward has settled that the weave-in log is where a priority belongs, and this item is closed as pinned open with that word recorded.

title: A contract at its 100-line ceiling cannot carry the changelog row its own amendment owes
description:
Contract: documents.v1 clause 2 (fifty to a hundred lines) against documents.v1 clause 4 (Changelog only if amended).

Four of the five contracts amended by the six proposals ratified on 2026-09-06 cannot carry a changelog row without breaking the length bound, because none of them had a Changelog section before and the first one costs six lines: a blank line, the heading, a blank line, the table header, the separator, and the row. Measured on this tree by adding exactly that section to experience-console.v1.md, which went from 90 to 96 lines.

The arithmetic for the other four, each at the length the ratified proposal itself predicted:
  contracts/experience.v1.md              100 + 6 = 106
  contracts/experience-direction.v1.md     99 + 6 = 105
  contracts/experience-operation.v1.md     99 + 6 = 105
  contracts/experience-collaboration.v1.md 96 + 6 = 102

The bound is checked (documents kit rule 2, a hard 50 to 100). The changelog is not: the kit lists Changelog under its optional sections, so nothing fails today either way. So the four were left without one and this was filed rather than resolved in passing. experience-console.v1.md did get its row, because it fits and because it is the contract whose 2026-09-05 word never reached it.

Reflow was measured and will not buy the room: re-wrapping every non-clause paragraph at 79 columns frees 0 lines in experience.v1, direction and operation, and 1 line in collaboration. Re-wrapping the Core clauses themselves would free lines, but it would also change how many clauses run past three lines of why, which is the count row CVG-060 is pinned open on, so it would answer a steward's open question by typography.

Three ways out, all of them the steward's call rather than a lane's:
  1. Let the archive in docs/workflow/ be the record of an amendment, and say so in documents.v1 clause 4, so a contract at its ceiling is not in breach for lacking a row.
  2. Raise the bound, or exempt the Changelog section from the count.
  3. Shorten the four contracts by real words, which is a new proposal against each, with its own evidence.
acceptance: GIVEN documents.v1 clause 2 and clause 4 THEN a contract that has been amended and is at its length ceiling has one written answer for where its amendment is recorded, and the documents kit checks that answer rather than being silent on it; GIVEN contracts/experience.v1.md, experience-direction.v1.md, experience-operation.v1.md and experience-collaboration.v1.md THEN each either carries a changelog row inside the bound or is covered by the answer above.

title: documents kit rule 11b's SKIP reason names surface rule 5, which after the renumbering is a different rule
description:
Contract: documents.v1 §5 (a kit's rule numbers follow its contract's clause numbers) — the same anchor the steward ratified on 2026-09-03 (docs/workflow/owner-ratifications-2026-09-03.md, call 2).

conformance/documents/run.py:156, inside rule 11b's SKIP reason:

    "It is asserted where it can be seen, by conformance/surface against
     surface.v1 clause 8 (\"Technical detail waits behind a Details fold\"),
     whose rule 5 scans the app's own words."

Found while re-pointing the ledger (converge-hng) and the app test (converge-uli). Neither lane owns conformance/, so the id was left as-is and annotated in CVG-053's `proves` instead.

title: Console: the pane shows the session but is not it, and it reaches every session on the socket
description:
Contract: experience-console.v1 §3, §4, §10.

Measured 2026-09-03 by `uv run conformance/experience-console/run.py http://127.0.0.1:8788`:

- rule 3 FAIL — `#consoleInput` and its send button are both `disabled`, and the app answers no route that carries a keystroke to the session (`/openapi.json` lists `/api/tmux/{socket}/{session}` GET only). The clause says what you type there is what the manager session receives; today the pane shows the session but is not it. The app says "read-only in this version" in its own footer, which is what keeps clause 9 green — so this is a known limit, not a surprise, but it is still the clause unmet.
- rule 4 FAIL — the console becomes a tray at 980px (`app/static/css/console.css`), and `#consoleClose` dismisses it, but nothing makes the pane resizable on a wide screen: no `resize:` rule on `.manager-console` and no drag handle. The shape may follow the platform; the behaviour does not change.
- rule 10 FAIL — the app answers `/api/tmux/sessions`, which enumerates **every** tmux session on a socket. Against the live socket that returns the watchdog, other lanes, and other manager sessions' work. The console pane itself shows only this manager's own targets, so the defect is the reach, not the display. The client does not currently call it.

Owner: whoever owns `app/` (`app/tmux_view.py` for the route). This lane owns `ledger/` and `conformance/` only.

Ledger rows this closes: CVG-162, CVG-163, CVG-169, CVG-205. Grouped by cause and component on 2026-09-04 by docs/workflow/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-09-04.md, which is where the whole mapping of rows to items is printed. The rows already named this item as their fix; what was missing was the list, written down here.
acceptance: GIVEN the running app WHEN `conformance/experience-console/run.py <app>` runs THEN rules 3, 4 and 10 report PASS: a live console input with a route that carries a keystroke to the manager session, a resizable pane at wide width, and no served route that enumerates sessions beyond the manager's own.

title: test_direction_writes_rendered.py's Ask test still pins the pre-route behaviour and is red on main
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 §9.

`app/tests/test_direction_writes_rendered.py::test_ask_is_offered_at_three_scopes_and_never_pretends_it_recorded_anything` fails on main (48cdc90) with no lane branch merged in:

    the app said: Proposal VISION.v1-candidate is waiting in Review.
    working tree unchanged: False
    HEAD unchanged: True
    1 failed, 10 passed

That is the test working exactly as its own docstring said it would: it pinned the behaviour that shipped before the ask route existed — the ask fails out loud, names converge-ddt, and writes nothing — so that "when the route lands, this test fails and has to be rewritten to assert the proposal. A test that quietly tolerated both would be worth nothing."

converge-ddt has landed. The test now needs rewriting to assert the half §9 actually asks for: the ask returns a named proposal at all three scopes, the proposal exists on disk beside the document, and the document itself is untouched.

(The other red in a full-suite run, `test_console_live_rendered.py::test_a_line_typed_in_the_browser_arrives_in_the_manager_session`, passes in isolation and is the shared-tmux-socket contention already filed as converge-791 / converge-bdc.)
acceptance: GIVEN main with the ask route WHEN `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx --with playwright pytest -q app/tests/test_direction_writes_rendered.py` runs THEN it is green, and its Ask test asserts that a named proposal came back at each of the three scopes and that the document itself did not change.

title: app/README.md documents every other surface but not the host panel
description:
Contract: experience-collaboration.v1 (the host panel this section is missing — Core 1 git is the protocol, Core 5 your answer returns where the proposal came from, Core 6 inbound changes arrive without you asking) — `app/README.md` documents every other surface at that depth and this one not at all.

`app/README.md` has a section for each surface the app carries — What is real, Changes, History, The other writes, Ask, The console — and each says what is read from where and what is deliberately not claimed. Lane w8-collab-bridge added a sixth surface (`app/collab.py` plus the `collab.html` partial) and could not document it: `app/README.md` is outside that lane's file ownership.

What a paragraph there should say, so nobody has to read the code to find it out:

- **From the host** — open pull requests read with `gh pr list` / `gh pr view` in each of the manager session's repositories, laid out in the same proposal shape a `*-candidate.md` file produces, so the review anatomy is identical whatever the origin.
- **The routes** — `GET /api/collab/{mid}/pulls`, `GET /api/collab/{mid}/pulls/{number}`, `POST /api/collab/{mid}/pulls/{number}/comments`, `POST /api/collab/{mid}/pulls/{number}/answer`, `POST /api/collab/webhooks/host`, `GET /api/collab/{mid}/freshness`.
- **Answering writes twice, and reports both** — `app/writes.py` appends the word to `docs/workflow/owner-ratifications-<date>.md`, and the same word is posted to the pull request as a comment. The response carries `recorded` and `returnedToOrigin` separately, so a host that refuses the comment never makes the record look unwritten.
- **Freshness** — a webhook when the host can call one, polling every 60 seconds otherwise, and the panel prints which of the two is carrying it. Today it is polling: the webhook path is behind the sign-in gate (see the item about `PUBLIC_PREFIXES`).
- **Nothing is kept here** — no pull request, comment or answer is stored by the app; the only state is when the host last called, in memory, so a restart goes back to saying polling rather than claiming a webhook it has not heard from.
- **`gh` is required** for this surface and this surface only. Without it the panel says so in plain words rather than showing an empty list.
acceptance: GIVEN a reader opening `app/README.md` WHEN they look for the host panel THEN a section names its routes, both halves of what answering writes, which freshness mechanism is in use and why, that nothing about the conversation is stored, and that `gh` is required — the same depth every other surface's section has.

validator this host does not have. Reading the manifest and finding it
well-formed is the artifact's own claim about itself; the runner accepting it
is the check. Recording CONFORMS on the manifest read alone would be exactly

half I could not run is red rather than quietly folded into the half I could.

HOW THE ROW NOTICES WHEN THIS CHANGES. CVG-291's probe asserts the ABSENCE
(expect VALIDATOR-ABSENT). The day recipe-runner lands on the host, the probe
misses its expect, ledger/checks/verify.py fails NAMING CVG-291, and the row
must be re-read before it may go green. Movement back toward spec is drift too
(LEDGER-FORMAT section 3), and a row keyed on the harm itself could only notice
movement in one direction.

WHAT CLOSES THIS: recipe-runner available on the host (or vendored into the
kit), then `recipe-runner validate recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml` -> ok,
schema_version 2, and `plan` naming each helper against its supplier; CVG-291
re-derived to CONFORMS on that measured output. Alternatively the steward rules
that the offline manifest read at CVG-290 is sufficient to assert the whole
bullet, in which case CVG-291 is retired with that ruling recorded.

RELATED, NOT DUPLICATED: converge-lhkf (open) asks for a KIT RULE for this same
bullet and deliberately left the ledger row unwritten pending a design call
about `recipe-runner plan` needing the network on a cold cache. This reconcile
answers the row half of that item (CVG-290 offline, CVG-291 red and honest) and
leaves the kit-rule half to converge-lhkf. Note for whoever takes either:
converge-lhkf records `recipe-runner validate` running in 0.27s on 2026-09-04,
so the validator half is answerable offline ON A HOST THAT HAS THE BINARY —
which this one does not. That is the whole of this item.

Filed by the scheduled seed-reconcile run (unattended). Nobody was paged.
acceptance: GIVEN a host running this repository's ledger checks WHEN `command -v recipe-runner` resolves AND `recipe-runner validate recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml` is run THEN it reports status ok at schema_version 2, AND `recipe-runner plan recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml` names anchors:explorer against the foundation/anchors bundle dependency and converge:reconciler against the converge@v0.1.0 behavior dependency, AND ledger row CVG-291 is re-derived to kept, citing that measured output, and drops this work ref. Falsified if CVG-291 is called kept while `recipe-runner` is still absent from the host, or on the strength of the manifest read that CVG-290 already covers. Until the validator is on the host this stays can't check, not not yet: the instrument is missing, not the event.

title: app/tests/test_direction_final.py expects the lock write to be missing; the app now performs it
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 Core 11 (the lock control is gated on the four conditions, and nothing locks on its own) — the gate is not in question here; what the control does after it, and whether the app is meant to write a lock at all, is.

Found on 2026-09-04 while running the whole app suite for lane w8-web-polish. Not this lane's file (`app/tests/test_direction_final.py`, and the write itself lives in `app/actions.js` / `app/writes.py`), so it is written down rather than fixed.

WHAT FAILS

    app/tests/test_direction_final.py::test_locking_says_out_loud_that_no_write_answers_yet
    AssertionError: the refusal was swallowed: 'Locked: FROZEN'
    assert 'Nothing was locked' in 'Locked: FROZEN'

The test drives the lock gate at 1280, ticks the three steward checks, clicks "Lock it", and asserts the toast reads "Nothing was locked" -- its premise being that the app answers no route that locks a document yet. That premise is now false: the app locks, and the toast reads "Locked: FROZEN".

IT IS PRE-EXISTING, NOT THIS LANE'S

Reproduced on clean HEAD (4fd7592) with this lane's changes stashed -- byte-identical output, same assertion, same toast. This lane touched only `app/static/sw.js`, `app/static/js/main.js`, `app/static/css/console.css` and a new `app/tests/test_web_polish.py`; none of them is in the lock path.

Whole suite on this branch: 1 failed, 354 passed.

THE FIX IS ONE OF TWO, AND THAT IS THE DECISION

- If locking is now meant to write, the test's name, docstring and assertion all say the opposite and should be rewritten to assert the write it now makes (and what lands on disk).
- If locking is NOT meant to write yet, then the app gained a write nobody asked for and the test is correctly red.

Someone who owns the lock path has to say which. A test that asserts a limit the app no longer has is the same defect class as converge-gf0's toast: a true sentence that stopped being true, kept alive by nobody re-reading it.
acceptance: GIVEN `uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests/test_direction_final.py` WHEN it runs against the current app THEN it is green, because the test asserts what locking actually does now -- either the write it performs, or its absence -- and not the opposite of it.

title: Core 9 has never seen a stall: the reading runs and finds nothing to judge
description:
Contract: operation.v1 — Core 9 ("Stalls are decisions, not loops"). Ledger row CVG-019.

Carried forward from converge-5vz, which closed the other two of its three clauses and could not close this one. Step (j) says it plainly, in its own words:

    Core 9 (CVG-019) SKIP: no lane ended without commits, so no stall exists for
    this reading to judge — the reading ran and found nothing

That is the honest answer and not a pass. The reading works: it looks for a lane whose terminal session is gone and whose branch carries no commit beyond its base, then asks whether any record names that lane and says what stopped it. A lane still running on an unchanged branch is deliberately not counted, because it is working, and counting it would fabricate a red. The self-check proves both directions — a stall nobody named FAILS, a stall named with its cause PASSES.

What is missing is the event: a gate that has only ever seen waves finish cannot say what happens when work stops moving. Every lane on this host so far has produced commits.

Deliberately stalling a fixture wave is the cheapest route — a driven turnkey run whose fixture manager launches a lane that exits without committing, so the reading has something real to judge and the plan record either names it or does not.
acceptance: GIVEN a wave in which at least one lane ends with an unchanged branch WHEN turnkey step (j) reads it THEN Core 9 returns PASS or FAIL rather than SKIP, naming the lane and the record that does or does not say what stopped it; AND CVG-019 quotes that reading and says what it does not prove; AND `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` exits 0.

title: No presence channel: another person editing a section cannot be shown
description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 §10 (IDIOM) — "While a person is editing a section that is shown softly, and the manager session backs off and queues rather than fights."

converge-6cc built the editing surface in the Reading view, the soft `is-editing` presence marking, and all three collision choices (Use combined · Keep mine · Review both), which reconcile against the document as it stands after a clash.

Two halves of §10 remain, and both need files outside converge-6cc's ownership (`app/serve.py`, `app/state_store.py`):

1. **Presence is this browser only.** The app has no channel that says who else is editing which section, so a second steward on a second machine is invisible to the first. What is shown softly today is your own open editor. A real presence signal needs somewhere to put it — the read-point/kept store in `app/state_store.py` is the obvious home — and a route to read and refresh it.
2. **The manager session does not back off.** Nothing tells a running manager session that a section is being edited, so it does not queue; it simply is not looking. That is a contract between the app and the manager session, not something the browser can assert.

Until both land, §10's collision half is real (a clash is detected from the writer's own refusal and the three choices reconcile against the current file) and its presence half is honest but partial — the app says so in a Details fold rather than implying more.
acceptance: GIVEN two stewards signed in on two machines WHEN one opens the section editor THEN the other sees that section shown softly with who is editing it, and WHEN the manager session is told THEN it queues its own write against that section rather than making it.

title: Direction: restore and per-change choices show a message and forget

title: The priority write landed without an offline refusal ending, so refusing it falls back to generic words
description:
Contract: platform-web.v1 §11 — "Offline it refuses the five writes in a plain sentence. A browser cannot promise to send something later … so the app says the write is unavailable and names what to do instead." Ledger row CVG-210.

MEASURED 2026-09-05 (converge-07k3) after the wave-9 merges, against the app at 127.0.0.1:8788.

The fifth write now exists. `curl /openapi.json` lists `/api/managers/{mid}/priority`, and `uv run conformance/experience/run.py http://127.0.0.1:8788` reports rule 4a PASS naming it among all five. converge-a5g landed it.

Its offline refusal ending did not land with it. `app/static/sw.js` lines 150-159:

    const ENDINGS = [
      [/\/decision$/, 'so nothing was recorded — reconnect and answer it again, …'],
      [/\/feedback$/, 'so nothing was filed — reconnect and send it again, …'],
      [/\/steer$/,    'so nothing was sent — reconnect and steer again, …'],
      [/\/ask$/,      'so nothing was asked — reconnect and ask again, …'],
      [/\/read$/, …], [/\/keep$/, …], [/\/edit$/, …], [/\/restore$/, …],
    ];

There is no `/priority$/` entry, so `refusal()` falls to FALLBACK_ENDING — "so nothing was sent — reconnect and try again, or tell the manager session directly". That is a plain sentence, and it is honest about the failure, but it does not name what to do instead of raising a priority, which is the half of clause 11 that says "names what to do".

The row's own probe still reads the same number for a reason that inverted underneath it:

    python3 ledger/checks/offline_refusal.py
    OFFLINE-REFUSAL=PLAIN-SENTENCE-RELAYED WRITES-NAMED=4-OF-5 MISSING=priority

Before the write existed, 4-OF-5 meant "the fifth cannot be refused at all". Now it means "the fifth is refused in generic words". Same count, different fact — and CVG-210's 2026-09-04 note had predicted exactly this ("this row moves the moment the write lands and needs its own ending").

Filed separately rather than folded into converge-rpae: that item covers the refusal half of clause 11 across all five writes and is the row's live cite, but its description is about actions.js relaying a fetch error, which the rewritten probe says is no longer what happens. A precise fact deserves its own item rather than being widened into someone else's prose.

Not fixed here: `app/**` is outside this lane's ownership (ledger/** and docs/work-items.json only).
acceptance: GIVEN the app offline WHEN a raise-or-lower-a-priority write is attempted THEN the refusal names what to do instead of raising a priority, in the same shape the other four writes use — an ending of its own in `app/static/sw.js`, not the generic fallback; AND `python3 ledger/checks/offline_refusal.py` reads WRITES-NAMED=5-OF-5 MISSING=none; AND ledger row CVG-210 is re-derived from that run and reads Kept, or says in plain words which part of the clause is still not yet kept.

title: Corrected record for converge-nht — its stored resolution contains a retracted false claim that cannot be edited
description:
Serves documents.v1. This item exists to carry a TRUE resolution for work that is finished, because the resolution stored on converge-nht is false and the tracker will not let it be corrected.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH converge-nht's STORED RESOLUTION

It states: "This repository has no ledger — there is no ledger/ directory and no rows.yaml at any commit, and AGENTS.md §3 still says the ledger does not exist yet."

WHY IT CANNOT BE FIXED IN PLACE — both paths tried, both refused

  work_claim(converge-nht)  -> "claim failed: issue not claimable: status closed"
  amplifier-work-tracker resolve --id converge-nht --reason <corrected>
                            -> exit 0, and echoed back the ORIGINAL resolution
                               unchanged (a readback-checked no-op, as the CLI's

So the retraction lives on converge-nht's description, in a different field from the claim it retracts, and this item carries the corrected reason in a resolution field where a reader looking at resolutions will actually find it.

title: “Copy the five files” in docs/CONTRACTS-README.md names five of eight templates and omits the hook's rename
description:
Contract: documents.v1 §12

docs/CONTRACTS-README.md:151-156, "Taking this to your own project", says "Copy the five files" and names five: a vision template, a contract template, an AGENTS.md addendum, a pins template, and the pre-push scan. Measured 2026-09-05, docs/workspace-template/ holds eight kit files — plus an index README added by lane w10-adoption-docs on the same day, which is not copied anywhere. The three the sentence does not name are GOAL-FILE.md.template, converge-dir-README.md.template and gitignore-addendum.txt. The onboarding audit found this at six files (finding c-2); two more have landed since, so the count in that sentence is now wrong by three rather than by one.

The same sentence says to enable the hook with "git config core.hooksPath .githooks", but the file ships as docs/workspace-template/pre-push-scan.sh and git only runs a pre-push hook at .githooks/pre-push. Following the sentence alone points core.hooksPath at a directory holding nothing, and the guard silently never runs.

Lane w10-adoption-docs could not edit this file: docs/CONTRACTS-README.md is outside its ownership. It wrote the corrected procedure in the two places it does own — docs/workspace-template/README.md (an index of all eight kit files, with the rename, the chmod and two ways to prove the guard is installed) and docs/ADOPTING.md. The sentence in CONTRACTS-README is what remains.
acceptance: Given a reader who opens docs/CONTRACTS-README.md and follows "Taking this to your own project" with no other document open, when they finish the steps as written, then every file in docs/workspace-template/ is accounted for — copied, or named as not needed — and the pre-push scan ends up at .githooks/pre-push, executable, with core.hooksPath pointing at it. Falsified if the sentence still states a file count that does not match the directory, or still says "enable the hook" without the rename.

title: README.md's host requirement is now false: seed-reconcile no longer resolves helpers from the calling session
description:
Contract: composition.v1 Core 4 ("The host requirement is one sentence in the README. Steps can use only helpers present in the session they run in; Converge needs its own full setup or a host on the same lean base.")

Discovered while closing converge-4sr. `README.md` belongs to the composition lane — PINS.md says so outright — so this is filed rather than fixed.

WHAT CHANGED UNDER THE SENTENCE. `recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml` carries `schema_version: 2` and a dependency manifest (commit ac8d687). Its two `agent:` references now resolve from the declared closure, not from the calling session's agent map. Measured on this tree, 2026-09-04:

    $ recipe-runner validate recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml
    status: ok
    schema_version: 2

    $ recipe-runner plan recipes/seed-reconcile.yaml
    dependencies (1):
      - git+https://github.com/microsoft/amplifier-bundle-converge@main [bundle]
          -> 4507e462d1e801a2b0080c58417ec9647b313880
    agents (12): … anchors:explorer … converge:reconciler …
    steps: load-contracts, derive-rows, run-conformance, file-drift

    Amplifier recipes tool, validate:
      {"execution_mode": "runner-isolated", "schema_version": 2, "status": "valid"}

WHAT NOW READS FALSE, both in README.md:

1. The Host requirement blockquote:

       > **Host requirement.** A recipe resolves its helpers only from the
       > session it runs in, so running Converge's recipe needs either
       > Converge's own full-workspace setup or a host session already on the
       > lean `anchors` base.

   The first clause is the exact property schema v2 removed for this recipe.

2. The "What differs between the two paths (honestly)" table row:

       | `seed-reconcile` recipe runnable | only if the host is on the
       `anchors` base (the recipe's read-only intake step is `anchors:explorer`) | ✅ |

   `plan` resolves `anchors:explorer` from the declared closure, so the `--app`
   column's caveat no longer holds.

NOT A ONE-LINE EDIT, and that is the point. Core 4's own wording carries the same claim, and composition.v1 lists "Automated steps that bring their own helpers — when the engine supports it" as deliberately NOT frozen. The engine now supports it. Promoting that item into Core is the steward's call, not a lane's — see the sibling item for the amendment. Whoever owns README.md should either:

- wait for the Core 4 amendment and restate the sentence to match, or
- state the truth now with the contract's status named ("the recipe declares its own helpers; the contract clause has not yet been amended").

Do NOT quietly rewrite the sentence to something Core 4 does not say — `conformance/composition/run.py` rule 4 reads README.md for it and currently PASSes on the existing wording, so a rewrite that drifts from the clause turns a green rule into a lie rather than a failure.

The measured facts are already recorded in PINS.md under "The recipe declares its own helpers", including why one dependency and not two, and why `@main` and not a SHA — both reproduced rather than assumed.
acceptance: GIVEN README.md WHEN a reader looks for what the seed-reconcile recipe needs of its host THEN the sentence matches what the recipe actually does — it declares its own helpers and resolves them from that closure — or names plainly that the contract clause has not yet been amended; AND the "recipe runnable" table row no longer says it works only on a host already on the anchors base; AND `uv run conformance/composition/run.py .` still reports rule 4 PASS.

title: The voice write answers nothing until app/serve.py mounts its router: one include_router line
description:
Contract: experience-operation.v1 §10.

converge-rj1 wrote `app/feedback_voice.py`, an APIRouter carrying `POST /api/managers/{mid}/feedback/{form}` -- the *drop feedback* write told which form arrived. `app/serve.py` is another lane's file, so the two lines that mount it were not added:

    from . import feedback_voice
    app.include_router(feedback_voice.router)

Until they are, the module is inert: no route, and the rest of the app runs unchanged. The browser half is already live and will report the refusal in plain words if a steward sends a voice note before this lands -- "Feedback filed at <...>.md. The voice note was not filed: <what refused>" -- so the text still lands and nothing is silently lost. But voice does not work in the running app until this line exists.

Two facts for whoever adds it, both measured 2026-09-04:

* The sign-in gate in `app/serve.py` is middleware, not a per-route dependency, so the route is behind it the moment it is mounted -- nothing else is needed. `test_the_sign_in_gate_covers_the_voice_route` proves it answers 401 without a cookie.
* It adds no sixth write. `conformance/experience/run.py`'s `write_tail` drops a path parameter, so this route reads as the `feedback` write and rules 4a/4b/12 go on counting five. `test_the_route_table_still_reads_five_writes` asserts that by importing the kit's own reader.

`app/tests/test_feedback_voice.py` mounts the router itself in every test and reports -- never asserts -- whether `app/serve.py` carries the line, so it neither fails before this lands nor goes quiet after it:

    app/serve.py mounts feedback_voice.router: False
      the line it still needs, exactly as every test here writes it:
          from . import feedback_voice
          app.include_router(feedback_voice.router)

Verified end to end with that line added by hand, in a real browser at 1280x800 and 390x844: one press of Send feedback wrote both `2026-09-04T06-39-10.md` and `2026-09-04T06-39-10.wav`, the recording byte-identical to what was attached, the note's front matter carrying `voice: 2026-09-04T06-39-10.wav`.
acceptance: GIVEN the app started by `python -m app.serve` WHEN a steward drops feedback with a voice note THEN the recording lands in the project's `.converge/feedback/` folder, and `app/tests/test_feedback_voice.py` reports that app/serve.py mounts the router.

description:
Contract: experience-direction.v1 §6.

converge-4pq landed: restore now reaches any snapshot in a document's own history, and the History panel no longer says an older snapshot is out of reach. Two tests were written to pin that honest sentence while the gap was open, and both said in their own docstrings that they are the ones to rewrite when the route lands. Its docstring: "This test fails the day someone adds such a control without the route behind it — which is the failure it exists to catch." The route is behind it now (`app/serve.py`, `snapshot_or_refusal`), so the sentence it pins is false.

2. `app/tests/test_direction_persist.py::test_the_panel_says_what_it_cannot_reach` — rendered; asserts `"converge-4pq" in said` and that the panel says plainly an older snapshot is out of reach.   uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx pytest -q app/tests
    1 failed, 226 passed, 123 skipped        (the polish one; the persist one skips without a browser)

  uv run --extra app --with pytest --with httpx --with playwright pytest -q app/tests
    3 failed, 347 passed                     (both of the above, plus a third filed separately)

Filed rather than fixed: neither file is in lane w8-direction-restore's ownership (it may edit app/writes.py, app/serve.py, app/static/js/render/direction.js, app/static/js/actions.js, app/static/js/api.js, app/templates/direction.html, and app/tests/test_direction_restore.py as a new file only). AGENTS.md §5: stay in your lane, write the fact down for its owner.

The replacement already exists and passes: `app/tests/test_direction_restore.py::test_the_history_panel_no_longer_says_an_older_snapshot_is_out_of_reach` asserts the opposite — that the panel no longer says it, no longer names converge-4pq, and is actually built from the snapshot's own reading (`restoreReading()` / `openSnapshot()`). (2) is rendered and worth rewriting rather than deleting — the same walk, asserting that picking an older row redraws the panel against that commit.

title: Two lanes were briefed to carve one file by row, and Core 6 promises different files — the reader counts it as an overlap (CVG-016)
description:
Contract: operation.v1 Core 6 — width is a collision decision; lanes fill to the steward's count only with items that provably touch different files.

Discovered from converge-1nb4 while re-deriving CVG-016, and it is the question converge-usns said must be decided rather than guessed.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Two briefs in this wave split one file by row: w14-adopt-rerun owns ledger row CVG-302, and the reconcile lanes own ledger everything except that row. Both write ledger/rows.yaml. Run against the harness's own reader functions on 2026-09-06:

  w14-adopt-rerun   ['evaluations/adopter', 'ledger']
  w14-reconcile-8   ['ledger']
  adopt-rerun x reconcile-8 declared collisions: [('ledger', 'ledger')]

The row-level qualifier is invisible to the reader by construction. Its brief_ownership takes only backticked path tokens up to the first sentence break, so "EXCEPT row CVG-302" and "(row CVG-302 only)" are dropped as prose, both briefs normalise to ledger, and paths_collide reports an overlap.

SO THE ANSWER IS: IT MUST COUNT IT AS AN OVERLAP, AND BY THE CLAUSE'S OWN WORDS IT SHOULD. Core 6 promises items that provably touch DIFFERENT FILES. Two lanes carving one file are not touching different files, whatever the briefs say about rows. Teaching the reader to honour a row-level split would make it agree with the briefs and disagree with the contract, which is the wrong direction to move a check.

WHY IT IS FILED ANYWAY. The verdict flips with which lanes happen to be live at the moment of the read, not with the practice. Taken earlier on 2026-09-06 the same reader said FAIL, naming w14-adopt-rerun and w14-reconcile-7 both owning ledger. Taken later it said PASS, because the pair it saw was w14-run-the-app and w14-reconcile-8, which share nothing. Same practice, opposite verdicts, hours apart. Ledger row CVG-016 is CONFORMS today on that second reading and its note records both.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS. Either the briefing practice stops carving one file two ways between concurrent lanes — which the clause plainly asks for, and which also removes the merge hazard of two branches editing one file — or Core 6 is amended to say what a row-level split is, through a candidate file, with the evidence that the split was paid for and worked. Guessing is what converge-usns asked no one to do.

NOT A REF FOR CVG-016. That row is green on today's reading, and a green row may not carry a work ref.
acceptance: GIVEN the manager session's briefs for any two concurrent lanes THEN no two of them declare the same file, or Core 6 carries a ratified sentence saying what a row-level split is; AND GIVEN the live step (j) reading THEN Core 6 no longer swings between PASS and FAIL on which lanes happen to be live rather than on the practice.
